I bought this along with another brand of shortbread for my Dad's 90th Birthday Celebration. He enjoys his shortbread so much he would not let any other family member share it with him. He proclaimed how delicious this shortbread was.  It must have been for the sheer joy of teasing the family. This is wonderful shortbread that should be shared and enjoyed by everyone.

Wonderful taste - a bit different from the usual icings.  I'd have given it 5 stars, but for the difficulty in getting out of the tube pouch.  Finally, I cut the top off of the pouch, squeezed into a dish, and microwaved on high for 20 seconds.  Then it was spreadable.Edit:  The flavor I tried was Traditional Chocolate.

Breads you make yourself are often, compact, heavy.  This bread is good-tasting, light and moist.  And it is not overly-sweet (even though it has the raisins) which I find important as I don't like items that are too sweet.  An excellent product, I would recommend it highly.  The packaging is also superb and focussed on freshness.
AWESOME BREAD.  MY HUSBAND AND I BOTH ARE VERY HAPPY WITH THIS PRODUCT, WILL BE COMING BACK FOR MORE.THANK YOU!

My husband and I, through the past 25+ years, have searched for the coffee we enjoy the most, and found it in Antigua  Guatemala coffee. We first started drinking this coffee through our local coffee roaster, but then they suddenly were unable to supply the coffee. We tried several other brands of this specific region, but most were not as flavorful as the fresh-roasted. We tried fresh-roasted from other Central American countries, but they did not have the flavor we so enjoyed.We were thrilled to find this brand of Antigua, Guate coffee and at such a great price! The coffee tastes yummy first thing in the morning and the price is perfect. The coffee arrived quickly [I usually order this kind of stuff on a Monday] and it came in a vacuum packed bag. We buy only whole bean coffee.Everyone has their own tastes in coffee, hence the plethora of varieties. But I do have this story to tell. After spending five days with a very picky relative who drank Choc'ful of Nuts [sic and yuck] coffee, I had to throw away what extra was made for me and bring out my little baggie of whole beans I brought with me. Because this relative left early in the morning, the way to solve the waste was for me to grind the beans at night and prepare the coffee maker with my Antigua coffee for both of us. The relative did not seem so pleased.The first morning we tried this one-coffee-for-two approach, I was awoken with my relative beaming a huge smile down upon me. "This is the BEST coffee ever!" my relative said, before marching out and leaving for work.I have promised to buy the relative and spouse a big ole supply of this coffee and don't mind one bit! It's share the love and help the coffee farmers in a country I love and admire. A win/win situation.I don't know all the various terms for coffee, except that this coffee tastes better to me than any other coffee I've ever had and I have had soooo many different kinds of coffee, even chicory roots :>)Try it ... you'll love it! But buy whole bean and grind it for yourself; we grind the night before and have it ready for us in the a.m., not purists, but a practical approach.
misleading info on the product, price quoted for 5 lbs, however when follow the link it is for 1lb bag

We had ordered the sugar free logs from another company and they were delicious.  As we love Amazon,we thought we would try buying through them.  However the logs were sticky and hard.  They stuck to our teeth.  Ugh!  Very disappointed!
Great seller and very fast service.  This is a product I have had to use for several years because of some health problems and it works wonderfully.

column9: A little too spicy and needs a little more help.
column10: I purchased one bag of this at a specialty store.  I made it but added a can of tomato sauce with the hamburger, seasoning and macaroni.  This last time I decided to make it as the bag stated and my family wouldn't eat it.  The tomato sauce helped to mellow it out a bit.  Since I have 5 more bags I will be doctoring it to find the best method of cooking it.  I love Namaste baked goods but this item isn't that great.

I was very happy to find a gluten free dish that my whole family can enjoy.  I add a can of black beans and a can of Muir Glen Fire roasted diced tomatoes w/chilies.  I also have added ground beef.  I like it with a little sharp cheddar grated on top.  My son (age 9) who is allergic to dairy still loves it without the cheese on it.

column9: Great go-to dish for gf and gluten eating kids
column10: Buying bulk means I always have this on hand. Sautee onions and add ground beef and seasoning, cook noodles, mix. Have fed to at least 15 kids and everyone loves it! You cd add veggie or other ingredients, noodles and sauce alone too spicy for mine. Oh, only CON is the noodle packages aren't sealed and open on the bitten, take extreme care or noodles will end up all over floor in 2 seconds.

column9: The best coffee I've ever had
column10: I discovered K Cups in Dec, 2007 and discovered Tully's Italian Roast about a month later.  It is the best coffee I've ever had, rich, full-bodied, smooth and satisfying.  I drink it every day.

column9: Very Good Tasting But Could Be "Bolder" - Recommended
column10: Tully's Coffee "Italian Roast (Bold)" K-Cups makes a very good cup of coffee in my Keurig B-40 B40 Elite Gourmet Single-Cup Home-Brewing System. This is a fairly strong tasting brew that has much more flavor than the Coffee People, Donut Shop K-Cups for Keurig Brewers (Pack of 50) [Amazon Frustration-Free Packaging] I generally drink in the morning.I really enjoy the rich flavor of this coffee but my wife thinks it is "slightly burnt" tasting. It is not as "bold" as Emeril's Big Easy Bold Coffee for Keurig Brewers, 24-Count K-Cups (Pack of 2) when made on the machine's "large" cup setting.Recommended!CFH
better than average coffee but not bold enough for my taste! I definitely prefer Emeril's Big easy Bold!

I am a big fan of dark roast and full bodied coffees.  I like something strong for my K-cup brewer because if it isn't strong then a larger cup is just too weak.This cup is nice and full bodied.  A good blend of flavors.  Not too bitter but it does have a slightly burnt taste in the finish.  I'm no connoisseur, but I know what I like.I also know that this isn't for everyone.  If you don't like bitter or burnt, stay away from this k-cup.  However, I enjoy it and would buy it again.I also like Green Mountain Dark Magic, and Timothy's Rainforest Espresso.

We've had a K cups coffee brewer for two years and this is the best coffee we've come across so far.  In general the brewer produces weak coffee, even if one selects the 'small cup' size.  Tully's Italian and French Roasts partially overcome this with a bold roast or perhaps just more coffee per cup.  On a scale of 1 - 10 where 1 is a cup of Folger's crystals and 10 is cup of Starbucks coffee brewed on a Clover, this comes in around a 6 or 7.  Not fantastic but very drinkable.
Rich, aromatic and tasty. I love this product and will purchase more in the future. Everyone in this office loved it!
A fabulously bold blend!  I love it!  If you like a bold blend and high quality, this is it!

column9: I was told this was the best K-cup
column10: The guy who services our company K-cup coffee brewer recommended this exact brand and flavor of coffee. I wouldn't say it was any better than the Diedrich K-cups that I already have (the Paradiso is good). Tullys is great, however it just doesn't live up to the expectation I had after receiving the glowing recommendation. Saying that, I would re-order this product unless I can find Pete's k-cups somewhere.

column9: Makes a great cup of coffee at a great price
column10: I couldn't believe the low price here on Amazon (less than 16 bucks!) so despite there being no other reviews to go by, I took the plunge, and I'm happy with the decision.While the Cafe Honduras isn't as strong as say, Coffee People's Black Tiger Extra bold, or Timothy's Parisian Nights (so strong I think I could stick a fork in it) it's not weak either. It makes a good cup of coffee at the larger cup setting, and on my machine (Keurig B60 Special Edition) that is 10 ounces. I have also found it works very well for iced coffee using the small setting as instructed over a full glass of ice- and since it's not super strong- it balances well with other flavors you might wish to add. For me, variety is the name of the game with the Keurig, and this is a nice addition to what I already have on hand to offer guests.
It has been many years since I have tasted a good cup of Honduran coffee.  Coffee is bold, without any hint of being over-roasted.

column9: Change of Pace for the Dark Brew Lover
column10: Generally I love a really dark, bold brew (think Coffee People Black Tiger K-Cups for Keurig Brewers (Pack of 50) [Amazon Frustration-Free Packaging], Emeril's Big Easy Bold Coffee for Keurig Brewers, 24-Count K-Cups (Pack of 2), Gloria Jean's Coffees, Black Gold Extra Bold for Keurig Brewers, 24-Count K-Cups (Pack of 2)) However, change is good, and I appreciate an excellent medium roast once in a while and this Honduras was an unexpected find.It is a Bold variety ("bold" refers to the amount of coffee put into a k-cup, not whether it is a light, medium, or dark roast), and I like a somewhat stronger cup of coffee.  It has a very distinct aroma and flavor which I find rare in the k-cups and also tastes really fresh and somewhat sweet.  The lighter brews generally taste too "sour" for me, but I really enjoy drinking this coffee.  If you generally tend towards dark roasts but want to try something different, I can recommend this coffee highly.  Out of approximately twenty different light and medium roasts that I have tried, this is the only one I truly enjoy.
This is very good coffee.  I will definitely order this again and the price is right too!

Having tried just about every brand and flavor of k-kup coffee available, this one stands above all others for overall flavor and enjoyment. The only negative; it can be difficult to obtain at times. If you have not yet tried it, please do so.

*****The 2 star review is not necessarily for the coffee inside the k-cup - but for the way the Van Houtte k-cups I ordered malfunctioned.*****I received 2 boxes of Van Houtte Honduras k-cups from Amazon in mid October.  The first few were fine - the coffee was good - nothing spectacular, but not bad either.  Then I noticed my machine was dripping very slowly, then hardly at all. I also saw that coffee grounds were dripping through along with the coffee.  When I opened the top of my Keurig machine, I saw that the k-cup was overflowing with water and coffee grounds. My Keurig machine was only a few weeks old and had been working wonderfully until that time.  I cleaned it out and tried another Van Houtte k-cup hoping that would take care of it.  The same thing happened.  I cleaned the machine again and ran hot water through it a few times to make sure the grounds were all out of it and tried a different brand of k-cup.  It was fine. I used the other brands for a few days and didn't have any problems.Then I tried the Van Houtte again and the same thing happened.  I repeated the cleaning - ran hot water through it and tried another one. Ditto.I think I may have gotten a defective box or two.  The foil on top isn't flat - but is puffed up as if there's too much air inside. The coffee doesn't seem to be very loose when it's shaken like the other brands of k-cups I have. Perhaps they were filled too much.Since I had used so many of the Van Houtte trying to fix my machine,  I figured I was stuck with the remainder.  I still called Amazon to let them know there might be a problem with the product. Not only did they refund my purchase  - they did not ask me to return the remainder of my order. I doubt I will use them - I'm afraid they'll clog up my Keurig machine.Thanks again Amazon - your customer service is terrific, as always.

This is the coffee I have on hand at home all the time.  Everyone who tries it loves it.  It's is hard to keep a decent supply on hand.  When I run out, I always get asked, when are you getting more.  It's not as strong/bitter as starbucks and not as weak as D&D.  I would and do recommend this coffee to anyone that wants a good cup of unflavored coffee.
I love the super bold flavor of this coffee, definitely not for the cream and sugar people. But if you enjoy a good strong cup of coffee I think you'll like these k-cups!!!

column9: My mom's favorite out of the 20 or so k-cup varieties she's tried
column10: We got my mom a Keurig machine for her birthday a couple of years ago, and since then, she's tried over 20 different k-cup varieties (from assorted collections to single boxes with 20 or 50 cups in them) and she claims this one is her favorite.It's flavorful, tastes like "real coffee" as she put it, and no matter which setting she used (small, medium or large cup), the taste was great.I'm knocking down a star because unless this particular product is on sale, it is REALLY overpriced.

This is an even-bodied, medium roasted coffee, that works best for multi-cup breakfast and lunch duty, as well as a general purpose all-arounder for guests wanting a good but not aggressively flavorful cup of coffee.  The packaging states, 'extra-bold', but I do not feel it is bold enough for travel-mug size.I'd definitely keep on hand for those wanting a mildly flavorful brew.

That is my new favourite k-cup. I've tried about 20 flavours of k-cups thus far and this one is TOPS for me.  It's what I'm looking for in a coffee:  complete and full body, ABSOLUTE flavour (your taste buds don't have to dig in to find it, it's there). I think it's perfect for any time of the day - morning, after lunch, after dinner. This is the one. My financial advisor came over recently and I asked him if he'd like a cup of the Van Houtte Honduras. He liked it a lot. Next time he came over, I asked him if he'd like something to drink and he asked for "that coffee you gave me last time". Yeah, it's that good.

I just got this yesterday and my husband and I both tried it this morning.  We both felt that it makes a very full cup of coffee, not terribly complex in structure, but still very good.  I was surprised with the fullness because of it being a medium roast.  Don't let that fool you though because it behaves like a dark roast.  I do think I like the black tiger better though because I can get the fullness and a little more complexity in the same cup.  I would get this again though because of the richness it offers without the slightest bitterness.

column9: Best K-Cup I've found, brews a strong flavorful cup of coffee
column10: We recently made the switch from Senseo pods to K-Cups after our Senseo machine died after many good years. The main reason for the switch was for the greater variety (and availability) of coffee. However I've struggled to find a K-Cup that I would drink on a regular basis. I prefer a stronger brew of coffee (I always buy the Starbucks Bold selection for example) and the Keurig has plenty of strong cups, but I've found these to be strong (like espresso) with very little flavor.Then I ordered the Honduras, and finally found a cup of coffee that I will drink on a regular basis. It brews a nice strong cup of coffee that can take a small amount of cream & sugar without becoming too milky. And it's not overpoweringly strong & bitter like some of the espresso and Italian roast K-Cups that I've tried.

column9: This is the most delicious taffy ever.
column10: It tastes the exact same as the kind at carnivals!  It is truly delicious.  (:  We received ours on the ninth, it's gone.
Better than the ones I grew up with long ago!But beware...most packages contain broken cookies when shipped from the manufacturer; however, they are still worth it.Enjoy!

This new pop up popcorn bag is EXTREMELY dangerous!!!  I did not use the popcorn button, rather I set the microwave to the indicated time (2.5 min) and the bag spewed hot oil all over the microwave, staining it.  This was the least of my problems because the microwave was SMOKING horribly from all sides when I came into the kitchen.  The smell lasted all day long and the microwave itself still smells very strong a day later, even after being cleaned.  This bag needs to be taken off of the market before it burns someone's house down.Again, I just cooked the popcorn for the specified time.  I cook regular popcorn at the specified package time and step away to go to the restroom and wash my hands all the time and never have a problem.  This product is scary!If you have this product, please return it rather than putting yourself, your home, and your family at risk.  I cannot believe that such a dangerous product made it to the shelves.  What a very sad shame.

The bowl bag does not pop in the same amount of time as a normal bag so it makes your microwave's popcorn button useless. Additionally, about half of the bags are faulty and open when popping resulting in very little popped popcorn. Last, I have found it almost impossible to get the bag to pop completely even when watching it pop (since I can't use the popcorn button!). Overall, this new bowl design is terrible and I would recommend switching to another brand until they go bag to the old bags that work.

I was disappointed to find that this is the only option in orville redenbacher popcorn.  This "bowl" is impossible to open without making a big mess.  I must dump out the top inch or so in order to use it as a bowl.  HATE IT!  Bring back the bag.

What a wonderful idea. It creates its own bowl! It's very easy to use if you follow the directions. Do not try to tear the plastic top open like I did the first time. It was my fault that I did not read the directions. The entire plastic top is removed. If you do it right, you will not burn yourself and it's very simple to open.

The first 3 bags out of the box ripped while popping and not only lost unpopped kernels but most of the butter emptied and did not cover the pop corn remaining in the bowl. Until they have had time to fix it, I will not buy again.

Just recently bought this because I finished building my home theater and wanted the "authentic" look as much as possible instead of going for an actual popcorn machine. Was surprised at how well this idea worked.  THe popcorn is also pretty darn good! My friend who doesnt really like popcorn loved it! Definitely buying more in the feature for my concession stand!

column9: Sprayed orange grease all over the inside of the microwave
column10: The pop-up bowl sounds like a great idea, but evidently they rushed it to market before all the bugs were out.The first bag I cooked was fine, except the instructions for opening the bag are far from clear, and even after you figure out how to do it it's a lot of trouble and makes a big mess.But the second bag evidently sprang a leak - it sprayed bright orange grease all over the inside of my microwave, even into the tiny vent holes inside the top and side. I always watch popcorn carefully while it pops, but I could not see the grease spray until after it was done and I opened the door. Cleaning it all out was a horrible ordeal, and I'm sure everything I cook in the microwave will come out smelling like popcorn grease for weeks.They released this product too soon. It needs serious redesign. I will not buy it again.

column9: Love the new Pop Up Bowls!
column10: I was skeptical when I saw these at first, thinking the design would surely be flawed. The package design is great. Stands up by itself and doesn't collapse or leak if I add butter. The first two bags I made did burn because I was following the directions on the back of the box. The cook time listed is entirely too long. I started experimenting with shorter times with the second bag and got lucky with the third: 1 minute, 45 seconds seems to be the best cook time, at least for my microwave. I now get a full bag without any burned popcorn. In fact, usually the bag is overflowing when I get the plastic off. Taste is great and the entire bag is only 4 Weight Watcher points.

I popped this for 2 minutes 7 seconds and while the corn was still popping the plastic began to melt and SMOKE.  The popcorn was not burnt but the plastic was and my office quickly filled with smoke.  It was disgusting and unedible.  For years I have used a pair of scissors to cut out a large square from my regular OR Popcorn bags instead of opening the end, thus creating  a "bowl"  for myself.  So far, this plastic top and bottom seems like a TERRIBLE idea.

I loved the idea of having an actual bowl, but when I put it in the microwave, the popcorn just didn't pop. I first microwaved for the instructed 2 min 30s... less than half popped...i microwaved again in intervals, adding up to nearly 5 minutes....i finally got half of the bowl to pop... Due to this, the excess oil and flavoring intensified the popped popcorn, making it very oily and salty.. The flavor is great (besides its overly intensified nature), but I wish it was easier to pop it.
I love to exercise and this bar was recommended by my sister.  I tried the bar and got hooked immediately.  Worth every penny spent!!

These Bars are awesome there are so tasty and healthy the calories count is great for a snack only  130 or 160 and you get don't hungry right away.There have a fresh task and for me there are a must to have.

Jumpstarter Bodyfuel energy bars are truly what they claim to be; outrageously delicious! Not only do these bars satisfy my sweet tooth, they provide me with more of a leap start rather than a jump start. These bars come in 6 different flavors; with Chocolate Raisin, AppleBerries, Cranberry, and Raisin being my favorites. The taste of these bars isn't the usual dry, crumbly, bark like flavor so often found in energy bars. Rather these bars have a fresh homemade taste where the cranberry bar has real cranberries and the chocolate raisin bar has real raisins, etc; which results in a truly fresh dense scone like flavor rather than that of hard wet sand. These bars definitely provide the needed energy needed to carry one through those hectic and/or strenuous days when missing meals just seems to happen. These also happen to be great for hikes, bike rides, road trips, etc. Downside; difficult to find in retail stores (hopefully this will change soon) and at $2.00 a pop, it can get pricy. However, when considering the bar can easily keep one satisfied until their next meal, it's definitely worth the price. Major pluses: no trans fats, no eggs, dairy free, and absolutely no preservatives. Makes me wonder what energy bar fairies they've got working for them that make these bars so delicious. Recommend: An AppleBerries bar with a morning cup of Joe or Chocolate bar with an evening cup of Joe equals yummy for my tummy. Thank you energy bar fairies.
These are by far the BEST bar you can buy.  They are the closest to real food-taste wise and the best you can get nutrition wise.  Plus every flavor is delicious.  you cannot beat this bar!

column9: Good but very expensive. Sells in Indian store for $1.47
column10: This is an outstanding spice and I use it a lot. You can buy this from an Indian grocery store for $1.47 for 100 gm and $5.99 for 500 grams. All these MDH spices are too expensive at Amazon.

column9: The best masala for chaat (Indian snack), fried potatos and vegetable & fruit SALADS
column10: This is the THE BEST CHAAT MASALA.  I mean chaat not chat(chatting with someone).  Read about Chaat here  [...]I have been using it since 1990 in Delhi.  THIS IS A MUST TRY - all the ingredients are very nutritious.  Some of them anti-cancer and anti-oxidant properties.You can a packet for three dollars or less at an Indian Store though...

column9: put 'em on your 'do not buy' list
column10: The text box for this review stated 'Reviews must be at least 20 words long.'  I can get 'r done in six: "bland.  insipid.  Edible, but just barely."  I have been eating canned sardines for better than 40 years, and this brand was one of the few that, while eating the contents of the can, the only thing that kept me from dumping the entire works in the garbage after the first bite was not wanting to deal with the funky smell in the kitchen after doing so (there was a fresh liner in the garbage can).  Admittedly, sardines are an acquired taste but, trust me, you don't want to acquire a taste for them by eating these.
This is Jasmine Tea pictured NOT Green Tea, however it is very tasty and of superior quality!
I love this decaf coffee. It is smooth yet full bodied rich tasting coffee. Not quite as dark as expresso, but nice.

column9: Good seller and fast delivery but
column10: I liked some spices more than other and would buy in one container at a time for now onDid not like to have all that space taken up on something half empty/

I love the soda, great product, but was very unhappy with Nutricity vendor.I asked to cancel the order 2 different times with no response from the company because I was charged such an enormous shipping fee. More then the price of the product.  The first time I bought this product I received free shipping , this time I was charged over 30.00.  I would never buy from this  company again.Alice Delaney

column9: Bye-Bye Zeros, Hello My New Hero--Zevia
column10: I grew up drinking Diet sodas.  No joke.  I'd never tasted a regular Coke until I was 13.  I thought I'd gag.In recent years I've scooted from one Diet brand to the next, avoiding all those empty calories and eventually avoiding caffeine.All these new 'Zero' products may not have sugar or caffeine but they are loaded with artificial sweeteners that I've generally heard nothing but bad things about.So, get fat with sugar or get cancer with artificial sweeteners.  Doesn't seem like much of a choice.  And, of course, I am prone to exaggeration on this matter.Having used Stevia before (an all natural herbal sweetener from South America) I was thrilled to find Zevia...sweetened by aforementioned sweetener.If you're used to the taste of Diet or Zero anything, then this won't be a far leap for your taste buds.  I love this stuff!The only down side for now is the price.  AT nearly $6 a 6-pack (or more) it's a pricey artificial sweetener alternative.But if you aren't a soda-holic (less than a can a day on average) then this really isn't so bad.

I have tried most of the Zevia soda flavors. I love the taste now, it took a few days to get use to the different taste from the other calorie free sodas. I love that they don't have the Aspartame and Surcalose as other soft drinks. I don't have the horrible side effects from the major brands give me.ZEVIA Natural Black Cherry - With Stevia (Case of 24) Zero Calories

This isn't sprite but I really like it. I picked up a 6 pack from my local grocery to try it I'm really pleased. I just got a subscription to get the full case from Amazon. Great straight from the fridge, guilt free soda with no horrible aspartame after-taste.

I really would rather give this stuff three and a half stars, but I rounded up because my third grade math teacher said to round up for half or more. And I don't want her to think I didn't learn anything. She'll find me, just like she did all the others. The horror...Anyway, this stuff is pretty alright. What it lacks in the crispness of a 7-Up, it makes up for in flavor and not giving you diabetes if you chug the whole 24 pack in a week. Which, given the taste, is not impossible. The diet-y bluntness is still there from other flavors, and if you're used to 7-Up like I was, its pretty noticeable. But once you get used to it, its pretty good for lemon-lime, which I've never been a huge fan of in general. Drink it on the verge of freezing and finish before it gets warm, because when it does, it feels kind of like thin syrup.Should you buy some? If you want stevia-sweetened pop, sure. I do wish Amazon offered six or twelve packs instead of only twenty-four. I'd love to try out black cherry, but frankly, $25 is steep for me right now.

column9: Ok - Black Cherry the best flavor
column10: I like Zevia for their "natural" claims. I say this because just as aspartame was produced and marketed to the masses, and people were not aware of the dangers of chemicals, I wonder about the synthesized version of stevia.But, for now I'm trying to do the best with the information we do have - drink water most of the time, but when I just have to have a soda like with a pizza or something spicy, I reach for my Zevia.I've tried all the flavors but my favorite is Black Cherry. The lemon is weird tasting and not very refreshing.Black Cherry hits the spot.

I was a huge soda drinker, but I gave it up, due to the huge amount of calories in regular versions and the huge ugly headaches I get from artificial sweeteners used in the diet versions.  This stuff is delicious and happily free of both complaints above!  Zevia has given me back the ability to enjoy soda again!  Hooray Zevia!
I love Zevia soda, it has a weird aftertaste for some but I am in love with this soda that is good for you!  It does have a very citrusy taste!

this is so good! i was on a no sugar diet for three months before i found this product. and i'm so happy i can now drink soda again. my kids can't tell the difference between these and regular. my favorite flavors are natural twist and cola.

column9: Zero Carbs+Zero Cals+Zero Artifical Sweenters= Zevia
column10: If you are looking for something to quench your thirst without sugar, without artificial sweetener (Splenda, Aspartame) then you need Zevia Twist.  This is the most refreshing beverage out there. It has the all natural lemon and lime and tons of carbonation that you've been looking for.

Zevia Twist tastes so refreshing. The flavor from natural oils of lemons and limes really comes through. I'm a water drinker because soda just never quenched my thirst. But this stuff does. And it's healthy - none of the artificial sweeteners, colors and flavors - chemicals - in all the regular diet sodas. You have to try it to believe it.
I was addicted to Fresca for years.  I knew the Aspartame was bad for me but I still chugged 3 a day.  No more!  Zevia Twist is better and uses Stevia which is natural.  I love it, love it, love it!
After you get use to the lack of sweet from all the sugar in soda it is hard to go back to regular soda.  Hopefully it is a healthy alternative.

lemon lime twist and all zevia sodas are great and a  healthier option to regular and diet sodas.  They don't have all the sugar of  regular soda and the harmful chemicals of the diet sodas.  A Dr I work with stated she normally eats healthy but she stated she has a soda addiction and she is worried it's going to  harm her bones.  I had a zevia mountain dew with me that night and asked if she likes mountain dew, she stated that's her favorite so I gave it to her, she looked at the ingredients and was thrilled with what was and wasn't in it.  She stated she thinks she could definitely get used to this, and not hurt her bones.  Amazon shipped it quickly, great product.

OK, let me start out by saying I'm extremely biased when it comes to sodas. I grew up with all the delicious teeth-rotting HFCS sodas such as Coke, Dr. Pepper, 7Up, Mountain Dew, and Fanta. And I'm allergic to Aspartame, so artificial sweeteners and I don't usually get along. But I have tried some Stevia-based products before and they weren't too bad, so I thought maybe this would be OK.Boy was I wrong. This stuff is now on my list of "Worst Sodas I've Ever Tasted", right up there with Russian malt soda and that disgusting No-Cal junk. I had expected a little better than this, but should've known better. If anyone ever comes out with a better Stevia-based soda, let me know. I'm willing to give anything a try at least once.

column9: From a recovering Diet Mountain Dew addict
column10: Last year, I was drinking probably two 24 packs of Diet Mountain Dew a week. I thought this was rather unhealthy (and expensive), so I decided to gradually taper off. I had decided to steer clear of all types of pop, but while at Sunflower Market, I noticed Zevia. I liked that it was sweetened with stevia, rather than something a little more artificial. I allow myself a maximum of one Mountain Zevia a day, if that. It has helped me rid myself of a pretty bad DMD addiction.

I had a Diet 7-UP a few days ago, and this tastes exactly the same to me. I love soda but I gave up my Diet Coke addiction a few months ago. Now I have one of these every few days and it's a really nice sweet treat without the addictive properties of aspartame-sweetened sodas.

I love this soda. Absolutely delicious. I used to be addicted to diet sodas, but after reading that sucralose (i.e. splenda) acts as a pesticide in your body (killing crucial intestinal flora) and that aspartame is made up of a main ingredient in paint thinner (methanol), I knew a change was necessary. Zevia was the exact crutch I needed to make it through. Incredibly, when I try other sodas now, it makes me sick and burns my throat. I would have given this product 5 stars, but the price recently went up, and it is not cost effective for most people to switch from cheaper sodas.

This was a first, but I couldn't get through the first can and my husband didn't get beyond a sip.It has a very strong aftertaste. Bitter almost.. I've been drinking beverages sweetened with stevia for several years now so I found the taste of the Zevia to be very enjoyable.  There was absolutely no after taste with the Zevia flavors I've tried and they are just as refreshing to drink as traditional sodas without any of the bad stuff! column9: Chemical-free Diet Soda + Free Shipping Make for a Winner
column10: I recently found out about Zevia through a friend but have had trouble finding it outside of health food stores, which aren't that easy to come by in my neck of the woods. I wouldn't have guessed to look for soda on Amazon, but the Zevia website pointed out it was for sale here, and when I found out about the free shipping, I ordered it on the spot.At just over a dollar a can, it's a tad pricey compared to other diet sodas, but that's to be expected for a specialty drink. The price here at Amazon is comparable to the prices I saw at the health stores, especially if you sign up for the subscription delivery which discounts things 15% at the time of this review. Also since you're not paying for shipping, I think it ends up being a good deal, especially considering the limited availability of the drink across the country.As far as taste goes, I've tried several of the flavors and like the lemon lime the best. If you're a Mt. Dew or 7-up fan, this is a similar style of drink. I do recommend that you try a can somewhere before ordering a 24-pack. If you at one time switched from regular soda to diet soda, you may remember that period of "getting used to it." I don't think it's as much of a stretch to switch from aspartame-sweetened diet soda to this, but I didn't love it at first taste.In regards to other flavors, I thought the orange and Dr. Zevia were okay. I wasn't a fan of the ginger ale at all, but that may just be because it uses real ginger (and tastes like it), unlike the watered down fake stuff I'm used to. I haven't tried the other flavors yet.Overall, I recommend Zevia to anyone who's trying to avoid high calorie beverages as well as artificial sweeteners.

column9: Very Good - Requires a few to get used to the change.
column10: OK,..I'm speaking on behalf of the Orange Soda here. When I first popped the tab and drank a sip of the Zevia Orange,..it did NOT hit me with the anticipated sweetness that I had come to expect from say a Diet Sunkist Soda or any of your typical SugarFree Orange sodas. I wasn't disappointed per say, but just surprised a bit by the unexpected lack of sweetness. Now, with that being said,...and a few cans later,..this has quickly become my "go to" drink when I want a refreshing orange soda. It is very good and very quenching (due to the noticeable lack of sodium) on a hot summer day. The aroma is wonderful and the flavor is very close to as real as you can get before drinking straight orange oil. It's a really good soda and I'm now tempted to try the Root Beer and the Cola.

This soda hurt my teeth. Drank one a day for 6 weeks. The Enamel on my teeth has eroded. My teeth are now still very sensitive. Read ingredients before drinking.  Consider battery  acid or this soda if your goal is to erode enamel!

column9: Great Base Sauce (and Low in Sugar!)
column10: I'm going to sound very old when I say this, but Classico Pasta Sauce has been my jarred pasta sauce of choice for 20 years.  It's not really that I'm old, just that I stick with what I like once I've found it, and though I've tried other sauces, I always always always come back to Classico.First of all, Classico's sauces are all very low in sugar.  Remember how Atkins and South Beach had everyone reading labels and forgoing ketchup and vinaigrette because of "hidden" sugars?  I'm not sure if Classico was ever Atkins-approved, but it is one of the national brands with the lowest sugar content.  In other words, if you like sweet tomato sauce, you might not like this one, but if you're trying to eat low on the glycemic index, look no further.  I really love the savory quality of Classico's sauces, which let the acidity of the tomato and bright punch of the basil, fruity olive oil and other pungent herbs shine.Of all Classico's pasta sauces, this is the ideal one for "semi-homemade" type dishes, where other ingredients share the spotlight.  For a straight pasta dish, I like adding sauteed garlic (don't let it burn!), crushed red pepper, and chopped kalamata olives, heating them through in the sauce, then adding the almost-cooked pasta and letting it finish cooking in the sauce.  If I'm feeling fancy, I'll saute my garlic in the oil from some pancetta I've rendered at the start, then sprinkle the finished, plated dish with the crispy pancetta bits.  Because Classico's sauces are a little on the thin side, they're perfect for finishing pasta; basically just undercook your pasta by a minute or two, then strain it and add it to the saucepan you've used to warm the Classico, letting the pasta absorb some of the sauce (instead of just the cooking water) to finish softening to al dente.I've given Tomato Basil "only" a four star review because, as much as I enjoy it, I agree with another reviewer who noted that their Four Cheese pasta sauce is really divine.  Tomato and Basil is a great basic, starter sauce, but Four Cheese is spoon-from-the-jar good.  (Don't judge me!)  I'm also very partial to their Florentine flavor, and the newer Carmelized Onion one as well, though I can't say I've tried a bad flavor yet.  Highly, deliciously, completely recommended.

column9: Good, but Classico makes an even better sauce than this!
column10: As a vegetarian, I find it a challenge to find jarred sauces that have great flavor on their own because I won't be relying on ground beef or chicken at home to add more flavor.  I need them to taste like real vegetables because that's what I want them to be made of!  I've used this Classico tomato and basil sauce for years, and have always been fairly satisfied with it.But, I just discovered Classico makes an even better sauce that is organic!  It's the Classico Organic Tomato, Herbs, and Spices sauce, and it is amazing.  Minimal sugar, so it's not too sweet.  I sampled it at a chain warehouse store and immediately bought the 3-pack of jars.  I recommend trying it if it's sold near you!
I saw this in a local store and on a whim I grabbed it.IT WAS LIKE SOMEONE OPENED A JAR OF DELICIOUSNESS AAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa.Seriously, it's good stuff.  Buy some.DO EEEET.

My Mother bought this a few months ago and it is by far the tastiest and most memorable pasta sauce I have ever had! It is so good that I just HAD to come online and share my thoughts about it with others. I definitely agree with 'booklover79' that many times, companies that make sauces seem to make them without vegetarians/vegans in mind. They make the sauce rather plain or bland and if eaten alone is rather...dull.--BUT NOT CLASSICO!The sauce has juuuust enough of a sweet taste to it that literally has me licking the remnants off my plate everytime. Leaves me wanting more, more, more.I feel like some sorta Ad-commercial with all this praise but, really, it is just...that good!I would deff recommend this to anyone looking for a new flavorful pasta sauce (also comes in many other flavors which you can find on the actual website right here: [...]5/5 :P
This sauce is a little thin and not very sweet as others have noted. I doctored it up with splenda and some spices, probably would not buy again.
I have yet to find anything better! It has a lot of flavor, thick chunks of tomato, and is low in price. Awesome sauce!

I really prefer homemade sauces and usually it doesn't take much time to make a simple sauce from scratch if I use canned tomatoes to start with. It's not always an option though. My husband lived in Italy for a few years and can be very picky about tomato sauces as well so finding good convenient ones is a little trickier.The first thing I look for in a jarred sauce is that it's not too sweet. A lot of jarred sauces suffer from too much sugar so you can't taste all the flavors of the sauce itself, much less what you put it on. So I look for ingredients similar to what I'd use. This sauce is made from tomato puree, diced tomatoes, onions, salt, basil, garlic, olive oil and other seasonings in trace amounts. Pretty close to what I put into mine except I'm also nuts for oregano. There are nice sized chunks of tomatoes in the sauce and it's liquid enough. The flavor is good, the garlic and onions aren't overpowering and it doesn't have that off taste that some sauces can have. It does taste pretty fresh.It's great for quick meals. Poured over chicken breasts and topped with cheese, or baking fresh ravioli in it are two of the meals my family makes when I can't cook. We always keep a couple jars on hand for that reason. It also makes a decent pizza sauce when my daughter wants quick pizzas.

column9: Classico sauce is the only sauce I use!!!
column10: I absolutely love Classico sauce.  It's the only Sauce I buy.  It's been a staple in my house for years.  The four cheese sauce is the best!!  Every time I am forced to use a different brand of sauce I am sadly disappointed!!

I was looking for something with real ingredients that did not have preservatives and artificial ingredients and was pleasantly surprised. This is such a rich and thick, creamy texture. There was a sticker on the bottle that said "Tastes great on fresh peaches." Now, I did try it on fresh peaches but it definitely had to be an acquired taste, meaning I was not too cray about it. Just the right size, easy to store, looks great and tastes wonderful.  Superfast shipping.  I don't know why people joke about not liking fruit cake, we like it much better than pumpkin pie.

Claxton Dark Fruitcake has been a holiday tradition in our family since the mid 1950's. I ordered it directly from the company this year and when I served it at Thanksgiving, my guests and I thought I must have been fooled by a counterfeit website just claiming to sell Claxton fruitcakes. It was at best 40% fruits and nuts and consisted of a gummy light colored "cake". I emailed the company and expressed my disappointment. After several emails back and forth and after today talking to one of the owners, they assured me that it was the original dark recipe.In reading the ingredients, I noticed that corn syrup, sugar and high fructose corn syrup were listed after flour which was the 4th ingredient. At the very end were listed molasses, spices and 3 artificial food dyes. High fructose corn syrup wasn't widely available until the mid 1970's to mid 1980's, so I'm not sure how it was one of the original ingredients.All of the people I talked to seemed to have the attitude that I was so stupid that I couldn't possibly be observing what I had correctly. Although they offered to send replacements if I returned it at my own expense, they told me that what I would receive would be identical to what I have. One of the owners informed me that they had received zero complaints this year.I am grieving the loss of an almost 55 year tradition, but the other 4 cakes are now in the trash.

if you can believe it im 32 and never had fruit cake before. so i decided what the heck i'll buy some. had to shop here because it's obviuslly not in season at the stores. needless to say i thought it had to be the nastiest thing anyone has ever tried to pass as food. tastes like really dark licorshe. i gave the rest away, but those people seemed to like it , so i guess it's just a matter of perssonal taste.same thing happed when i ordered bauklava, which i had some years ago and liked it.the moral of the story is try not to go grocery shopping on the internet!!hope this helps!!
dark recipe.  This fruitcake is just what I was hoping it would be.  I believe anyone who is a fruitcake fan will enjoy these tasty tidbits.

column10: Claxton fruitcake is just the best.  We used to get it from the church that sold it as a fundraiser in Worcester,Ma.Had not seen it in years, and my spouse  mentioned he'd like some good fruitcake. I went internet fishing and the result is the best. Still !!

My vet recommended Dentahex Chews for our two poodles. That was three years ago and we have never looked back.  I order the petite size. One piece can be broke in half and is enough for each to enjoy. They seem to be content as they chew on their daily treat and both have nice white teeth.
Best treat for keeping your dog's teeth and breath fresh and clean.  This is a great product and worth the cost.
I guess they are pretty good, Lacy loves them. She gets a couple a week most of the time.

I happen to enjoy London Dry gin. Usually I drink a dry martini but I'll sometimes drink a salty dog or, as Douglas Adams once wrote, a Jinnon Tonnik. (42 to those in the know). A Salty dog uses grapefruit juice as a mixer, and it really brings out the juniper flavor of gin without competing with it.I bought these bitters because I had read an online recipe for "The Queen Mum's" cocktail of gin and duBonnet. Several ratios were mentioned but in the ratio I liked best, the recipe recommended a few dashes of these bitters.I have to agree with the advise. These bitters bring out the juniper flavor without competing. I haven't tried them with a dry martini and probably never will, but for the Queen Mum's cocktail they were just the thing! I guess they might work with a Salty dog, too, but as there's already grapefruit mixer in that one, I'm not in a hurry to find out.These are like a concentrated grapefruit flavor without the tanginess. More flavor, not more citric acid, and a little bit of something else I can't quite place. Not for every liquor, but for gin, I'd heartily recommend these!
These bitters give a nice fragrant tang to your drinks.  They're very good with gin drinks or anything that you might serve with a lemon twist.

"The bold citrus taste of glycerin combines with the artificial flavors to create a uniquely disgusting cocktail ingredient."Excuse my sarcasm, but this is one of the most disappointing bar purchases I've ever made. Unfortunately, I didn't look at the ingredients until after I purchased the bottle. I had read about Fee Brothers Bitters in an old New York Times article about the rebirth of cocktail culture. Silly enough, I assumed they were artisanal and naturally flavored. The ingredients list reads like a pack of Fruit Roll Ups: Water, Glycerin, Flavors - Natural and Artificial Extracts and Flavors.These bitters taste awful. There's a slight grapefruit flavor behind the awful, overpowering lime (as in limestone, not key lime) flavor. If you want grapefruit flavor in your drinks, this isn't the bitters for you. You should really just buy a bag of grapefruits and spritz a small amount of juice into your drink. I've used this in a couple of drinks, and each turned out poorly. I thought it might give my Negroni a nice additional grapefruit boost, but all it did was poison the drink. It tasted chemically and sour. DO NOT USE THESE BITTERS!!!

column9: Best Tea on Earth (No, I don't own company stock!)
column10: Everyone in my house is addicted to this tea. We drink it iced. Make one or two pitchers of it a day. It's not sweetened, but has a subtle, natural sweetness to it. column9: Spendy, but my 7 pupkids love it!
column10: Received 3 cases, 1 each of the beef,pork,chicken, a week ago. All of my dogs love this mixed with their Wellness dry foods. When we introduced Beefy Rice to our three "kids," Sturgis-the-Wonder-Peke, Bobette (aka Alien-Love-Child), and Ellie Mae Dobby Diana (our little rescue mix), the response was overwhelmingly over-the-top HAPPY!!  They've always been pretty much tolerant of their dry food, no one seemed to be doing the happy dance prior to meal-time.  Well, except for EMDD, who spent her first year being horribly neglected.  She does the happy dance for just about anything now that her life has turned around. She is now back to full health with all of her hair back.  Thanks Rudy Greens, your food is great.

I was a little hesitant to buy this.  Glad I did; I love this vanilla product.  From hot cereal and smoothies, to coffee and tea and hot chocolate, to baked goods and fresh fruit ... well, just about anything that could benefit from a little sweet richness without any alcohol. column9: Spam, Spam, Spam, Spam, SPAM! (Don't knock it 'til you try it...)
column10: This is the perfect put-it-in-the-cabinet-and-forget-it emergency meat with a very long shelf life.How long a shelf life? Well, I've got some that says "Best by Apr. 27, 2012" which has probably been in the cabinet for at least two or three years already.It's not something you'll probably want to eat every day (or even every week), but it's great to keep on-hand. Good for natural disasters, power outages, camping, college dorms, financial shortages or times when you just don't feel like cooking anything.One pack is the perfect serving size for a sandwich or to chop up and mix with a can of beans for a filling meal.You can also eat it straight from the package without barfing because it doesn't have a ring of gelatinous goo like its canned counterpart.
This is an excellent backpackers meat.  My son loves the taste - I am impartial, but the packaging is great for travel/backpacking.I understand they love this stuff in Hawaii????
I love these individual packages!  Now I don't have to waste half a can if only one person wants it.  My sister sends these in her husbands lunch.  They're great!
Spam brings back happy memories of a simpler childhood, and happiness was easier to attain. Each time I have an individually packed slice, it brings a smile to my face.

Ok, we get it, not everyone loves SPAM. Yeah, it's meat...in a can.But you can do many things with this delicious treat. Like others have mentioned, SPAM Musubi is great "sushi" treat popular in Hawaii. Rice, Nori (Seaweed) and some slightly cooked, thinly slice Spam makes a great Lunch or Dinner. Problem is, when you use a whole can of SPAM, you usually can get 8, maybe 9 slices out of it. So if you don't plan on making Lunch/Dinner for 3 or so people, you end up with extra SPAM you either have to eat right away (within a few days) or it goes to waste.But these are terrific! You can take one out, fry it up, and your done! Can't believe I didn't think of getting these earlier. Personally, I love sliced up Spam on rice with a little Furikake on it.

column9: Great to have in the pantry
column10: Okay, while this isn't health food by any stretch of the imagination, two of my children love it. I think it is great that the packages have such a long shelf life. Buying on Amazon, especially with Subscribe and Save is much cheaper than purchasing this product in the grocery store. Always love having some on the shelf. Not an every day food, but a great "mommy is tired, here you go" sort of thing.

I love spam.  But not many others do.  So having it in this size pouch is perfect.  It makes a nice sandwich, since it's about the size of a piece of bread.  Another reviewer mentioned Hawaii.  Yup, spam is very, very popular there, and is found in many flavors.  This single-size portion of original flavor spam is large enough to make 2 "Hawaiian breakfasts" of fried spam, sliced warmed/fried pineapple and a croissant.  And it is a good thickness to make spam musubi, a sushi roll made with spam, rice and seaweed that is often offered in Hawaii as a grab-and-go meal.  Hmm, I see a spam sandwich for lunch today after all this spam talk.

OK, I can't stand this stuff -- but my husband absolutely loves it.  Brings back memories of his distressed childhood in the '50s, when no one in his community had much meat and a can of SPAM was a treasure to be shared breathtakingly with a lot of people.OK, so what do we do?  I hate having an open whole can in the fridge -- for one, it's unpleasant for me, and two, it just means that to try to finish it he'll eat more as soon as possible, which is hardly good for him (or he'll eat the whole can right from the start --ditto!).But these single serving packs are a godsend.Yes, one is exactly the right size for a sandwich.  So what if I hate it that he takes 2 to work?  That's better than a whole can's worth, right?  And it IS great emergency food (for him, I mean -- I can't imagine how hungry I'd have to be to eat this, even if the power were out, but then again he can't stand my emergency pouches of white meat tuna in water, so we're even!).I don't care that the packaging is wasteful, I don't care that it costs more -- this product is terrific, solving different problems for both of us!  We're happy to have a case in the house, now almost empty, and we'll be ordering more.  For the SPAM lover in your life, this is a good solution for both of you!

Check the nutrition info.If you use Amazon Prime and subscribe 'n save, the price is cheaper per oz than by the can at the grocery store.Use it for a quick sandwich, or add to a pasta salad.Just the right size to fry up and make a spam n veggie frittata.Take it on hikes or backpacking, or keep some in you 72hr pack instead of so many granola bars and jerky.Can millions of Pacific Islanders be wrong?

column9: Perfect for travel, fits all screw-top pouched baby food
column10: Bought this at Babies R Us.  They are perfect for feeding baby on the go directly from the pouched baby food.  Although it says it was designed for Plum, it indeed fits most pouched brands including Plum, HappyBaby, and Ella's Kitchen).  The dispensing hole is bigger than some of squeeze top feeder so you can feed meals that are a little bit chunkier than puree food.  Pouched baby food is already easier to pack than jarred food, with this spoon, pouched food is the way to go for traveling with babies!!!

This is one of the COOLEST baby gadgets I've found, I feel like shouting it from the rooftops.If you buy organic baby food for your little one, these spoons are a MUST!  They make feeding on-the-go so easy and make clean-up a cinch.  No bowls for your baby to put their hands in (or for you to wash).  These spoons screw onto the top of pouch baby food that has the screw-top.  It works with Plum Organics, Ella, HappyBaby, Peter Rabbit and Revolution Foods.  I have also used the Boon Spoons which are cool but do require more cleanup as you have the spoon, tip and silicone base to clean up.  These are also MUCH smaller and more portable for travel, I slip the case of spoons and 1-2 pouches of baby food in the diaper bag.  You can feed her solid food in the car and it's relatively neat!If you don't buy organic food (normally) for your little one, but are interested in this product for travel / eating out, I'd still recommend it.  You may be able to find a pack of 2 for a fraction of the price sold here (which is a 4-pack).  So do check your local baby food store as well.We use the Gerber Organic plastic tubs at home, too, as they are cheaper than the pouch foods.  The nice thing about the spoons is that it doesn't contaminate the food so you can reseal and reuse it later if the feeding was not very productive.  (I'd say within 24 hours or whatever the manufacturer of the food recommends).  My husband is guilty of opening the Gerber tub food, not putting it in a bowl, feeding our daughter two bites and then the rest goes to waste.  So this system is a lot more efficient despite the higher cost of the 'pouch' food.

column9: Not as great as I anticipated
column10: I bought one of these and used for feeding with my 6 month old.  I thought it would be very convenient, especially on the go.  However, I found that the spoon is too deep for my baby.  She can't get all food into her mouth so there's always some left on the spoon.  And since the hole is at the bottom of the spoon, you need to squeeze a lot out in order to fill the spoon up.  It might work better when she's older and can take bigger bites.

These are the perfect travel spoons.  They work perfectly with the Plum brand, as well as other brands of baby food in the pouches.  With 3 kids, the less I have to remember when I travel, the better.  I definitely recommend these to other moms working on solids with their babies.

This is one of those, "now why didn't I think of that?!!" products.  I thought the pouches were a great improvement but never thought about connecting an actual spoon to the pouch to make it even better.  I'm so glad Boon did!  I came on Amazon to buy another of the Book Squeeze Spoons and saw these.  It's exactly what I wanted and I didn't even know it.  I was squeezing the pouches into the Boon Squeeze Spoon - this removes an entire step and makes things every so easy.  And for people like me who want to use every last drop of the food it ends the frustration of knowing that I'm losing a little on the inside of this and the inside of the container I put the food into.  On the first use I was already developing a technique to get the most out of those pouches while squeezing it into the spoon - I'm a little crazy about stuff like that :)I know people complain about the spoon bowl being a little deeper than most baby spoons but I don't see it as a problem at all. When my babies are little they don't clean the spoon on the first pass, I either turn and tilt the spoon so they can get the last bit or forget about it and squirt more in.  It's not a big deal.  When they get older they'll clean it out just fine.  It's the same size as the Boon Squeeze Spoon so we're already used to it.The only concern I had was that these would get lost down the garbage disposer when tossed into the sink.  I solved that by putting in one of those mesh strainers that covers the drain.  All in all it's a great product!

I often use the pouches of food and I thought this would be so great!  My only complaint is that the hole is all the way at the top of the spoon so the food pools up there.  You have to shake it to move it down or overload the spoon.  I still like it and I use it a lot when I'm out, but I wish the hole was a little more centered or towards the front.  I have no idea how that would work (constructionally), but it would be easier feeding.
