column10: These were selling for approx $12.50 for 2 boxes of 160 pieces per box....some of the vendors on amazon are charging double that. I ordered the watermelon and the apple- it's nice to get your favorite flavors and not have to dig through a bag looking for them.Mine arrived in clean boxes. they were sealed and wrapped in plastic. i've opened up 1 box of watermelon and 1 box of apple- they weren't broken and they weren't melted or stuck to the wrapper. and they taste great. i purchased from amazon and not an independent vendor.

I have been hooked on Jolly Rancher watermelon candies since high school (that's 40 years this year!); they were in the only vending machine in the school...next to the gym. A classmate offered me one and after that I saved up a quarter to get them whenever they appeared. Later on you were able to buy bags of watermelon only candy in the grocery store. Then a few years back Jolly Rancher stopped this practice and only offered the mix of five original flavors. Well, the apple was sorta edible, the others less so, especially the cherry...if you were raised in the early 1960s like I was, you'll remember that EVERY med for children (except for Liquiprim, which was bubble-gum flavored), liquid and chewable was cherry flavored. And the cherry flavor Jolly Rancher tastes exactly like all those awful cough syrups, liquid antibiotics, and whatever else you had to swallow when you were sick. Talk about bringing back bad memories!More recently I had been buying my watermelon Jolly Ranchers at a candy store called Fuzziwigs, but it closed. I was reduced to filching watermelon candies out of mixed bowls at events (my last three came out of the candy bowl the fire department had set up at the Home Show). And then I searched on Amazon...Thank you for one of the best early birthday gifts ever!

The product name led me to believe that the total package is of 160-count, split in two packs of 80-count each. However, there are two boxes of 160-count each.These shipped from Amazon quick, via subscribe and save. When I first signed up, the estimate delivery date was a week later. However, these were shipped the same night, and arrived the next day, 5 days earlier than the estimate. So definitely don't worry about the shipping speed.These are very fresh, unlike some of the old shelf Jolly Ranchers that are kind of melted into the wrapper, and you can't take the wrapping off without your fingers getting all sticky. There is definitely a difference in the freshness,  and it's a good thing.Flavor wise, this is my favorite flavor, and if they came in a mixed-flavor pack I'd pick these out right away. However, having only watermelon, all the time, without having to pick them out, got really old really quick, and kind of ruined the flavor for me. Maybe it's because I ate like 20 of them the first day they arrived. lol.Anyway, if you like the watermelon flavor, definitely get this. A good idea is to buy this, plus a mix-flavor bag, and mix them together. That way, you get some variety once in a while, but still able to eat as much watermelon ones as you want!
I love Jolly Ranchers and I love watermelon so this is the prefect buy. You get two boxes full of Watermelon Jolly Ranchers.

column9: Exceptional value for an all around favorite treat
column10: Watermelon Jolly Ranchers are sumptuously good and whether you've got a candy jar on the corner of your desk at work, at home, or need something for a road trip, these are the hands down winners by far.I cannot count how many times I've seen adults pout because there were no more Jolly Ranchers in the candy jar on my desk at work, or how many times grown men would cull through the assortment to find that last, golden Watermelon candy.So, when they started to come out with the mega pack of just the watermelon candies it was a no brainer to grab one up.The problem with that is that they are so good they disappear quickly, and when I found these at a local wholesaler, I paid for one box what they are charging for a double pack here, so BUY, BUY, BUY!The other fantastic feature about these phenomenally delicious watermelon candies is that they are no fat and very low in calories, so you can indulge with big flavor and have zero guilt.

column9: Glad I found watermelon flavor here.
column10: Just like every one else here, I love the watermelon flavor but couldn't find them bulk at local stores.  I'm glad I found this one for a couple of dollars cheaper ($12.55 ss) than Jolly Ranchers themself for twice as much (320 total) on Amazon.  I was going to give these out for Halloween, but these two boxes of 160 Jolly Ranchers will go fast in my household. Time to buy more. :)
What an easy transaction. I originally got one box of these for my wedding candy buffet, but needed more. This was so easy, and the price was GREAT!
Ahh, this reminds me of when I was a kid, going to the local drugstore to get the famous Jolly Rancher Watermelons! Brings me back to my early childhood and tastes just how I remember!Enjoy! I am ;)

Watermelon Jolly Ranchers.  Seriously, how can you go wrong with a bulk package of these?  This was a double pack, two, 2 lbs boxes (320 count total), and will last months.  Absolutely nothing wrong with that.

I decided to sign up for this and have had great service since I did.  The product and cost are both great.  I have recently signed up for another service from them.  Would buy others if they offer them.  Great, Great...Items, Service and Cost.

I ordered Cherry. I don't like any of the other flavors.  I made sure that I ordered cherry but got watermelon and now it changed what I ordered to watermelon in My Account.  Guess I can give them out at Halloween.
No fuss no mess.  It was just exactly what I wanted.  The price was fantastic and I received just in time to start my sweet pickles.
this is my flavorite flavor i use this for rock candy for christmas for my grand children they lkove it
This is a very hard oil to find in your average supermarket. Ordering from LoriAnn was quick, easy and inexpensive.

column9: Not hard to find, thanks to Amazon
column10: Old Bay makes a lot of different mixes, but this exact one has been hard to find at my local stores, but Amazon came thru. A bit of a kick, (I use less than they suggest) but makes great crab cakes.
If you are looking for an easy way to make the best crab cakes, this mix is it.  The crab cakes are great, and easy to make.Everyone I have served them too loves them.
Excellent product, takes the guess work out of preparing Crab Cakes. So much simpler than using eggs, baking powder, parsley flakes and dried mustard.
This item was bought from Amazon, because they had the best price for a large quantity. Jiffy has always made a great product that is quick to make muffins.

My kids are 8 and 10, and they love to make these as either muffins or pancakes in the mornings. They are simple to make either way - and taste great! The fact that I was able to buy a case on Amazon was the true selling point for me - my kids go thru the mix like water and when I buy alot at the supermarket I have to lug all those groceries up stairs, with the Amazom Prime I get them shipped to my front door for free and cost me the same as I would have paid in the store. My kids also love the Jiffy Blueberry muffin mix and the Chocolate muffin mix as well. I am extremely happy with this purchase, and I plan to order these again in the future if they are available!

column9: Good fairly healthy for on the go
column10: I only got one of these to try so I didn't get to do much experimenting, but here is what I have to say after eating one of them1) yes, the entire thing was completely cooked to a good temperature after 60 seconds.2) this does not have to be refrigerated, making it an excellent choice to keep in a drawer at work or to take with you to school, not sure how well it will sit in a hot car, but seems like a good choice for that meal you wish you had the time or money for but just can't squeeze into the day3) Fairly healthy choice, whole grain pasta that actually tastes pretty good, and a tomato sauce rather than a dairy based which makes it a better choice4) portion size - I added this as a side to a breaded baked Italian chicken dinner.  It added a nice flavor and served the two of us well as the side.  If this were to be my entire meal I imagine this would feed one, as a side dish it feeds two.5) I don't know what the real price is for these, I would consider them to be valued at two to three dollars each.6) As far as the overall flavor, I found the sauce to be a little sweet for my taste, but for the convenience I could put up with the overly sweet sauce.I think that if the price is right, these are an excellent choice for healthy eating at the office, or at school or any other time that you are lacking on time and options.  I would buy these if they were to come available at the local grocer for a reasonable price.

This is my second experience with microwaved whole grain pasta. My first was was the Barilla Whole Grain Fusilli with Veggie Marinara and it was very tasty and enjoyable. This Tomato and Basil Penne Pasta dish not so much. The pasta was gritty, the tomato sauce was sweet with a tad too much basil AND something missing. The sprinkle of Parmesan/Romano cheese I added didn't help. I'm just not a fan of this entree.I still like Barilla's concept of pasta in 60 microwave seconds with the option for adding a teaspoon of water and another 30 seconds for more tender pasta. But even that can't remedy the gritty penne pasta. The 2-stage plastic film venting and removal is STILL a bit tricky. The unique packaging that separates the pourable sauce cup from the pasta to avoid sogginess while cooking can be the source of spillage and additional cleanup. Follow the directions AND steady the container removing both the plastic and the sauce.I'm not likely to purchase this item regardless of the healthy fiber and convenience.

Pasta with pre-made sauce isn't very hard to make.  You boil water, drain it, and heat some sauce in the microwave. The idea that somebody needed to prepackage it and make it simpler seemed to be going a bit far to me. But the convenience factor of having a meal in 60 seconds, not needing a refrigerator and being able to heat it up in workplaces made me want to see how much I'd be compromising for convenience.I shouldn't have fretted. After all, Barilla makes Tomato and Basil Sauce and heating it after taking it out of a jar is no different from heating it while it's in its own compartment in a microwavable tray. I used to make my own pasta (whole wheat is harder to work with so I got lazy) and if I can accept dried pasta, then the idea of pasta that's not dried but has the right water content to be microwaved isn't as odd as it seemed.It turned out to be just as advertised. You cook it for 60 seconds, a tray of sauce lifts out, and you pour it on the pasta. It tastes just as good as if you bought dried pasta and a jar of sauce. You don't lose out by getting something microwavable.The company is also fairly honest about the ingredients and it says right on the front of the package that it's made with 51% whole wheat pasta.  That's a lot better than the competition, which likes to say "made with whole grain" even though they refine some of the grain and pretend the two are separate ingredients. All the ingredients seem good and wholesome except for the mysterious "natural flavors" ingredient. It's not necessarily bad for you, but it's not necessarily good for you. I have no way of knowing. This is low in saturated fat, the non-saturated variety comes from olive oil, which is good for you, and the only thing that it's a bit high in is sugar. It contains eight grams. But I'd guess that it would contain about five grams if there were no added sugar, since it occurs naturally in other ingredients.The bottom line is that this is as good as store bought pasta that you boil yourself. If you like Barilla's jarred sauce, and you like their dried pasta, then you'll like this just as much and you'll like the convenience.

There is no question that when it has came down to microwavable pasta meals, they have been more of a miss than a hit, and sadly lagged upon the taste that was originally was suppose to appeal to the eyes. Barilla has known that when they have made pasta, and their microwaveable pasta meals actually stand out well. Their Whole Grain Mezze Penne with Tomato & Basil stands out well, not just in taste, but also feels like you're really eating pasta on the go, rather than something that was watered down from the other companies like Healthy Choice and their Fresh Meal makers, or other pasta meals that feels waned down. I liked how this tasted at the start, and it was easy to make and a treat to taste. I definitely love this pasta.Price: BTaste: B+Overall: B+

This is a non-refrigerated, microwaveable meal containing whole-grain pasta and tomato sauce. The packaging states that it is "100% Natural" and contains "No Preservatives." How Barilla is able to give us tomato sauce in liquid form yet without any chemicals to keep it palatable is a mystery to me. The plasticized tray packaging is sealed tightly with a stout film cover, so I guess that's the key.The primary ingredient is whole-grain pasta which is made with whole-grain Durum, Semolina, Durum wheat flour and oat fiber. Speaking of fiber, the one portion will give you 11 grams worth or a whopping 44% of a 2000-calorie diet! For those of us who have reached the stage of life where fiber intake is critical, this is a wonderful bonus. Unfortunately, the pasta is a bit on the chewy side, owing I would guess, to all that fiber. The instructions indicate that you can add a little water before cooking and then cook a little longer to soften the Penne. I had only the one evaluation package, so I was not able to test this option. I have an 1100-watt microwave, and found the 1-minute cooking time adequate.The rest of the ingredient list yields nothing suspicious other than "Natural Flavors," and "Tapioca Starch."The Tomato sauce is packaged in a separate "Sauce Tray" which fits in the main packaging and is microwaved with it. Prior to heating, you peel back the film covering over the sauce to vent the package. When heating is complete, you remove the sauce tray and pour it over the pasta. That works fine. I had no difficulties with any of this.The package will give you 310 calories with 5g of fat and 690mg of sodium. The sodium is high (29%) as it is in virtually all pre-packaged meals. It seems the manufacturers have learned how to control all the nutrients--calories, fat, cholesterol, carbs, everything--except salt.I don't think I'd go out of my way to eat this, but for what it is--an ultra-simple, convenient, quick meal that you could stick in your briefcase or backpack on the way out to work--it was pretty good. If you don't have a cafeteria and don't want something from the deli or the take-out places, this is a good alternative.I just need to say a word about price: I never base my ratings on price, because that can change with time and retailer and sales, but DO NOT pay 45 bucks for 6 of these shipped. That's just plain nuts. At three to four dollars apiece, they make sense based on their convenience. At seven plus, they don't.

I do like the fact that you can just store these in a drawer at work... they need no refrigeration/freezing. So they're very convenient (that's the third star). However, they're not particularly great.First off, the plastic film cover is practically superglued on, so be prepared to clean up a lot of tomato sauce when you finally manage to rip the thing open. The instructions say "ready in just 60 seconds," but you're really talking around 2-3 minutes. I honestly don't know where they get 60 seconds from.The pasta tastes like rubbery plastic, even if you add a little water before microwaving. I do like how the little sauce compartment lifts out of the main dish so you can then pour the sauce separately. Taste-wise, it's... edible. Not horrible, not great. When you don't have the time to go out for lunch or prepare your lunch before work, you'll be happy to have one of these handy containers in your office drawer, but I'm afraid it's not particularly tasty.

column9: Bland and vaguely gamy tasting, skip this one
column10: As far as prepared dinner kits go, "Barilla Whole Grain Mezze Penne with Tomato and Basil Sauce" just did not do it for me...and this is coming from a person who ONLY eats freshly-prepared Barilla Whole Grain Pasta at home!The sauce is blandly sweet and completely forgettable, while the pasta itself was more mushy than al dente and had a vaguely gamy taste, too boot.In all, as a long time Barilla fan, I'm quite disappointed with this product. There are far tastier prepared dinner options out there to recommend this.

column9: Fantastic for meals on the go!
column10: I'm a landscape architect and at any given moment, I can end up in one of three neighboring states working on jobs. Eating out is EXPENSIVE and after you've had a month of home-made sandwiches, even the Earl of Sandwich can no longer entice me to chomp down on one.So, I'm constantly on the look-out for meals that I can keep in my truck that require NO REFRIGERATION or Pots/Pans to create the meal. I usually have access to a microwave at a client's home or a gas station, and if you know the staff well enough, they have no problem with your using their microwave to make your meal.I was exceedingly pleased with this product. The whole grain penne made me happy that I was eating well and the sauce had just the right amount of kick without it tasting like a Kid's Meal. Perfect portions; I didn't need anything else to fill me up for lunch. I plan on keeping a box of these meals in my truck for times that I just can't eat one.more.sandwich. or for a quick pick me up when supper is hours away. Plus, I love Barilla pasta and frozen meals so I was delighted to know that these meals come from a company I buy from and trust with quality products.

column9: Don't care for  the whole grain
column10: We got this along with the spicy marinara one. I thought we should try and 'go healthy.' There is much better whole grain pasta out there. This was not a big hit with me or my kids. We liked the concept though. It heated quickly. I guess it's precoooked so that's why it's really ready in 60 seconds (as stated on the package). The price is fine too -- just go for the Spicy Marinara instead.

I was starving after coming back from my workout, so I wanted something quick and healthy for my lunch. This pasta meal did the trick. It cooks up in one minute and was easily prepared by mixing the sauce tray with the pasta. The sauce made this dish. It was very flavorful and not overly salty. The pasta was served al dente. The portion was actually about right for a lunch item. The other thing I like is that it is not a frozen food item, which is great for those that don't have a refrigerator/freezer available at work to store it.The only downside is the high amount of carbs, which can be expected from pasta. The Amazon pricing is competitive with other meals of this sort, at roughly $3 carton. If you use Amazon's subscribe and save, and the $5 e-coupon, it is definitely a bargain and must have for that last minute lunch.

column4: Glenda Boozer "Live, live, live! Life is a ba...
column9: Plain, but easy, satisfying and reasonably healthy
column10: Barilla Whole Grain Mezze Penne with Tomato and Basil Sauce really is ready in just one minute: peel back the cover to the dotted line, hit the Add Minute button on your microwave (it's easier if you set it on a plate before you put it in there, but ok without), and rustle up a drink and a fork during the short wait. I forgot to put my thumb on the sauce tray last time, but even that was no disaster; I pushed it back down from its tilt, poured the sauce on the pasta and grabbed a fork. I thought I would be much hungrier, but this was enough for a light meal or a substantial snack. I need to see about getting a stack of these for bringing to work.

I was actually pretty surprised that this tasted as good as it did. I hate the taste of Chef Boyarde and feared Barilla  would also have that dead can mass factory mystery product taste and oder. It did not. In fact it actually tasted pretty close to what you'd get if you use their dry product and jar pasta sauce.What i really liked was that the sauce was in it's own separate dish. This allows you add as little or as much sauce as you need. The pasta was aldente. Often timesthese type of products have a very mushy consistence but this did not. Perhaps because the product is not sitting in sauce the whole time prior to cooking.The portion is reasonable as a side dish. However, too small for a stand alone lunch or dinner. This is an excellent product to add your own left over beef or chicken or vegetables.

column9: Who would have thought fast pasta could be so good?
column10: Simple review: Good Flavor, quick, easy and appropriately sized for one person. Keeping the sauce separate makes the flavor of the pasta and the sauce come alive. Well done Barilla!

column9: not bad for a quick microwave meal
column10: You could certainly do worse than this for a quick microwave meal. You heat up the pasta and sauce at the same time. Of course, it's not like real pasta. Still, I was pleasantly surprised - even without adding water, the pasta comes out well cooked - not too soft, not too hard. The only thing I don't like about the pack is that it's tricky to peel back the lid without getting sauce all over. Be careful when pulling back that lid.

This is a great product for those seeking an alternative to prepare a quality dish.  The product is very easy to prepare and gives you the basics.  You can enjoy as it is prepared, or simply add vegetables, meat or fish and you really have built a very good meal.  The packaging is attractive and the directions are very straightforward.

I had a good impression of the product overall. My specific observations:- The meal has some protein, iron and vitamin A with no cholesterol. Like that. You can tell it's going to be a substantial lunch because the package is heavier than any of the frozen food lunch entrees I've purchased. (I like that it doesn't have to be frozen or refrigerated, by the way -- more portable and practical for taking for lunch.)- The packaging is user-friendly and the instructions clear, with illustrations.- A minute for the cooking time was perfect. The sauce tray lifted out easily, and the sauce poured out of it and onto the pasta just great -- not too thick that it had to be spooned or scraped out.- The pasta was very firm, and I could taste the whole wheat flavor. The flavor of the sauce was nice; I enjoyed it.- I love that the ingredients on this are all-natural -- I wish more companies would do that. The packaging separates the sauce from the pasta to help avoid the need for preservatives. A+ on that. It would be great if there were a way to make the bowl cardboard instead of plastic, since microwaving plastic is not healthy, but I won't quibble about that here.

Having always been partial to Barilla sauces, when I saw this offering on the Vine program, I went for it.And we were not sorry. This was a nice "fast" food dinner, without the extra calories or fat.The sauce in this case was a little sweet, but it was a good meal. Thanks Barilla!

column9: Pretty good for microwavable food, but too pricey...
column10: I really wasn't expecting much from this dish, but was pleasantly surprised. Most one-bowl microwave meals are edible but not much beyond that. This dish, however, was quite tasty and filling as well. Keeping the sauce and pasta separate really does the trick, since the pasta has no chance to get mushy. On the contrary, it was pretty firm and had a nice bite to it. I prefer whole wheat pasta, and the taste, while not as good as if I'd cooked it myself, was more than passable. The tomato/basil sauce was quite good, just spicy enough, with some distinctive and separate flavors. And designing the sauce tray so that it can be picked up and poured over the pasta was a nice touch. All in all, I found this much more palatable than other microwave dishes I've eaten. However, the current price of 6 for $36 ($6 apiece) is far too high for what you're getting, especially when similar dishes sell in supermarkets from $2 to $3 each. So is it good enough to buy? No. Lower the price and I'd consider it.

I have previously tried the Whole Grain style of pasta from a box and thought it was very nasty, but thought that I would give this one a try as I had hoped it had improved over time (not same brand) and was a healty choice.After slightly opening the plastic cover/wrap, to allow venting, you place it in the microwave to cook for 60 seconds.  After removing it, the plastic cover/wrap seems to be stuck a bit firmly to the container, so removal of it should be done carefully or you will spill your sauce.  There is a separate removable mini sauce tray inside of the larger pasta tray that allows you to pour the sauce on your pasta.The sauce tastes just like the normal Barilla sauce (not my normal brand) and the pasta was cooked just about right.If I had not known that this was Whole Grain pasta, then I might not have noticed the slight Whole Grain flavor of the pasta.  It really is not that noticeable and was not bad for what it was.If the price was right, I might have this again in the future.  Would be good for less than 2 bucks, but under three would work too.It is more likely to be used for a work or school lunch, as the portion size was not a "meal" for someone like myself.

I was so hungry, but feeling uninspired to cook another meal or even make a simple sandwich.  What a great time to try out this easy microwave pasta.  It's so easy, even for microwave food.  No scissors required, just pull back on the cover, microwave, mix the sauce that's been separated with the pasta together and voila, you have a side dish or meal for one.  I sprinkled a little parm on, to make it better.  Still it did seem a little lacking in flavor.  Maybe more salt and pepper would have helped out, or better yet, some frozen meatballs from Costco to throw in. For the ease and how handy it is, I would give it 5 stars.  For the healthy natural ingredients, I'd give it 5 stars. The flavor brings it down to just 4.  To be fair, the quick microwavable food that tastes better, usually isn't as healthy.All in all, a good choice for a simple, basic pasta dish, that's storable anywhere and healthy to eat.

This pasta meal tastes almost as good as Barilla's non-whole grain version. The main benefit to this whole grain version is--of course--almost twice as much fiber as the conventional version. It also contains 10 fewer calories and slightly fewer carbs and less sodium, so this whole grain dish delivers comparable taste in a healthier option. The tomato and basil sauce is just as tasty as Barilla's jarred sauces, and the shelf-stable convenience really can't be beat. Be careful as you're removing the film cover--be sure to hold the sauce tray down while you do so, or you'll risk spilling the sauce. I also recommend following the supplemental directions and adding a little extra water after the initial heating period and heating it for an additional 30 seconds in order to soften the noodles.

Barrill's pasta is basically canned spaghetti but the sauce is separate - making for firmer, tastier pasta when you heat it.  Cooks very quickly.  Box says 1 minute.  That wasn't quite warm enough for me using an 1100 watt microwave - 70 seconds was fine.The pasta was slightly too firm - box gives an alternate cooking method for less firm pasta but, since I only had the 1 box, I wasn't able to test that.Sauce was excellent and there was a lot of it.This would be an OUTSTANDING meal to take to the office since it's not frozen.Low fat, (5g/ 1g sat) Sodium 690mg - ok if you're good for 2,000 mg a day.  11g(!!) of fiber.  That's an amazing amount.This is good stuff.

Barilla Whole Grain Mezze Penne with Tomato and Basil Sauce is incredible.  It needs no refrigeration, so you can toss it into your kitchen cabinet, your desk at work or leave it in your briefcase.  It's quick to fix - only taking ONE MINUTE to heat in the microwave, you'll be eating before you know it.  And it's delicious!  Not something you just nuke and scarf to fill your belly.  The 9 ounce size is filling, but you can add a salad and bread if you're really hungry.  The pasta has a nice al dente chew to it and the sauce is really flavorful.  I love that this meal is only 310 calories and made with healthier whole grain pasta.  I will definitely buy these to keep on hand when I need something fast and flavorful!

What's nice about this is that you don't need to keep it in the freezer and it heats up pretty nicely.  The sauce is delicious, but I didn't care for the pasta that much.  I have a love/hate relationship with whole wheat pasta, being it seems to turn to mush if you have any as leftovers, but then I like the extra fiber.  So I thought a single serve might be a good way to get it.  But this pasta had an extreme nutty taste to it, much stronger than in any other whole wheat pasta I have ever eaten.  I didn't care for that and also it had a strange texture, almost rubbery.  The sauce was very good and I liked the how the sauce was packaged separate from the pasta and did a pretty good job of covering up the overly nutty pasta, but in the end I didn't enjoy the pasta so I most likely won't get this again.  I might try the non-whole wheat and see if that has a better texture because for me bad texture is as much a turn off as bad taste.  It's very eatable, but not what I would call good.3 stars.

column9: I have to admit to being a little skeptical.
column10: I was skeptical when I saw the information on this packaging that it cooks in 60 seconds in the microwave.  Then I have to admit to being skeptical that it would come anywhere close to being good.  Guess what folks?  Barilla made a believer out of me on both counts.This is a very ingeniously designed container so you need to read and follow the directions exactly.  Otherwise, I'm envisioning sauce splashed all over the inside of your microwave.  You also need to be careful after it has cooked and you have to pull that film off while holding the sauce container down with your thumb.  Once more, the possibility of sauce everywhere.  But the good news is that if you follow the directions and take it one careful step at a time you will be rewarded with a tasty meal of whole grain penne pasta in tomato basil sauce for 310 calories.  Definitely not a bad thing.  And I like that the sauce and pasta are in separate containers so it is my choice as to how much of the sauce to pour over the pasta.  The label says 100% natural with no preservatives so I worried just a tiny bit about that pasta (which simply MUST have been partially precooked) holding fresh until the best-if-used-by date, which for my box was March 2013.The 60 seconds was just right for having the sauce and pasta thoroughly heated through.  The marinara sauce has chunks of tomato in it so you know it's the real thing.  For my particular taste, the basil was a little too prominent, but at least you could easily see that fresh basil had been used.  I like food where I can recognize ingredients.  The 9 oz tray is a serving for one and was actually a little more than I could finish.  The pasta was definitely al dente so there are directions for how to soften it more if you don't like that much texture remaining after it is cooked.  This whole grain pasta provides 44% of daily dietary fiber, which is great, but also 29% of daily sodium which I thought might be a little high.  Total carbohydrates are 57g or 19% daily recommended.This definitely falls into the "fast and convenient" food category.  It also falls into the "good taste" food category for me.  I use Barilla dry pastas already but I have never tried any of their jarred sauces.  Now I'll be trying some of those too, just maybe not the ones with the basil.  I can positively see the benefit of having several boxes of this pasta meal on my pantry shelf.

column9: It has its pros and cons
column10: Pro: the package directions are correct when they say it only takes one minute to microwave this. If I still worked in an office and I wanted a fast lunch, this would be perfect. Pro: one serving is almost half the daily recommended amount of fiber you need. Con: the texture of the pasta is not great; I could definitely tell it was whole wheat. I like the flavor of whole grain pasta, but not when the texture is slightly gritty. Con: the basil flavor in the sauce is a little overpowering. This isn't my favorite pasta dish ever, but I would consider it again if I needed a really fast, convenient meal that would put a little more fiber and veggies in my diet.

This was the first time that I have used Barilla so I was interested to see how it was.  I do have mixed feelings.  I liked the flavor of the sauce, it was pretty good.  However, I did not like the noodles. I am not sure if it was the whole wheat pasta that I didn't like or what, but they were chewy and didn't have the best flavor.  Now I think this is a great product if you are in a hurry for several reasons, and here they are.  It is convenient, you can carry it with you to work or at home and just pop it in the microwave and have a meal. column9: Getting used to Turkish style coffee
column10: Let me start by saying that, while not a snob or connoisseur, I have tried just about every method of making coffee known to humanity. Drip, perk, pump and steam espresso, Aeropress, Neopolitan, Canadian-made coffee bags, Toddy concentrate and everything but pan boiled with eggshells. I've ground my own beans and even roasted them in small quantities. (I must have been an alchemist in a previous time!) Most of my gear (La Pavoni espresso machine, Capresso pump machine, Capresso conical grinder, countless Bialetti pots, Revereware stainless drippers, etc.,) have come from fortunate thrift store finds.My interest in Turkish style coffee came about with the purchase (online auction-used) of an ASTOUNDING Turkish-made fully electronic, sensor controlled masterpiece of an automatic maker from Beko which is even easy to clean! It has won awards from CeBIT, the world's largest and most international computer expo. Atatürk would be proud!I found that my grinder could produce very close to the powder-like nature of ground Turkish coffee. But I wanted to try "the real thing," so I ordered this brand and another. This brand is from Israel and comes as a set of smaller pouches, fulled sealed.My biggest surprise was that the coffee is not as dark roasted as what I had used before. But very pleasant with (traditionally) sugar or without.If you have a local coffee supplier with the gear to REALLY grind down to Turkish style, you are in luck.  If not, give this a try. Standard stove-top boiler pots are cheap, but the Bekos are not.

I am not sure why this particular order did not have the rich flavor that I have come to associate with "Cafe 1820"... it has been one of the my favorite coffees.  It usually has great rich flavor without the high acid content.  This batch seemed to be missing a lot of the flavor - it may have been on the shelf too long or stored at a high temperature.  I'll order it again, but if it is not up to par - I'll find another source.If you have never tried Cafe 1820, you should... but try to make sure that you are getting a true sample of their normally excellent product.

column9: I Have To Admit This Chili Is Seriously Delicious
column10: Bottom-Line: It's what for lunch every day.As I stated in my review of Campbell's Chunky Grilled Chicken w/ Vegetables and Pasta soup, I am a family man with the normal trappings of American society; i.e. a mortgage, car payment, insurance payments, children in school, medical bills, grocery bills, well you get the picture.  I am therefore frugal by design, because I do like to save a little of what I make.  That means that I rarely buy my lunch in the company-sponsored cafeteria, or at a local (sit down or take-out) restaurant.  I bring my lunch to work every day sometimes in the guise of "Campbell's Chunky Roadhouse Chili" in an 18.6 oz can or 18.8 oz microwave bowl.The soup brand, whose tag line used to be "so thick you could eat it with a fork, but bring a spoon because you'll want to get every drop,"  is actually quite tasty, much more so than Progresso Soup, which I find (very) bland in comparison.  And Campbell's Chunky Soup is good for you; most of the varieties have vegetables and lean cuts of meat, and are low in fat and contain at least 2 grams of dietary fiber, but "Campbell's Chunky Roadhouse Chili" contains a whopping 8 grams per serving."Campbell's Chunky Roadhouse Chili" has 230 calories and a still low 8 grams of fat per serving.  Loaded with generous portions of both beef and kidney beans this hearty bowl is enough to satisfy me for a few hours and the average cost is only $1.59 per microwave bowl at my local Target Super Store.  How is that for an inexpensive lunch?  However, my local Target and Jewel does not carry all of the varieties of this delicious chili, but enough so that I can partake in at least four times a month in a different flavor.Other varieties Campbell's offers include Firehouse Chili, Sizzlin' Steak, Tantalizin' Turkey, and Hold The Beans Chili.Nutritional InformationIngredients: water, tomato puree, seasoned beef crumbles, diced tomatoes, red kidney beans, kidney beans, contains less than 2% of the following: red peppers, green peppers jalapeno peppers, dehydrated onions, salt, sugar, dehydrated garlic, paprika.Servicing information: One serving (1 Cup) of "Campbell's Chunky Roadhouse Chili" contains 230 Calories, 8 grams of fat (including 3.5 grams of saturated fat), 30mg of Cholesterol, 870mg of Sodium, 25 grams of carbohydrates, 8 grams of dietary fiber, 11 grams of sugar, and 15 grams of protein.ConclusionThere is always plenty of Campbell's Chucky Soup in the pantry at my house.  It is by-and-large the only kind I buy and "Campbell's Chunky Roadhouse Chili" figures highly on my shopping list each week, even my wife likes it and she is a finicky eater.  Low in calories and fat, "Campbell's Chunky Roadhouse Chili" is a tasty alternative to burger and fries, and even a sandwich.  And most importantly if fills me up until my mid-afternoon snake.  Yes, the chili is a little higher in calories than other soups in the chunky line line-up, but hey a guy has to live a little; no worries.

If you want to be able to eat any other meals in the day, you should partake of this sparingly.

It has a slight kick, but nothing that most people won't be able to handle, and you can always get some chili powder at the grocery store if you want to crank it up a notch.Obviously don't expect an inexpensive can of chili to be anything mindblowing, but, for the price, you'll be hard pressed to find anything tastier.

It's not as good as Wolf's, and I won't be buying it again. However, I once had a can of Campbell's chili and beans that I liked very much. Could it be that it's another type that is not being sold by Amazon? That's possible, because I have sometimes rushed to Amazon to reorder something that I had bought in my local supermarket only to find that it wasn't here. So my search for the perfect chili  goes on. Wolf's, as I have mentioned, is pretty good, but it just lacks sufficient hotness, as does this type of Campbell's chili. I've tried to blend in chili powder, but that tends to make the beans too mushy. Sigh. Anyway, it will be no kind of ordeal to finish my remaining ten cans; in fact, I might eventually develop a real liking for the stuff, because it seems to be the kind of thing that grows on you. Anyone have an idea of how to make canned chili hotter without spoiling its consistency and texture?

I must admit that this one is very close to Bush's Homestyle Chili, (my fave) but it has been discontinued.  And you could get it in 2 sizes of glass jars, which I prefer.  That being said, I just had a can of this one and I'm in chili city.  I prefer my chili HOT, so in goes powdered habanero pepper.  The meat is lean and tender, the beans not mushy, and the sauce...killer!  But it DID need the pepper.  I usually don't put chili over rice, but my wife used to make a cold garden salad with most all the vegies in it.  Then pour a heated can of chili over it.  Don't knock it if you haven't tried it.  You get the greens WITH the gas.  I'm set to try all the other chili styles Campbell's makes (I've already ordered them from here) and hope they're equally as tasty.  If not, there are many food banks that are in desperate need of canned goods.  BTW, one writer mentioned the salt problem.  I found nothing like that with this style.  But I have had a similar experience with some other canned products.  Very seldom.  So I can empathize with the writer.  All that said, this is now my fave because I haven't received the other ones yet.

Not only is this Chili the most delicious canned chili I've ever had (speaking of the Campbell's Chunky brand in general), it's perfect for use in various quick and easy "recipes" since heating it up takes just moments versus the time involved in making homemade chili from scratch.  The Roadhouse isn't "hot" spicy, but it is very hearty and has a zing due to the great spices included.  If you add a little extra chili powder, you can adjust the flavor a bit (again) without the hassle of making chili from scratch when you only have a few minutes to begin with.

column9: Four Out Of Six Of My Cats Love It!
column10: I have six cats and am very picky about what I feed my cats. It doesn't help that I have to give one cat herbal supplements and another extra food since he gets run off from the food dish. It can be very challenging to say the least when the other three are just trying to snarf down everything they can get.I am adamant about a grain free diet but also have to find something that everyone will eat. This is hard because not everyone wants to eat the same thing. My oldest cat doesn't even like canned food. If he gets special treats, its sardines only so he was out when I tried this food. The other boy doesn't like the ground up texture of many canned foods. He only eats stuff that has really pieces of food and gravy. He turned his nose up and walked away. The other four all ran to the plate and cleaned it off every time I put it down. Four out of six cats ate it.The sad thing I find with this food is it talks about all the healthy veggies and fruits in it but from looking at it, the only vegetable I see are carrots. What does encourage me is a cat blog I follow, The Conscious Cat, recommends this as one of her top grain free foods to feed your cat. She is also very picky about what she feeds her cats, and I trust her word.Now, having said all of that, I feel that this is one of the better canned cat foods on the market. Personally, I wouldn't really buy much of it since I don't feed the four cats this that often, just often enough to distract them while I am trying to feed the one that got run off from the food dish. If you buy this, expect to pay a little less than forty dollars for 24 3-ounce cans (as of 10/4/12). That's a little steep for me, but I do feel that the food is worth it for your cats if you plan on feeding them a wet diet.Shawn Kovacich100% Cat LoverAuthor and Creator of numerous books and DVD's.

Wow, do my guys love this stuff. Usually when I try something out new they look at it, walk around the bowl & act like I just gave them a bowl of used kitty litter. Not here.
