Most highly recommended.

column9: Nutritious and Wholesome Cat Food for a Picky Older Cat
column10: I have been at my wit's end trying to find a good cat food for my 15 year old cat, Lily. She is finicky and even worse, has a delicate stomach condition. Not only do we get the usual hairballs, but I've had to clean up after her about three times a day.As a result, we're very careful in how we feed her. In terms of dry food, we've given her IAMS and Science Diet. After a brief honeymoon period, she wouldn't touch the stuff (Science was very expensive, so I learned my lesson there, pricey doesn't mean Lily will like it). In terms of wet foods, she likes Fancy Feast Classic but never manages to finish a can. There's always leftover meat in her bowl.Then I gave her Nature's Variety. The first time I served it, she lapped it up. In fact, she licked her bowl clean, not a speck of food left! I was also surprised to see tiny bits of an orange-colored vegetable in her food (carrot?). Since I'm a bit of a vegetarian myself, I highly approve of the 5% veggies that come in this type of canned food. I'm also glad that this grain-free food is a pate, which makes it perfect for older cats like Lily.She's been eating this non-stop for about two weeks now (still licking the bowl clean!) and so far so good(fingers crossed). Fancy Feast seemed to be the only type of food she liked, so I'm happy to be able to add this to the list.

column9: Healthier for my kitty, she's not terribly fond of it, but is adjusting (I think?)
column10: The ingredients are much healthier, IMHO, than most cat foods with filler grains, etc. It does have flaxseed oil, which is great for her coat (has linoleic acid in it) & the chicken should be a good source of arachidonic acid *both are reportedly necessary for cats, as they can't manufacture these themselves.) It's nice to see cat foods that are meat a cat would normally eat in the wild along with oils that help their coats shine & are good for their kidneys. I'm not sure what the ratios are, and these can be very important if you have an older cat with renal issues, hypertension, arthritis, and so on, so I'd dig deeper &/or talk you your vet if your kitty has any health issues.I think for cats, health-wise, it *seems* the duck is the healthiest in this brand to balance the EFAs for kitties (I'm NOT a vet & every car is different, so if in doubt, check with your vet. My cat will snag ice cream & even cotton candy if you let her, so taste prolly isn't the vest indicator... Also, if you cat is used to eating a food that isn't as healthy for them, once they get the junk out of their taste buds for a few weeks to a month, they tend to eat the healthier foods & will stop craving the junk... people are much the same way, so once the kitties or kiddy's are off the junk, then they'll tend to eat what is healthier for them!)The food has no coloring or artificial preservatives, so it might just be better for you than canned food for humans (Interesting that there is a Bill on the ballot in CA, perhaps nationally under different state laws? I dunno, I haven't received my booklet yet re: bills/initiatives & different states are likely to have different proposals, so READ CAREFULLY!It appears as though the food companies more likely to have "Genetically Engineered foods", & more "junk foods" are against it) that reportedly would require dog & cat foods to be labeled for coloring, genetic alteration, preservatives, etc., but a commercial sponsored by some food companies SAYS not on human foods??? Well... maybe we should vote yes on the bill to at least get some labeling laws started [IF it doesn't prohibit making human foods labeled in a later initiative, then just buy pet foods that are healthy enough for humans?) It sounds like some pet foods are already healthier for humans as it is now, so truth in labeling should be the #1 priority for ANY foods ANY of us AND our pets eat, especially with a lot of "syndromes", etc. popping up in the last 20-30 years & the probability that some genetically altered foods *MAY* make our pets, and thus us more susceptible to infections with parasites, viral infections, fungal infections and bacterial infections such as: protozoa, worms, malaria, West Nile virus & other diseases that are more difficult to detect in our pets AND in us!Some pet & human foods already label these things, so for those opposed to labeling truthfully, you have to wonder WHY they would NOT want us to know what we are feeding our animals OR us, as our pet's health can directly affect OUR health!I'm all for a boycott of ANY food company (pet or otherwise) that wants to keep what's in our pets, wildlife foods or our foods from us! That one susceptibility factor to a single one of millions of different infections could mean encephalitis, worms or maggots eating your liver, eye, intestines and most likely our skin, yet it only take one susceptibility to be passed from our pets to us to kill or harm our pets & jump the species barrier, survive cooking, used in cotton plants to make them (& any other plants that happen to get in the mix, cross-bread, etc. non-susceptible to even Round-up, so once the cat's out of the bag, if these cross species, or if these plants support, or take out ANY section of natural resistance to pathogens ("prion-free" may look great on one level, yet may support pathogens in other ways), then we'll have a massive crisis on our hands that could make pandemics of the past look like a single funeral... The fact is we don't know for sure & it's incredibly clear that not enough research has been done

Anyone owned by cats knows that they can be very finicky and might turn up their little noses at the best food while happily scarfing down food filled with nasty-sounding things like poultry digest.My two cats eat a popular, grocery-store-variety, canned cat food in the morning and have dry available to them the rest of the time. One of them will pretty much eat anything that doesn't move and probably would eat the stuff that does move if he were an outside kitty.  The other is old and scrawny and hard to feed.On the first morning, the kitties looked at this food a bit suspiciously and then started nibbling which turned into chowing down.  After that first try, they both ate it enthusiastically.  Fat kitty even makes "nom, nom, nom" noises while he is eating.I really like the ingredients in this food.  However, I was concerned about the inclusion of montmorillonite clay.  Do I really want to be feeding my kitties clay?  So I researched this edible clay a bit.  It is full of minerals that are good for kitties but is also used for very non-food purposes.  I'm no scientist, but after reading the information I could find, I've decided that I won't be alarmed by that ingredient in the food.  Because very high quality ingredients are higher on the list, I believe that the manufacturer includes it as a true benefit, not as a filler.  You'll have to make your own decision about that.And your kitties will make the decision about whether they will eat it or not.This stuff is definitely pricier per ounce than the bigger, mega-brand cans of food, but I think that the excellent ingredients justifies the difference.`

It's difficult to write a review for food that I have not personally eaten or been able to obtain a verbal response for from its intended consumer. I don't think my normally voracious cat loved this product though; she would often take a few bites, then walk away from it, then come back to it only when she became very hungry. Of course, this is only one case, and I have no explanation--the ingredients seem to be good and it didn't smell or look particularly offensive.

I like that this is a better product for my pets but really for the price of it I couldn't afford to buy this all the time. My cat isn't very picky usually and she ate this, we usually buy her the friskies prime filets, the vet said it is better to not change their diet and buy different types of food and flavors all the time so we normally stick with the chicken. I am glad this is a chicken formula since that is what she is used to. If it weren't so expensive I would buy it all the time but I do have to budget. I take good care of my animals but I have to watch the cost so that the humans can eat and pay bills. I am trying to get a baby kitten to start on solid foods and I am trying with this since it is quality and it is easier for him to try and eat than the filets.It is a good quality cat food but it loses one star for being more than I can afford to buy on a constant basis and the cans are very small so it would take more cans to feed a cat.

Our six cats vary in age from nine months to 17 years and finding food that suits all of them can be difficult.  Like most cats, they all like junk food -- grocery store canned food made of by-products and grains -- but not all of them can handle it, and frankly, we prefer they only eat junk food occasionally; just like us, they're healthier with a better diet. Over the last couple of years, we've switched our brood to 75% freshly cooked chicken/25% canned (grocery store) food. Along with that, they eat a premium kibble that provides nutrients  (Kirkland Premium, Costco's cat chow, which is priced similarly to grocery store brands even though it's the equivalent of brands like Felidae.)Nature's Variety Instinct Grain-Free chicken formula is excellent food, complete and balanced, and I wouldn't hesitate to replace the chicken breasts we prepare with this product.  The cats even react similarly to it: if they've recently had cheap canned food -- junk food -- two aren't as interested in it because it's not pumped full of lord-knows-what to enhance the flavor. Still, they eat it, but the other four, who prefer fresh chicken to junk food, practically inhale it.There are no digestive upsets with Instinct, and nothing in the litter pan that indicates intestinal trouble. That's never the case with the grocery store brands, even the priciest ones.  If I had only one cat, I would happily stop cooking up chicken breasts and rely on this food and the kibble, but the cost is a little steep.  (I'd love to see this food packed in the larger-sized short can at a better price per ounce.) As it is, I'm keeping a few cans around for treats, and when the budget is a little roomier, I plan on buying it by the case and cooking a lot less chicken.I'm really glad this food exists; I actually feel good about feeding it to our little pride of house lions.

October 23, 2012****This is quite possibly the single most perfectly delicious cat food Miss Flufferpants has ever tried.  She eats almost exclusively the dry kind of food, with the occasional ort "accidentally" dropped on the floor thrown in.  I've never seen her go so totally nuts over a cat food.  She almost literally inhales the entire three ounces in a frenzy of happitude that I swear make her virtually purr.  Miss Flufferpants has never been exactly what you would call a picky eater -- rotting squirrel and rabbit are not unknown to her palate -- so I'm not impressed that she ate Nature's Variety Instinct Grain-Free Canned Cat Food, Chicken Formula, 3 Ounce Cans (Pack of 24) at all, I'm impressed with the degree of vigor and seeming delight with which she ate it.The stuff is expensive, which is why I subtract a star, especially if you regard it as your pet's daily meals.  I use it only as a treat.That there are no grains according to the labels is surely precisely why it is so expensive per ounce.  Grains are cheap ingredients that bulk up volume and weight.  Turning grains into meat is expensive, which is why more experts nowadays are recommending eating more grains in the form of grains and less in the less healthful form of chickens and cows and pigs.Did I forget to mention that Miss Flufferpants is my 70-pound dog?  She is.  However, my cat, Bently Geene, likes the stuff too, just not as enthusiastically.****

column9: Nature's Variety Chicken Canned Cat Food
column10: My cats are primarily on dry food.  But I like to give them a treat once in awhile; just something different from the same old same old that they get everyday.  So once a week they get what I affectionately call their "kitty crack".  That is, a can of cat food split between the two of them.And it never fails, doesn't matter what brand or what flavor, they go wild for it.  This canned cat food was no different.  They both got excited as soon as they heard the lid open and the chorus of meows started.  The can was small, but I still split it between the two of them as they have dry food always accessible if they are still hungry.  They gobbled it down at a fairly rapid pace, even on the third week in a row of it.It didn't smell very good, I will say that.  Not that most wet foods do, but still, this one isn't pleasant and definitely doesn't smell like chicken to me.  But as long as they like it that's alright.  The ingredients are quite good.  It is grain free like advertised and made with real meat and veggies.  They have some vitamins thrown in too, but not enough that you can't tell what the heck is in the food.  And the list isn't overly long, which I appreciate as well.  It also seems very digestible.  My cats have sensitive stomachs and its taken a long time to find things they won't react with.  This food seems to be one of those things they can eat without leaving a present on the floor for me later or hearing that dreaded retching sound in the middle of the night.A good canned cat food.  I would buy it for the girls in the future.Review by M. Reynard 2012

column9: Picky cat liked the first time but then will not want to eat it now
column10: Everyone's cat has its own finickiness. Our female cat, Sammy, is the pickiest eater. She has to have a rotation of different wet foods or else she just stands there and demands more... Anyway, she loved this item the first time that she ate it. However, on the second time, she was not really interested and remains uninterested. Not sure why. I am sure that the ingredients and nutrients are better, but she won't touch this food. It is a good quality product and my dogs like the similar type of food from Nature's Variety.

column4: John L. Hoh Jr. "Author and Theologian"
column10: This was not a product I was going to review by personal experience. I mean, it may be nutritional and all, but cat food is designed to entice feline, not human, desires.That being said, I started giving this as a treat to my cats in the evening. It is an understatement to say they love it! They devoured it. It is a good ten minute period of time when they are engaged in eating this food.The flavor my cats tried was chicken. They were not chicken about enjoying the cat food and it did not put them in a fowl mood.I would definitely buy this again. My cats enjoyed every morsel!

column9: The filet mignon of cat food... seriously!
column10: If you look at the ingredients of this stuff, it's a little bit ridiculous how high-quality it is. Tons of protein and none of that crappy stuff most cat foods - soft and hard - have that make your cat fat and unhealthy.My two kittens love this stuff and they seem a lot more energetic and healthy since they started eating it. My only problem is that now they won't eat the cheaper stuff.Sigh.

One cat likes it, one cat doesn't.  In fairness, the one that doesn't like it is not a big fan of canned food in general and, well, we all know about cats and finickiness.The ingredients here are excellent, and if you couldn't read the label, your nose would tell you:  Instead of a cat-food stench, it smells like you popped the top on a can of chicken.While it is significantly more expensive than many brands, compare ingredients.  Cats are obligate carnivores who must have meat, and meat is more expensive than soy, grain, starches, and nebulous by-products.  Additionally, I checked the label of a well-known brand-name canned cat food and found titanium dioxide, which is essentially a white pigment (and currently classified as "possibly carcinogenic," i.e., cancer-causing) and caramel color.  Who's that for?  Pretty sure my cat doesn't care what color the food is.I would consider this a very high-quality food and a good choice.  The missing star represents the vote of the picky cat who won't eat it.

My two cats loved this food and ate it readily (mixed with their "Before Grains" dry food). For two cats, I gave about 1/3 - 1/2 can daily, and they eat the Nature's Variety Instinct canned food first - and with gusto! It also doesn't stink to high-heaven, which is reassuring.There aren't any fillers or grains and - since cats are obligate carnivores - is exactly how it should be. There's some vitamin fortification, but that isn't superfluous or unnecessary. Very high quality ingredients, without too much fat or vegetables. It's expensive food, for sure, but it's an investment in my cats' health: high quality diet means less propensity towards digestive problems or later-life health issues resultant from long-term grain/filler diets.

I recently received this for my friend, who has two cats. I thought that they would be able to enjoy something a little different; however, I didn't realize that my friend was so strict and regimented with her pets' food and didn't want them to eat something new. So with 24 cans of cat food, and no cats to feed it to, I donated it to the local animal rescue rather than let it go to waste. I know someone who works there, and it just happened that the day I brought the food in two stray cats had been brought into the shelter. Both cats were fed Nature's Variety, and both loved it. So far I haven't heard of any complaints regarding other cats rejecting the food, and from what I understand it's quite a healthy product for them as well.

Now that the old cat isn't around anymore the younger two only get wet food on special occasions like holidays or birthdays. I put a can of this out and even the reclusive one made an appearance from under the bed. There is generally a pecking order to who gets to eat first but this time both of them stuck their gobs deep into the food and had at. They did seem to fill up fast and left about a quarter of the bowl still there which I thought was odd because they usually lick the bowl clean. Maybe all the good for them ingrediants filled their tummys up faster than some of the other brands? I should note that my cats are on the smaller size at seven pounds and just shy of six pounds.

column9: Fantastic cat food - my picky cat loves it!
column10: I know there are arguments for and against but I feel dry food is a "space age" relic that was good for pet food companies, but not necessarily for pets.  Cats in particular require foods with a high moisture content that dry food lacks.  That doesn't leave canned pet food marketers in the clear either as your definition of acceptable ingredients probably does not include many of the ingredients the FDA and AAFCO considers safe.  (Google the list, it'll be worth it.)My cat normally gets a variety of Wellness and Blue Buffalo Wilderness canned foods.  These are generally considered premium foods but I'm always on the lookout for other ways to add variety to her diet.  What I like most about this food is they clearly state the food contains 95% meat.  That is a huge plus that no other pet food I am aware of matches.  I realize other pet foods will list a meat as the first ingredient, but if the second, third, and fourth ingredients are starches, grains, or vegetables you could end up with food that is less than 50% meat even if it's the first ingredient on the list.  Humans are omnivores, dogs are to some extent, but cats must have meat and bones to survive.So many advertised cat food brands contain mostly unhealthy high-carbohydrate ingredients like corn, wheat and so on as primary ingredients that it makes me mad.  You don't see your housecat in the garden pouncing on a wild ear of corn or a potato, do you?  These items should have never made their way into cat foods in the first place.  That is why I am very happy to see a pet food that actually lists a high percentage of meat content on the label.  As you can expect, it tends to be more expensive, almost twice as much as cheap brands.  Consider this, however.  When I opened my eyes to what I was really feeding my pet and switched, my cat ate half as much as the brand-name junk.  It seems once you start feeding your pet real digestible food, they don't need to eat as much of it.Of course the real critic of this food is my cat.  I am happy to report that not only does she like this food but my normally quiet and reserved cat will meow her desire if she catches a whiff of what's inside the can.  Since she rarely meows for anything, that's quite a compliment.  I will be purchasing more of this in the future.

All three of my cats enjoy this healthy cat food.  Obviously the flavor is good.It's great to see companies producing grain free cat food (what moron thought it was a good idea to poison cats with grains in the first place?)."Nature Variety Instinct Chicken Formula" claims to be 95% chicken, turkey and liver. There is no mention of "meat by-products".  The ingredients also include small amounts of eggs, peas, carrots, artichokes, cranberries, pumpkin, tomato, blueberries, broccoli, cabbage, kale and parsley.  I think my cats eat healthier than my son does!

As cat food goes, this is an excellent product. It is good for your cat and your cat will love it.The one problem is value. You get 24 3oz cans for over twice what you can get 24 5.5oz cans of other brands. If you have just one cat, it might be worth it, especially for the quality ingredients, but if you are feeding the entire neighborhood as it seems for me sometimes (they know I can't say no to a hungry kitty), you would be better off with 9Lives or Fancy Feast.

My two cats really enjoy this food and are doing well on it. They're as healthy as can be and changing to this food didn't bother their stomachs. The ingredients are all excellent, it's made in the USA and I feel good about feeding it to them. The only reason I gave it 4 instead of 5 stars is because they seem hungrier between meals than with the other premium grain-free wet food they were eating. I'm not sure why because the ingredients are so good, but that's the only negative comment I have. It might just be them adjusting to a new food. The 3 oz. cans are convenient because I find the 6 oz. cans tend to dry out a little before the cats go through them.A quick tip: If your cat doesn't like this food and is used to eating grocery store foods, wait until the cat is really hungry and then try feeding. It takes some time and patience. My cats snubbed their noses at any high-quality foods until they were almost 2 years old. They preferred the taste of the grocery store foods they were eating. Once they got used to the foods with high quality, natural, ingredients, they started to enjoy them.

I have to say my cat just loved this food.  She practically finished it all in one bite.  Not like she is starving or anything.  She even ignored her treats just to eat this stuff.  I thought maybe it was because it was new but she continues to gobble up each can the same way as the first one. I am very happy as she is finicky.

column4: Shana "That's my opinion- I could be wrong!"
column9: All 5 of my cats seem to really love it!
column10: These cans are each the same size can as a can of Fancy Feast. So one I split up several times a day for my 5 indoor house cats. Two of my male cats usually only eat canned cat food once in awhile, they usually stick close to dry food. Though, both of them have been eating this food everytime that I've fed it. The other 3 cats are females who are not too picky, though, there are a few foods they won't touch.The food itself has several impressive ingredients and it has a nice broth in every can. What I have also noticed is that this food doesn't have that "fishy" smell or that "sandy/gritty like" texture like so many of the other canned cat foods that are on the market. All the cats have cleaned up all of it each time I've fed it, and it doesn't often happen with all 5 of my cats.Usually, I feed my cats Friskies pates, Whiskas, Fancy Feast pates and 9 Lives pates. My cat's won't usually eat any shredded canned foods, they like the ground/pate styles.Recently, one of my female cats, Sissy developed an allergy to one of her previously enjoyed foods and her front bottom lip swelled up (sometimes called a rodent ulcer) and I think this might be a good alternative for her as she hasn't had a reaction to this food. This food is more expensive than some, but, it's not as expensive as the Science Diet Prescription or the Royal Canin prescription diets for hypo-allergenic (though this food doesn't claim to be hypo-allergenic).Also, my 20lb., very picky Phatboy Cuddlecuss cat will only eat certain wet foods and he absolutely loves this, usually he will only eat Whiskas chicken, but he loves this one.Overall, I'd definitely purchase this canned food for my cats. They really seem to love it so far.

Of four of my cats only two eat canned food regularly and one nibbles canned food when the mood strikes him.  My fourth cat never touches any canned food.  Therfore, the two that eat the canned food regularly liked this.  They immediately ate some and although they did not finish all the food, I can tell they liked it enough to eat it regularly. (PS It is not too unusual for me to find canned food left behind no matter what the variety.) Right now they've had it a couple of nights in a row. The one that periodically nibbles canned food did not touch it.What I like about this food is that it does not stink. Many canned foods smell up a house the minute they are opened, such as the Meow Mix, Surf 'N Turf Variety Pack, 2.75-Ounce Cups (Pack of 48). This one's smell is barely detectable to me.The label also indicates this food meets the cats nutritional needs.The first five ingredients are Chicken, Turkey, Chicken Broth, Chicken Liver, Ground Flaxseeds, etc. The peas, which are the 8th ingredient in the list, are noticeable but the last 8 ingredients in the mixture (artichokes, cranberries, pumpkin, tomato, blueberries, broccoli, cabbage, kale, parsley) were not visible. Perhaps they were blended in. There are also various vitamins and supplements in the mixture as well as the necessary taurine.Overall, my regular canned-food-eating cats liked this and I believe the ingredients are healthy enough for them.  I would consider purchasing this or another flavor for them if I wanted to introduce some diversity in their diet besides their usual Friskies Savory Shreds Cat Food Variety Pack, 8.25-Pound or other Friskies canned food they are use to.

column9: Smells great with nutrition and my 3 cats love it!
column10: What more can you ask for: a can that's easy to open, the food drops right into the dish, it smells good, is nutritionally complete without grain fillers, looks good and my three cats, who after all are the final critics of all cat food, absolutely love it. I will be buying this food from now on. My cats are all adults, one is 14 and two are five. They deserve to be treated well and cared for by us in the best way possible. They give us a great deal of pleasure and companionship.

When I open a can of Fr****ies or F**cy F**st cat food the smell is overwhelming -- I KNOW what kinds of ingredients go into that kind of canned cat food (best left unsaid), and I also know that my co-worker's cat ate nothing but Fancy Feast canned for 21 years. Even so, I am happier feeding my cats something that comes closer to what they would eat in the wild -- almost all protein, no fillers like Soy or Wheat or Corn.The major ingredients in Instinct Grain Free Chicken Formula are: Chicken, Turkey, Chicken Broth, Chicken Liver, Ground Flaxseed, Montmorillonite Clay, Eggs, Peas, Carrots, Lecithin, Vitamins (and fruits) -- REAL meat is first, then broth, then liver  -- good solid nutrition for Obligate carnivores -- which is what cats are.I also like what is stated on the Instinct Cat Food website - "Instinct foods are grain-free and gluten-free - perfect for satisfying your cat's carnivorous cravings and nutritional needs. Instinct is also highly digestible and nutritionally dense"One of my cats (17 yrs old, but still thinks she is a kitten) has a very sensitive stomach -- but there is nothing in this formula, not even the flaxseed and the montomorillonite clay --to upset her stomach -- the other cat (14) has thyroid and heart issues -- after eating this food, her fur is shining and she moves like a frisky kitten. I would prefer not to feed my cats something that I know has dead bodies of downers or chicken feet or beaks/feathers. I feel more comfortable spending a little more and feeding them something that is purer, cleaner and healthier for them -- Instinct is one such food. Instinct also markets raw and freeze-dried foods as well. I feel that Instinct has a committment to making the best possible nutrition available to cat owners.Tha being said. both of my cats have no problem enjoying their Instinct cat food meals. At first I mixed the Instinct half and half with what they had been formerly eating (it was good food, the best I could afford, but still with rice as a filler) -- in order to make the transition easier on their stomachs. Now they dig into their Instinct and lick their plates clean (and ask for more).I plan to continue giving them Instinct Cat Food. Budget permitting, I may even try the freeze dried nuggets as a treat for them. I deserve the best nutrition-- certainly my cats should not be short-changed in that regard either.

column9: Cat did not care for this.
column10: For over $28 (plus shipping) for 24 cans, you would think this cat food would be something special. Alas, upon opening the can and peering inside, it looked just like any other cat food. Smelled like it too. I plopped it into my cat's bowl and she ate it, a little. I had a feeling she wouldn't care for this. She loves Fancy Feast, and only then the grilled variety kind. She doesn't care for the standard mushy-looking food at all. Same case here. Now, perhaps this food is healthier than some(I guess), but none of that matters if your cat refuses to eat it. Cats are picky and eat only what they like. From what I could tell, my cat didn''t care for this, and I wasn't too impressed either. Like I said, for the price I expected something better-looking. Thankfully, I was able to test this product out free-of-charge or else I would never have paid for it. If your cat likes regular, mushy cat food, they may like this, but if your cat (like mine) usually prefers something more flaky or grilled in texture, I would say skip this.

column4: Juanita A. Floyd "Life is too short to read b...
column10: This cat food smells delicious. It seems to have a very good quality and dense consistency. The problem is my cats don't seem to like it. They lick the juice off and leave the rest.  Was really hoping they would go for it since it is made from much better ingredients than regular cat food.

column9: Cat ate this with less enthusiasm than other less expensive brands.
column10: Our kitty seems to be partial to the Friskies pink can: salmon and beef.  This brand, though more expensive, did not seem to generate the enthusiasm that she has for the Friskies. She actually walked away and left this sitting. Maybe this would have generated more active gulping in the cold winter months (she's an outdoor cat) or maybe her tastes are just more pedestrian?The catfood has a pleasant color, looks fresh and smells OK. It does generate a little of its own juice.Surprising that she wasn't more interested in this well touted chicken catfood. Who knows-maybe she just prefers fish???Who knows what lurks in the minds of kitties........

When I first bought the antler the picture was shown with a box of antlers, therefore I mistakenly thought I would get at least a few but received only one.  That's my fault for not reading the description more carefully.  The antler I got was just under 6 inches.  For a "large" I thought it would be at least 8?  So for $17 I'm feeling a little jipped.  The only redeeming part is that my dog does love to chew on this.
Can find the 7 oz bottle online at many other retailers for about 1/2 the cost of this.  I would search elsewhere for this treat.  My dog loves them, but not at this price.

Our two dogs enjoy these treats quite a bit and certainly look forward to eating them. I like the small size of the treats and the recipe formula that uses chicken as the first ingredient. On the not so plus side, corn syrup is the second ingredient and also included in the mix is the wonderful, often used animal digest.Luckily our dogs can't read. They just like getting their soft, chewy treats.
These have been a fantastic tool for training my dogs.  I've been looking for something that would keep their attention and this has been a great way!
Was suprised to see this was the smaller bottle not the 7oz I am used to buying at the pet stores.  Seems like a lot of money.  Check out the cost of the 7oz before buying.

This is a delightful cookie with a great taste and low saturated fat.  Anyone with a sugar-restricted diet would enjoy this and other Murray Sugar-Free cookies (especially the chocolate creme's).  These only have around 3 grams of carbohydrates a piece!!

I have yet to try this product personally, because it is not currently available at our supermarket. But my mother,  soon will be 94, mildly diabetic and a long-time customer for sugar-free products, says they are the best! For some reason our store carries the other Murray varieties, but not this one any more, maybe because there are so many kinds. Mother picks out her own groceries, and was in the habit of buying these about every other week. She bought two other Murray's packages this week, but really wanted the peanut butter. That's why I went searching the internet for them. After I receive them, (12 boxes!) I probably will keep at least one box to try for myself. (It would be nice to be able to buy an assortment from Amazon rather than so many of one variety--that would be a lot for a 94-year-old woman to eat, even if they are that good!)

column9: No Health Benefits and Grossly Overpriced....Read the Nutrition Facts
column10: My wife just brought home a $3 package containing 5.5 oz of Murray Sugar Free Pecan Shortbread cookies, thinking the high price was justified on a health basis. It isn't. Read the Nutrition Facts (per 3 cookies): 160 Calories, 11 Grams of Fat, 3 Grams of Saturated Fat, 18 Grams of Carbohydrate....the same, or worse, than most cookies containing sugar. These cookies may be "sugar free", but the implied health benefit is completely imaginary. Furthermore, at over 50 cents per ounce they are the most expensive packaged grocery cookies you can buy, which is completely unjustified by ingredient cost, and flavor, which is adequate but not exceptional.It's an unfortunate fact that some companies prey upon consumers who seek or need "special" products by forcing them to pay huge premiums for the product. Using Murray's formula, a can of Diet Coke should cost at least $3....but it doesn't, simply because production costs do not justify the premium and the market will not tolerate such an unconscionable mark-up. Neither should you. Don't let your health or dietary concerns override your common sense and lead you to pay preposterously inflated prices for "special" products that, upon close inspection, provide no legitimate benefit.

I was looking for something sweet that I as a diabetic and my husband and son could all share. Usually if it says sugar free then it means it has a chemical taste. But not these cookies they taste just like the regular cookies. I highly recommend them. You do not have to be a diabetic to eat them. They are made with splenda and I use splenda in a lot of things, I also use the brown sugar splenda in my cooking. These cookies are great.

column9: Yummy~My treat instead of High Sugar Cookies.
column10: First I will make note this page says sweetened with sorbitol, they are not. They are sweetened with Splenda.I think they taste as good as any other basic vanilla creme cookie. I like a bite of sweet at night but sugar keeps me awake so these fit the bill. The special that was going on when I got them made it a great deal. They cost up to $3.99 a pack where I live.....so this is a SWEET deal.They still have calories so you cannot eat the whole bag but they don't spike your sugar. Three cookies are 130 calories and 6 gms of fat. They are very sweet anymore and you may feel sick.
These shortbread cookies are little drops of heaven.  Have you ever noticed that smaller food seems to taste better?  One pouch is one carb and very satisfying.  No meaasuring is always good too.

I purchased these for my husband as he was recently diagnosed as diabetic.  I eat them as much as he does!  There is no strange after-taste as with some sugar-substitute enhanced foods.  We highly recommend.

column9: The best gingernaps, the best sugarfree cookies.
column10: I love these cookies, wish I could find them, I buy lots every time I find them.....but I do eat them. Help! I need more!

Love these cookies! When I learned a couple of years ago that I was heading toward diabetes and needed to cut out as much sugar as I could I knew I needed a "sweet" substitute.  I tried various products and found Murray Sugar Free cookies. I like oatmeal cookies anyway so gravitated toward their cookie. I promise I couldn't tell they didn't have sugar in them. I'm so addicted to them that I even carry them when I travel (wonder what the suitcase inspectors think?!) My grandkids even recognize MY cookies and now ask for them over the sugar-loaded kind. Trouble is, I can never find them. I don't know if they're just very popular or the wholesaler doesn't bring enough. It could be that I buyt 4 to 6 packages every time I DO find them. Murray says I can find them at Wal-Mart but never have although they do have the other flavors. Now I look to Amazon and they don't have them either! I have a hint of how drunks feel when they can't get their liquor! Please, Amazon, hurry and get a supply before I run out!

When I was diagnosed with type-II diabetes about two years ago, it felt like a death blow. I mean, I love sweets. And my favorite were peanut butter cookies (my wife also made a mean peanut butter cheesecake that I still crave to this day but am able to hold off thanks to these Murray Sugar Free Cookies). I'd tried other sugar free items but they all had a seriously bad after-taste to them. The artificial sweetners were pretty bad.But the Murray brand are pretty darned good. And I can eat about 6 of them that equal 32 carbs (I'm a tall guy --- 6 feet, three inches --- with a big frame). There's no horrible after-taste and the peanut butter flavor is just enough to satisfy my slavering pallete.If you're looking for a quality cookie that won't shoot your blood sugar up into the statosphere, these are a great option.

column9: Fab, as long as you understand what's in them!
column10: My fiance & I are following a reduced carbohydrate eating plan.  Given that these are sugar free, they are great for when you need something sweet, but with a slighter glycemic impact than regular cookies.They taste almost like Girl Scout Thin Mint patty cookies!  They are NOT, however, low in calories, or free from ingredients that some may feel are "unhealthy".Since people's ideas vary greatly as to what is bad for them & what is okay, there is some understandable controversy.  In my opinion, most of America is over weight because they don't know HOW to eat, but that's just my take on things.  Everything is conflicting.  Low carbohydrate foods are higher in calories & vice verse.  I have an extreme digestive sensitivity to Malitol (Maltitol), which is a sweetener used in most sugar free chocolate items.  While these cookies don't contain Malitol (Maltitol),there are very few items available that are without it.Bottom Line: They taste great!  My suggestion would be to check the ingredient list & nutritional information each & every time you purchase, I recommend purchasing in a grocery store, rather than online.

The cookies have an excellent taste and texture. I took them to a friend's house and they had no idea the were sugar free until I told them. I snack on them at work and willl be trying other varieties by Murray.

For people avoiding sugar, Murray Sugar Free Cookies Oatmeal, are good enough! This whole thing about sugar free products got me intrigued and confused at the same time. Some products that advertised as being sugar free have a lot of other sources of sugar, like alcohol, that are high. The feeling I get with Murray's is that they are reliable in their claims. I see them in all sorts of reputable publications and that gives me encouragement regarding their advertisement. As to the taste I can say they are pretty good tasting. Have tried their other ones and this one and the chocolate are the ones I favor. Who am I? Hungry hungry all the time for sweets but I realize not all sugar free items are created equal. For now a decent 4 stars rating!

I ordered these cookies for my husband as he's diabetic and loves peanut butter treats, so it was no surprise that he really liked them.  What was surprising, however, was that I liked them, too!  As a rule, I do not like peanut butter anything, and can barely stand the smell of it.  But these cookies aren't your typical peanut butter cookie.  They are pleasantly fragrant, delicately buttery and crisp (no mealiness like most others), with good-sized pieces of peanuts mixed in. Just delicious!
theses cookies are good , oatmeal seems to be my favorite and best of all you would never know they were sugar free if the label didnt say it. i will purchase this product again ,they're that good!

column9: Do NOT taste like sugar free cookies.
column10: Good stuff. I despise the taste of processed sweetners and I was hesitant about what they would taste like, but I was not disappointed. They are very good. Highly recommended.
These oatmeal cookies have a great spice taste -- pronounced yet not at all harsh.  Light and crisp, and they also keep well.

column9: Good Crunchy Oatmeal Cookies. I prefer soft chewy...
column10: Good cookies. They're made with Splenda. I guess that makes them sugarfree. They certainly don't taste like they are. I despise the taste of fake sweetners, but the folks at this company did a great job. The cookies are very yummy! I only gave it four stars, because I prefer soft  and chewy oatmeal cookies.
These cookies are not only good tasting but helps me stay on tract with my diet.  It is a little expensive but, I have lost 40lbs. I like the convenience.  You can get them at "Wal-Mart" sometimes.

These are not soft shortbread cookies but Krunchy with a hint of butter. Great for t2 diabetics but, as you know, anything we eat moderation is key. Although pricey buying a case [12] is a lot cheaper than buying single packs retail at your local grocer.
These cookies are awesome.  Great for dieters and those cutting out sugar.  So good!  You won't miss your old Oreos at all.

My wife is diabetic.  On a recent ospital stay, she was served these cookies on her tray.  She brought an extra two pack home and I enjoyed them.  We went online to Murray website and ordered a box.  We are very happy with the product.  One thing ... separation of the two cookies happens sometimes....doesn't get in the way of these tasty treats!

I ordered a case of 12 packages and only three cookies were broken. They taste delicious and eight cookies are only 130 calories. Plus, overall, it was less expensive than purchasing them in a store (and that's not even taking into account gas for your vehicle).

column9: Fantastic solution for a diabetic and weight watcher with a sweet tooth!
column10: I LOVE these cookies!  As a Type 1 diabetic and a Weight Watcher I still have a strong craving for sweets and chocolate in particular!  This cookie packet solves it all for me!  They give me the great taste of sweet chocolate without the guilt of blowing my diabetic or my weight loss diets!  And I feel like I get so many of them since they're small!  I also love the fact that they're portioned out for me.I can't say enough about these cookies and cannot wait until they're available on the shelves again!  Please hurry, Murray! :)

My favorite uncle is diabetic, and I always feel awful when I invite him for my birthday and he can't join in on eating cake with the rest of us. I picked up a package of these and used them for a cookie crust on a cream pie with Jell-O Sugar-Free Instant Pudding & Pie Filling, Chocolate, 1.4-Ounce Boxes (Pack of 24) and whipped cream lightly sweetened with non-sugar sweetener. The result was gorgeous and tasted pretty good even to those of us who can have sugar. For him? He told me "You know I can't have sugar." and when I told him it was sugar free he dug in with gusto. He said "It's not even my birthday and I feel like I got the best present."It was so easy to make, and the crust was his favorite part. I gave him an extra package of cookies I bought and he enjoyed those a lot too.Love these for making it so much easier to make special treats for my uncle.

column9: Great taste for a sugar-free cookie
column10: Bought these for my mother online because she can no longer find this particular Murray cookie at the local stores. She likes these and the shortbread cookies. They have a nice flavor for sugar-free and I recommend them to anyone on a low sugar diet.

I could EASILY gain 15-20lbs from Halloween until New Years Day so this year my husband and I decided to try not to go overboard on all the cookies/candy that is so available.I bought these cookies thinking they would be a poor substitute but SURPRISE, they really do have a huge chocolately taste and while they won't take the place of home-made fudge or gourmet chocolates, they are still satisfying.They are tiny, not much bigger than a life saver really and come in 80 calorie packages so I don't have to worry about portion control. Also, it can be hard to get enough fiber in your diet every day so I like the fact that these have 3 grams of fiber per package. My husband is a type II diabetic and these do have 16 grams of carbs but because of the fiber, they don't spike his blood sugar.The only downside to these is they do have 3g sugar alcohol which can cause some people stomach upset.I'm still probably going to have goodies this holiday season but with these cookies in my pantry, I know I won't indulge as often.
My hubby loves these cookies.  He would eat the entire shipment in one week if I would let him.  :-)
Hard to find a better crispy sugar-free cookie and, believe me, I've looked.  Good price, good storage.

I can't have sugar, so was very pleased to find these great tasting cookies. Friends I have shared them with were surprised to learn they were sugar free. Being able to get them from Amazon is a plus, since distribution in my local stores is spotty.
These little chocolate bites give you the pleasing sensation of chocolate - without the guilt of the sugar calories!!  Great job Murray!!

Murray's Sugar Free Peanut Butter cookies are one of my favorites andare as good as any peanut butter cookies that are not sugar free. I keepa supply on hand and my some of my friends have started buying them eventhough they don't need to have sugar free products.  All Murray cookiesthat I have bought have been very good. I'm a many times repeat customer.

I have tried several types of Murray sugar free cookies and can say that they have all been good and the "Fudge Dipped Mint Cookies" are no exception. These are not quite as good as regular cookies but, being diabetic friendly, are a good alternative.Recommended!

column9: Good Tasting Sugar Free Cookies - Recommended
column10: Murray "Sugar Free Fudge Dipped Vanilla Wafer Cookies" are a good tasting, diabetic friendly, snack food.While not quite a good as regular fudge dipped wafers, having a slightly odd after taste, these are quite acceptable.Recommended!
Love these cookies, and in quanity, and free shipping, makes it cheaper than the grocery store!
Package arrived on time; however some of the packs were ripped.  Other than that it was satisfactory.

column9: Yummy Cookies. Taste just like OR*EOs
column10: Great stuff. Didn't expect them to taste as good as they do. I bought four different kinds of Murray cookies and these are definitely top of the list (2nd on the list are the Oatmeal). Do not hesitate to purchase. You will not be disappointed unless you have a finicky palate. ENJOY!
These cookies really satisfy my sweet tooth for chocolate chip cookies. Very tasty and doesn't make me feel so sugar deprived.

column9: A shout-out to those of us who want to maintain a healthy weight!
column10: Due partially to the use of Splenda, Murrays makes the best-tasting sugar free cookies out there.  But don't forget they still have carbs! Chocolate chip is my personal favorite.
The Murray's pecan shortbread sugar-free cookies are my favorite of sugar-free cookies.  The grocery stores that I frequent didnt seem  to stock these cookies.  The product is excellent.

So here I am thinking I'm getting a great tasting cookie with Splenda only to find out they use Hydrogenated Oils.  On top of that they use the worst kind of oil, Palm and Palm Kernel.Don't be fooled into thinking you are getting something Heather because it has no sugar.  I would rather eat a tablespoon of sugar then these cookies.I totally feel this is a misrepresentation!  Shame.

Sugar free bites are a great way to satisfy the sweet desire in all of us...but without unnecessary and unhealthy sugars and fats. The 80-calorie packs are perfect to throw in the snack drawer at work. Now, if Murray would only put some of its other non-chocolate choices into these packs, it would be great! (Sigh...yes, I love chocolate, but I'm a migraineur and chocolate is only a rare treat for me since it is a key migraine headache trigger...)
Murray's Sugar Free Pecan Shortbread Cookies are my favorite cookies. They're delicious and perfect for someone who has to watch their blood sugar levels.
always like this cookies i used to get then from kellogs store but they closed up and sent me a letter telling me i could get from amazon  glad they did

column9: I can see why there sooo good!
column10: Worth the price and trouble of buying them. Even if your not diabetic they will help you take sugar out of your diet.  These are by far NO regular diet cookies. There simply to good to pass up.  Get some.  I recommend it.
This is the best tasting sugar free shortbread cookie ever. Doesn't even taste sugar free.
These cookies are great for a diabetic.  4 cookies only have 10 carbs and they satisfy you desire for something sweet. They taste just like regular shortbread cookies.

column9: Best Sugar Free Cookie~You get 8 as a serving :)
column10: It is hard to believe these are sugar free. They are so good. They are buttery and rich tasting and a serving is 8 cookies of 130 calories. That is so filling and yet still keeps you on whatever plan you are following.I have tried many of the flavors of these cookies and not found one to be bad or have an aftertaste. This one is my all time favorite. You will not be disappointed. In my town they are usually $3.99 a pack so this is a fantastic deal.They come with a long expiration date also.

I've really enjoyed these cookies, and came to Amazon as this one is hard to find. Much to my SHOCK the price is 60+ dollars.. and it shows they used to be 30.00 and some change? Huh?? Other cookies by Murray are more reasonable. No way will I buy them at this incredible markup :-P

Not sure how I feel about the product, Murray Sugar Free Cookies. My disappointment is with Amazon for sending EXPIRED COOKIES. After notifying Amazon I received an apology email and a new delivery was sent to recipent. I was shocked to receive a second call from the recepient that the 2nd delivery was also EXPIRED having the same expiration date as the first delivery. Next thing I know I receive an email from Amazon my money is being refunded. Have no idea what happened. I was embarrassed and disappointed the first time. Imagine my embarrassment the second time. The recepient is a diabetic and loves Murray Sugar Free Cookies but she is only able to find Shortbread in our stores and Peanut Butter is her favorite.
Short & sweet.  These chocolate delights are hard to find in many areas. I found them on Amazon & bought a case & will surely buy more. Just the thing for that "Chocolate Fix".
All of Murray's Sugar Free Cookies are excellent, but my favorite is the Pecan Shortbread.  Delicious!

Have a family member that is diabetic, so I always keep some of these on hand for when we get together and standard sweets are not an option.  Very tasty.  They used Splenda, so that will be a pro or con to you, depending on if you like it.I am very thankful for these cookies for helping to provide a bit or normalcy for this family member.  Just like normal cookies, but sugar-free.  Several great varieties.  Worth a try if you are looking for a sugar-free cookie.

This definitely satisfies you when you need a little something sweet. I find I don't even have to eat too much of me to be satisfied. The taste is great and best of all it doesn't cause upset stomach like many other sugar-free products do.

column4: Bartok Kinski "A casual stroll through the lu...
column10: While I was in a coma I ate these for desert.  They are very good tasting, don't have any "Sugary muck" taste, just plain, but really filling and don't give me gas.I like them with iced tea or pelican juice.Since there's no Sugar in them you can leave them out in the sun without getting a diabetic seizure.  Ants don't like them for some reason.

column9: Murray Sugar Free Cookies Chocolate Chip with Pecan
column10: The last 2 cases of Murray Sugar Free Cookies Chocolate Chip with Pecan were over cooked almost burnt.. Date Code is MAR0810EAS.  I don't have the code in front me  But I remember MAR0810Exx?Murray Sugar Free Cookies Chocolate Chip with Pecan, 5.5-Ounce Packages (Pack of 12)

column9: You won't believe the taste right "outta the container"
column10: St. Dalfour is the best-kept secret on the gourmet diet market! Take it to work; pop open the can (no refrigeration required) and eat without heating in the microwave. You can heat if you wish, but the taste is to die for sans heat.Yes, this is imported from France where they really know about food. Contains vegetables and sea-caught salmon with no preservatives or additives--totally healthy! They do have a website with more variety, but as you probably know by now, the prices at Amazon can't be beat!

I bought these little meals (or snacks, if you have a bigger appetite) on Amazon and just had to buy more. They are really seasoned just perfectly. I don't add the honey, which comes in a packet - that honey must be a 'French' thing.If you normally get the tuna salad with crackers that is sold in the supermarket and handy for lunch or snacks, you'll love this. It is flavorful, a good alternative when you just get tired of tuna.I wish I could buy larger quantities of this stuff on Amazon.

We've grown to absolutely love La Preferida Mexican Homestyle Beans.  We have them every time we make fajitas at home.  I've even added them to chili.  There's just something about the combination of ingredients that creates a very flavorful dish.  And these are whole beans in a tasty sauce, not the smashed paste that all other brands seem to offer.  Alas, these La Preferida beans are no longer available in my neighborhood - and I'm not gonna eat that bean paste everyone else sells.  I was very pleased to find these available on Amazon.  Bought two cases, received in two different shipments.  First shipment was fine.  The second shipment not so fine - every can was dented.  So far so good, though.

column9: Best No Bean Chili for Hot Dogs!
column10: I discovered this product one day at the market and decided to try it.  It was so good that I stopped buying Hormel's no bean chili for my hot dogs.  It has a touch of sweetness and a little heat.  Since I'm from New Orleans, I had additional cayenne pepper and chili powder.  It has a good texture and taste!  I would definitely recommend this product.  Out of all of the canned hot dog chili's, I rate this one as the best.

column9: Great Chili - No Bean, No Corn
column10: This is a very good, no bean chili.  It is one of the few that has no corn: bits, starch, or meal.  The nutritional info per label is contained in the Nutritional Facts section.
The can says "Chunky" but I can't find any chunks. This has an odd consistency. It's like watery spaghetti sauce. It's also not very spicy at all. I'm not impressed.

column9: Best No Bean Chili in a Can!
column10: I stumbled across this Chili and glad I did. Great with Ball Park Deli Style dogs that just came out.
It has a good texture and flavor. A little sweet but not bad. Could have a little more heat. I would buy it again.

I considered buying this product but didn't because there was no nutritional informtion provided.When will manufacturer's learn that the majority of food buyers want to know calories, sodium content, etc. BEFORE they buy.  As soon I know this information is NOT available, I assume the product info isn't good.
After the second time around, my tree survived the cold Colorado nite weather and it looks great. They were nice enough to even plant it in a very pretty planter.

column9: More uses than you would think.
column10: These Anchos are fantastic. Ancho is actually ripe smoked and dried poblano peppers.Similar to how a chipolte is smoked and dried red jalapeno.These chiles have a mild to medium heat with a sweet fruity flavor with hints of cherry,fig, and mild tabasco peppers. It's a favorite in Mexican cooking, and especially in mole,but it has a wide range of uses from sauces to salsas and even steak and barbecue sauce.This stuff is also a critical ingredient in the best enchilada sauces.These Badia peppers are properly sun-dried and not the variety of oven dried peppers morecommonly found that makes the peppers somewhat bitter. You can use these right out of thebag by crushing or grinding, or you could toast them in oil to really bring out their flavor.Most people just reconstitute them in water and puree them for sauces. At any rate, this isone of the most useful and flavorful ingredients for a variety of dishes than you are likelyto find anywhere. 5 Pods

column9: Love my CBTL coffies and machine
column10: I would have given this a 5 star rating, but the coffee is lacking a bit of coffee flavor and body. But its a nice departure. I truly love my machine and all the flavors  of coffees I ordered. The prices are the best.

Cooked up nice... firm texture with beans retaining their shape (no splitting, no mushing); used a bit of bacon fat, fresh pot herbs, and canned chicken broth for the pot liquor.  The color was pleasing to the eye; a pinkish-kidney bean hue.  I used them in a chili with roasted sirloin tip and fresh peppers.  I rinsed them and soaked them overnight; they were remarkably clean and without blemish or "floaters."  More than what I typically spend for a humble legume but I'd buy them again.  Am well pleased with my selection.

A package of Gourmet Valley Heirloom Beans Red Calypso Beans were purchased at the very tony Ferry Plaza in San Francisco in January.  For something like ten dollars.  We attempted to cook them over the weekend, but after 17 hours with the beans, which had been pre-soaked overnight, still quite hard, we pitched them, knowing they would be a joke forever.  We realize now that they are called Heirloom Beans because they are from some long ago harvest.  Perhaps during the Great Depression, when beans were carefully stored.  Caution:  Stay far away from even thinking about purchasing these beans!

First got to taste this wonderful chai product @ the Vegefest and fell in love with it.  The nutty and creamy flavor works very well with the taste of chai.  I tried to find it @ Central Market but got an empty shelf, glad that I can order via Amazon.  For those are tired of Starbucks Chai latte or the liquid Chai product, give this a shot, hopes you like it.
I purchased Packets and 2.2 lb Pouch the tea is light to me. For strong flavor need to ad extra. The quality of the product seems to be alright.
My daughter loves many of the Sprout meals but this one she absolutely loathed. Simply no taste! I'm not surprised she fussed each time I tried to give her a bite. Thumbs down to this one.
My daughter refused to eat this. The food was very in appealing and tasteless. I ended up wasting $4.00. I won't be trying again

Our son has been enjoying these meals since he was 7-8 months old and still does at nearly 10 months old. We love that they are organic, easy and quick to warm and great for quick meals or on the go while traveling.  The variety is good and we tend to mix in other cooked veggies, oatmeal or whatever is on hand to enhance the nutrition and texture. I know these are for toddlers, but they work great for younger babies who are ready for more textured meals also (the texture of these meals is quite mushy/easy to gum).

column9: This Is What Gives Grits A Bad Rap...
column10: I was hoping I found a source for "real" grits.  I was tipped off that this wasn't the real deal when the label said something about "mush".  It fits the definition of mush i.e. soft or soggy mass.I have been searching for real grits since my supplier retired.  He refurbished an old grist mill as a hobby then decided to use the plentiful local corn to mill grits.  They were fabulous, the real kind that you had to add water, let the hulls float to the top, pour off the water, add more water, then cook for 45 minutes.  Lots of butter, salt, and pepper and there's nothing better.

Vegan. Natural. Big beautiful butter beans. Nice texture and flavor. Great for pasta with your favorite tomato veggie sauce. Butter beans also make a great topping on vegan (cheese-less) pizzas. I like them as a combo with spinach for pizza. Can also be used to make hearty butter bean burritos with salsa. Approx 627 calories and 45g protein per 14.28 oz/400g can. Case of 24 cans. Made with butter beans, water, salt. Product of Italy. This review is out there for those for whom this makes a difference. See all of my reviews and the vegancompassion Profile for more great choices. Check out "Vegan Grocery Favorites" and "Vegan Grocery Top Ten" & all the other helpful "Vegan Grocery" Listmania. Your input counts and will be greatly appreciated to benefit the search of others. Thank you.
REALLY LIKE THESE BEANS. LOTS OF PLUMP PRODUCT IN EACH CAN. HEALTHY BUTTER BEANS WITH NO ADDITIVES OR EXREME SALT. PERFECT AS A SIDE VEGETABLE OR IN SOUPS/STEWS. WILL BUY AGAIN IN THE FUTURE.

The beans are special, couldn't find the same type of bean domestically,the taste is good. Unfortunately many of the cans are crushed in the shipping, and I guess the the crushed cans were crushed in transit from Italy, rather than the cans from Amazon to us.The result of crushed cans is that the skin of the beans in the cans are separated from the bean. This is cosmetic, but if the beans are served just heated, it looks terrible. The importer needs to do a better job on packing and shipping to the states.

These beans are wonderful! Perfect texture,great taste, major nutrition. Good hot or cold. Mix with some salsa for a quick snack. Marinate & use on salad. I am expecting that once soup weather arrives, they will make an incredible soup. I've told several people about these already & recommend them highly. I WILL be ordering more of these!

column9: Very pleased--24 cans, a good deal
column10: From Italy, low sodium (the entire can has about 250 grams of sodium). They are plump and tasty, great to mix with rice, to add to soups and chili, etc.,  or to just eat plain. The flavor is very mild, similar to cannellini beans.  Not like lima beans (don't like those). Unlike someone else's complaint, the cans were not dented when I got them.  All arrived in good condition.  Great deal, saved even more $$$ by using Subscribe and Save.

I am currently overseas so just finding people who ship here can sometimes be a task. I purchased this through "Choo Choo R Snacks" and the item arrived very fast - in less than a week. They also shipped the item in a very sturdy box so everything was in good shape when it arrived.The jerky comes in a re-usable cooler of decent construction. The jerky is great and completely what I expected after previously having it on several occasions in the US.Everything is what I expected which gives it a solid four stars, what set it apart in my book is the multiple free samples that I received along with what I ordered. A beach ball also came as a freebie!Five Stars.
i have been using this cereal for my son ever since he was a year old. i love the taste to it and so does he. he asks for it every mourning, and u can make some for urself as well its delicious.
This sauce is wonderfully versatile.  We have marinated meat with it and have used for basting.  It does not have an overpowering flavor so the grilled meat or fish is enhanced.
Hey there is my favorite chewing gum.Got a great flavor,just luv that taste, yummy!!!.Hard to get in oz,but i can buy them online.

The quality of this gum has taken a major dive. It used to be more substantial, and it had a very prominent cinnamon flavor, which outlasted one's ability to keep chewing. It used to be great. Now, the flavor is almost straight sugar, and the taste is gone in a very SHORT time. I would much rather see a legit price hike due to inflation than a sharp decline in quality!

Yes, ALL Wrigley's Gums, even the ones with SUGAR, now contain at least ONE, (and many contain two or all of them) ASPARTAME, ACESULFAME-K, SUCRALOSE!WHY a gum with Sugar needs these dangerous chemical sweeteners is a mystery to me, but since they changed the logo of the packages on their gum, you can no longer buy any Wrigley's (or most other brands too) gum without one or more of these nasty chemical additives.Also note that Sucralose (AKA brand name Splenda) is NOT the same thing as Sucrose! (Sugar)  The slight spelling difference is to decieve those that read ingredient labels to think they are reading Sucrose and not notice it is Sucralose.Sucralose causes severe abdominal pain, so if you have had that after chewing gum, now you know why.Aspartame has dozens of books and thousands of websites explaining what is wrong with that, as well as the other one.Very sad that I never again will get to enjoy my childhood favorites of Wrigley's Spearmint, Juicy Fruit or Big Red ever again.
I love this gum! I got it right away after ordering it. I will most definitely be ordering from this company again very soon
When these arrived they were the 4" pops NOT the 5" like advertised. There is a huge difference in appearance between the 4" and the 5".

I first tasted Bull Dog over 20 years ago, at a Japanese restaurant in Northern NH....I tried it on Kushi-Katu (a chicken appetizer) and on my fried rice. Wasn't all that crazy about it in the beginning, but that soon changed. It's wonderful as a marinade on chicken, beef or pork. I've also used some in my meatloaf, and I'll bet it'd be quite tasty on grilled burgers.Love the opportunity to buy this in quantity. The only place we can find it is up in northern NH & it's a long ride for Bull Dog. Makes our lives much better to be able to buy this through Amazon, that's for sure!If you haven't tried it, go for it! Enjoy!
My wife is Japanese so she introduces me to this kind of food. Excelent sauce for fried meats, specially Milanese style pork, meet or chicken.Usually with burguers is a good tasting sauce too,

I really like this pasta, but if soft and starchy bother you, this may not be the right kind for you.  My son is aware of any texture changes, and coming from whole wheat pasta, there is definitely a difference.I only gave it four stars b/c the cooking time on the box is off.  If cooked according to the package, the noodles are crunchy.  They also have a tendancy to over boil, and this is with the heat turned down after initial boil.  So don't leave them unattended! :)

I cannot begin to state how excited I am to find this available from Amazon.com. Carnation Chocolate Malted Milk has been a favorite of my Mother Velia all my life, and therefore it was expected on the breakfast table. I'm 35 now with my own family and I have an incredibly hard time finding the chocolate version in particular. To be able to order this "comfort food" and have it shipped means a great deal. Highly recommended to anyone who enjoys chocolate milk!!

This product in chocolate is extremely hard to find.  A local grocer used to carry it and every time I bought it someone mentioned how much they loved it.  This is the best tasting chocolate malt product in the world!  Thanks to Amazon.com, it is now easily available!

column9: The best chocolate milk, bar none
column10: Better than milk with Trader Joe's Midnight Moo syrup.Better than Hershey's syrup.Way better than Quik.WAY better than Ovaltine, which should be drunk only by starving children in third-world countries and by people who like Vegemite.This is the real deal.  I have been drinking chocolate malt for over 40 years. First Horlicks, then when they stopped making it, the Carnation here.  It's hard to find in stores, and we had been ordering in flats of 12.  I am thrilled to find it in 3-packs on Amazon, and with FREE PRIME SHIPPING!Great with plain skim milk, and if you add a little vanilla ice cream, it's SINFULLY good.First-timers may want to note that this powder dissolves easily in milk, just stirring with a spoon.  No machines, no fuss.

column9: Absolutely the best... nothing better out there !!!
column10: My mother and I are huge fans of this product... there is nothing else out there that even comes close to it.  But it has gotten more and more difficult to find at my local grocery store.  And like another reviewer, I panicked when for the past week I found out that it is no longer in stock at the one place that I purchased it (I have gone to 4 different stores).However, my peace has returned as I can now buy it from Amazon.  And I can also have it shipped to my mom in Puerto Rico !!

For years, I could only find the chocolate flavor at one grocery store.  Then I panicked when I discovered that this store no longer stocks it.  My reaction was to "Google" it and, lo and behold, Amazon to the rescue!  This is a quality chocolate malted-milk mix.  It tastes wonderful not only in milk but in non-dairy milk as well, such as soy and rice, so even those who are lactose-intolerant can indulge in this treat!

I have to watch my calories and when I want a treat this is usually it. I don't feel bad having it because I add it to skim milk it's a more healthy snack than chips or cookies. One serving is pretty satisfying when I'm craving something sweet and chocolately.I sometimes add this to my chocolate chip cookie recipe. I just add and keep tasting little bits of the dough until I think it's "right". It does tend to make the cookies slightly more crispy than if I didn't use it but they taste really yummy. I've also made coconut cookies and added this. My kids thought they were great but I found them a bit sweet. Next time I'll try cutting the sugar a little and see if that doesn't do the trick.I'm currently working on using it for a coffe cake sort of recipe but so far my attempts have been not as good as I'd like.....cakes are just more tempermental than cookies and since we don't eat a lot of sweets it'll probably take awhile before I get it right.I think this is good heated too and adding it to fat free half and half makes a tastey coffee creamer.This is something I've used for years and will be in my pantry for as long as they keep making it.

column9: Love it! We make Chocolate Malt Shakes with it!
column10: Mmm...our favorite thing to do with Carnation Malted Milk is to make chocolate malt shakes. The instructions are on the package. We like to top them with whipped cream and mini chocolate chips! Delicious! This stuff is the best and the price on Amazon can't be beaten!

Please see my extended (with video) review of the Pro-Pest product.I keep and use industrial felt which is 50/50 wool/synthetic material. No bug problem in the first 2 years I have started using it. In the last two weeks, I start to see moths flying around the felt. Oh, oh, trouble, trouble. Googledee peck, peckity google.Identify malefactors. Did taxpayer money fund the research for this secret stuff? We want to know.Neither brand captures all flying moths like a magnet as at least one reviewer has stated. Hmmm, maybe a plot for a Japanese horror flick.The last time I had moths, 15 years ago, long and short, I used pesticides to finally rid myself of these pests. I cannot tolerate these pests, and now, regrettably, for practical reasons, I have decided to take the advice of my wool felt supplier: Raid Max Deep Penetrating Fogger. Stay tuned.

column9: Works as advertised, isn't going to solve your moth problem on its own
column10: I imagine the people giving this product low ratings either a. don't have clothes moths and expect it to catch all kinds of moths, b. didn't actually put the pheromone in the trap (you have to open the package and drop it in that hole in the top), or c. didn't read the package to see this only traps the MALE clothes moths and does not kill the larva which is what actually eats your clothes.First off, the type of moths that eat your clothes are very very small and very very fast. They also hate light so they are very hard to just spot. Most of the times I've seen them have been when I was watching TV in the dark and one fluttered by the front of the TV or I've found them hiding in cracks in my closet.I had a serious moth infestation in my clothes. I sorta ignored it until they ate about 10 of my sweaters. They were literally in shreds. When I threw all the wool clothes away they started eating the cotton stuff as well (although not as successfully) so I decided to get these traps because I didn't want to use poisons or whatever. They did a good job of trapping a lot of moths but like the packaging says, these basically will ALERT you that you have a problem they aren't going to totally solve it.Eventually I threw away a lot of old clothes and then washed everything else all at once and put anything wool into plastic bags. The moths WILL attempt to eat your cotton stuff but they don't tend to be as destructive to it (you'll see the cocoons on the clothes but they won't be all full of holes like the wool stuff) Vacumming in your closets will also help get rid of them. I then put cedar chips in my closet. Not quite sure how useful that is but I have definitely slowed them down and haven't seen any more destruction since.I uploaded a photo of one of my traps that caught about 20 moths to prove these do work. Just realize to get rid of your problem you're going to have to do more than just get these traps.

Don't buy the Safer traps.

Use other methods (freezer/dryer) to kill those.

column9: Amazing trap that Works Works Works!
column10: whoever wrote a bad review obviously isn't using these right. I have one trap with 31, yes thirty-one moths, and the other has 15 (fifteen) trapped inside. We have an air conditioner that isn't completely sealed in a window near one and I think it even attracted a few from outside and trapped them. So it captures the males no problem. But that's what you want to break the cycle in a cheap and effective way without poisoning yourself, the planet, your kids or your pets right? These work!

These traps are part of a program of integrated pest managemnt...ipm.  They are doused with pheromones from female moths so that they attract male moths and break the breeding cycle.  They work extremely well on that part of the process.  In fact, the minute you open the little package with the trap male moths start fluttering at you like drunken frat boys!  The second part of the program involves repelling the moths from their furry dinners.  Lavender, bay and cedar in a closet help.  Bagging sweaters over the summer will also help.  Being green really is not easy.  It takes extra steps and some research.  This is the way natures works.  We have killed off whatever the predator was for the moths so now we have to figure out how we can manipulate the cycle.  If you think about it, however, the moths are actually kind of a good thing.  If it weren't for these hair/fur eating creatures the earth would be a giant hair ball hanging in space.  Now if safer would only make traps for those annoying people who drive thru my neighborhood with blasting stereos I would be a happy woman!

These do a great job of catching moths in my closet, but you have to assemble them properly. The traps come with little lure tabs -- when you're ready to place the trap, open a lure envelope and find the small lure square inside. Stick the lure square to the adhesive inside the trap. It's the lure that the moths find irresistible, and then they get stuck to the adhesive. My traps generally get full in about 2 months, and then I have to replace them.
