Phosphorous is important to health, but must be on lower range for pets with kidney problem.Food is a bit higher in price, but very well worth the results. I now have a normal weight masculine happy active cat :-) ... woo hoo!!! MEOW!!! =>o<=

column9: Cat's coat has never been softer!
column10: After searching for a grain free cat food that made our cat happy, we discovered Now!. He loves it and it has made his coat super soft. He eats less compared to the grain stuff, and he seems satisfied for longer. We haven't switched for 3 years. When our cat lost a few of his teeth, we tried a soft food, but he preferred this softened with water to canned food, even.The side benefit was the smell from his litterbox dropped dramatically compared to the brands we tried previously.
Food was fragrant for dry cat food but my cat HATED this food. He is not normally a picky eater but he refused to eat this food.

Be sure to note that the reason they can call this 'grain free' is because they use potato and pea starch instead. (Just read the ingredients.)I ordered some without realizing this--when you open the bag you will be knocked off your feet by the smell of instant mashed potatoes.If your goal is to get your cat off starches, this isn't the one.

First, let me say ... To those of you who are reading reviews to gauge if you should by this or not, please don't base if you buy it or not on those reviewers who gave 1 and 2 stars only because of the SHIPPING! That has nothing to do with the juice itself! If you want to review the problem with shipping, don't leave it here, take it to amazon's customer care!On to the actual review. GREAT! I've purchased maybe 8 different brands of 'organic' juice in the last month alone and all have fallen flat. I finally found this one at the Whole Foods Store. When I'm out shopping for something new, I usually go to amazon.com to search for the product and read the customer reviews while I'm standing in the store with the product in my hand. This time, I was in such a hurry that I didn't because I actually thought that this would taste as bad as the other organic juices no matter what the reviews say. Thank goodness I was surprised. My daughter loves it. I tasted it and it tastes great. No sugar added? Yet it still tastes like fruit juice and not watered down crap. Thanks for this! Will continue to buy from the store.

totally agree with other reviews..i stopped buying these from amazon eventho they r slightly cheaper and more available.. every time i ordered these at least one box was WET last time i had to throw away 1 box.. (i got a refund) but still..my son lovvees this juice i just hafta go to Whole foods to get it now.. but sometimes they r out.. might hafta take a chance but with bein so hot im weary of ordering anything on line as far as food/drinks.. maybe when weather turns cold again.. lolanyway,but the Juice Is Great.!! so idk the reviews are mainly about amazons shipping process! but juice itself is very good :)
My granddaughter loves the taste, and I love that it's 100% juice; she can drink as much as she likes without me worrying about her getting "sugared out", or ingesting chemicals.

Three of the pouches in my shipment burst soaking all the boxes and pouches. Just like the previous reviewer, I couldn't store any of the juices in their boxes since they were all wet. As with other reviewer, my shipment had nothing else in it.  I just don't think the product is being package appropriately.  Our child loves the juice, but it's just not worth dealing with the mess.

I should have heeded the other review. Two of the pouches burst in my shipment, soaking all the boxes and pouches. So I had to open all four cases and take all 24 juice pouches out as soon as I brought it into my house, find the ones that burst, and wash the juice off all the others. I couldn't store any of them in the boxes they came in, since they were wet with juice. Unlike the other reviewer, my shipment had nothing else but the juice pouches in it, so I don't think it was items shifting that caused the problem.  Maybe something with the temperature in shipment or maybe the pouches themselves are weak?  The juice tastes great, and even though I don't really mind losing two, the mess is a problem and I won't order these again.

My children really like the juice. So I would give it 4 or 5 stars. Unfortunately, one juice from each box leaked. When the juices were shipped, they were also shipped with 3 other bulk snack items in a large box. The juices were the heaviest items in the box. The other items were crackers and cereal bars. I'm not sure if this was the reason why the juices popped or if they pop regardless of the shipping procedures. Good luck with your purchase.

Excellent tasting product with child appeal. The BB type shape and adding it to boiling chicken broth, beef broth or almost any other flavored liquid medium, makes it an excellent add to any meal, or dress it up with vegetables. Since it is whole wheat, it adds needed fiber to anyone's diet.

This couscous is easy to cook, delicious, and, since it is whole wheat, extremely healthy.  I've used it in salads with quinoa and split peas and fresh veggies, along with some feta.  Add the dressing of your choice (I lean towards a vinegarette), and you now have an amazing salad that functions as entree or side dish.

I used to buy Trader Joe's couscous but decided to try  this brand and type 'cause it sounded so good.  What a disappointment! TJ's is 10 times better than this insult to couscous. With the price so high I expected much better. I gave some to my neighbor and she wouldn't eat it either so I fed it to the dumpster in the parking lot. I'm going back to TJ's and consider this as money down the drain.

This cookie tin arrived the other day. It is just a FOUR inch square little tin which contains just 12 small cookies. Not quite the value for 14.99 plus the 8.99 shipping to where I live....... disappointing to say the least. At least it's cute.
I SPENT 6.94 ON A PACK OF GREENIES WHICH WAS SUPPOSED TO BE A PACK OF 10AND I GOT I LITTLE BONE FOR THAT MONEY WHAT A RIP OFF, THIS IS FALSE ADVERTISING.
There is no quantity listed, but let me tell you.  It is only ONE treat.  One treat.  Are you kidding me?  Original list price $75.00 for ONE treat?

I wish I had read the reviews before I ordered this product - there is something seriously wrong with their system.  The picture clearly shows a bag of 10 - but I received ONLY one Greenie.  I even paid extra to have 1 day delivery - only to receive ONE. I'm returning for credit but will probably be charged return shipping, with no way to find anyone at Amazon to listen. :-(

The picture shows a package of 10 Greenies but when you order it, you only receive one!  What a total absolute ripoff.  After going around with Amazon Customer Service though, I'm happy to say they are going to refund my money.  I only spent $5.93 but every penny counts and I'm tired of being ripped off by people.  Thank you Amazon and I hope they get rid of this seller completely.
I was worried my dog would chew on these and they would stain my bed, etc. They don't. She's happy, I'm happy. Good value.

Candy was just as I remembered as a kid.  Nostalgic contrast to the Red Vines in the day of the "grab bag" and 15 cent candy bars from the ice cream man that could be bought in the store for a nickle.  They were received fresh and within two weeks.  They are a little smaller (shorter and thinner) than the vines in the traditional small grocery packaging, but the taste is not compromised.  Price is average and the shipping cost was a bit on the high side, so there is definetly no bargain here, otherwise enjoyable.
These were very good, especially for the price but, were (unfortunately) not as good as McVittie's digestive biscuits.  Nothing, of course, comes close to Walker's shortbreads, however!

column9: good biscuit but gives you a sandy feeling in the mouth
column10: well, i am not that impressed by this product like others.I think overall it's okay but it leaves a sandy feeling in the mouth after you eat it.

I really recommend this noodle.  It is very delicious... My family's favorite is still the original flavor and not other spicy or shrimp flavor.  Just boil, once it's softened strain the noodle then mix with the seasoning.  The smell is so aromatic.  The packing is misleading though cause people might think there're additional ingredients other than the seasoning itself.  Normally we'd boil the frozen mix vege together with the noodle and fry some eggs to accompany it.  My toddler loves this noodle.  You can buy an individual pack at 99 ranch grocery store.

I found this gem while living in Australia and thank goodness for Amazon because I wanted some bad when I got back to the States...they are so much better than instant noodles or top ramen, they have several packets of different add-ins that really make this come alive...though it seems that they have changed them somewhat from what I remember in Australia, they are still delicious and I would recommend them to anyone...and at this price, you are not paying that much more (if at all) compared to the other stuff!

This is my second 30-pack of Mi Goreng noodles. The first I bought was BBQ Chicken flavor, and I was seriously impressed with their taste. My roommate and I polished off 30 of them in less than a week, so I just had to grab another case. These (the regular flavor) are quite good, although I do prefer the taste of BBQ Chicken. Each package comes with an adequate amount of noodles and seasoned oil, sweetened soy sauce, chili powder, and sauce mix. The oil and soy sauce packets are horribly designed. Anyone who can open them and squeeze out all of the liquid without getting it all over the place is seriously talented. Very Asia (the company that ships these) is pretty speedy, although these arrived slightly damaged (the sauce packages were busted in a few of the noodles). The BBQ Chicken case I ordered, however, was completely undamaged, so I guess it's hit or miss in that department. Anyway, buy these things. They are delicious and easy, and much better than plain old ramen noodles.

I first became addicted to Mi Goreng in university. Attracted initially by the cheapness of the product - which appealed to my frequently empty wallet. Soon after I was hooked. Even now as an employed person with a steady income, I still enjoy these noodles. They take me back to a simpler time when furniture was sourced from the side of the road and washed clothes was a luxury.High quality noodles with a great, complex flavour and just the right amount of MSG. Great for quick snacks, or as an additive to stir frys.Note: there is no egg inside the bag - no matter how hard you look.

column9: Still Very Good, but Not The Same...
column10: I fell in love with these while going to University in Australia. Eating three packs a day was not a rare event for me to say the least! These were my dietary staple - especially because you could easily add steamed veggies, garlic, shrimp, fish, crab, fried/poached egg, etc...to make it a more substantial meal.What I love about this instant noodle is that it is similar to Ramen in price and preparation but stepped up several levels in taste and complexity. I loved that there were five seasoning packets - a seasoning powder, fried onions, and three liquids which were chili paste, sweet soy sauce, and oil.Unfortunately, it is IMPOSSIBLE to find that five-packet version in the states! When I ordered these here (also ordered from several other specialty sites) they only came with four packets :( No fried onions, and the chili paste was instead a chili powder. While they still taste great, they are not the incredibly addicting noodles I was used to as a poor college student in Australia. I still crave that same taste I got from the version sold in Australia. I wish these were the same so badly, but they are not.I have also noticed a few other reviewers saying it does taste differently than what they remember. I still absolutely recommend these though, because they are still delicious and I always have a case available in the house. Would switch in a heartbeat though if I could find the original five-packet version!

It's one of my favorite instant noodles, I always buy a case of it. It's a bit spicy and sweet taste and it's smell so good for instant noodles. One bag is not enough, have to have @least 2 bag. Just like the picture, can add fried eggs and other ingredient on top of it. It's so Yummy and delicious, you gotta try it. Totally recommended!!!!!!!!!

Darn they still sell this... i used to eat this when i was a child, my mom (a Malaysian) would sometimes buy like 6 to 8 boxes of this noodles... and i still remember the smell and taste of it... mmmmmm... yum! I'd probably by this just cause i want to remember the good ol'days... I HIGHLY RECOMMEND THAT YOU BUY THIS... SERIOUSLY!!! IT'S BETTER THAN THAT ROMEN CRAP THING...

I have loved ramen noodles since my college roomate introduced them to me. I have tried all the flavors, and can buy them anywhere for a low price. I saw this and it's reviews on amazon and decided to try it. Anyway it tasts great, and for a decent price too.
These mi goreng barbecue noodles are good,they have a nice taste to them... luv em im odering more its worth your money!!!!!
I Don`t usually write reviews, but these noodles(sauce,flavor pack,oil,soy sauce,peppers) are really something special. If you are a fan of noodles you should really try these.

Tastes OK. Heres an idea of what it taste like if you've never had it: You could probably achieve a similar taste with common instant ramen  (maruchan, sapporo ichiban). Cook without seasoning. Drain. Add half seasoning packet, dash of veg oil and a dab sweet soy sauce. The sweet soy sauce is the main difference from other noodles.More importantly the online price @ $20 is double of what you would pay for at an asian grocery (i know not everyone has access to them but still good to know you're being ripped off). Furthermore the street price in indonesia is about 17 cents for each pack ( .17*30= $5.10) whereas this price is 67 per pack
I like it very muchtasty ........  and .......... easyI wold like to try other flavor ... ... ... ... ... ...

i wanna get this noodle but i dont know where this one made in?does this one made in indonesia or the imitation from china or other country?i only like the original from indofood indonesia,can anyone let me know please?

Best Ramen noodles I ever ate - I will be eating plenty of these as they are only 200 calories per package and make for an excellent snack.  I like dropping a jumbo egg (additional 80 calories with good protein) in for a poached egg effect as it gets close to the 3 minute boiling finish.  I will look forward to trying other Indomie flavors and products in the future.

These things are tasty. Flavorful but not too salty, a hint of spicy but not tongue-torching, moist but not oily. Of course they're easy to make, like any instant noodle product. One thing that's different from your run-of-the-mill pack of ramen is that these aren't soup noodles, so you'll need to pull out your colander to drain the noodles after they've cooked.My favorite way to make these into a heartier meal (1 pack probably won't fill up some big tummies) is pan-frying some cubes of tofu and seasoning with garlic and soy sauce. Top your noodles with the tofu and you've got a great lunch or dinner!I was pleased to see that these actually AREN'T terrible for you. A few highlights: (for 1 package/serving)Calories: 210Fat: 8g (12%)Trans fat: 0gCholesterol: 0mgSodium: 400mg (17%)Carbs: 30g (4%)Protein: 4g (8%)Go for it! These delicious noodles are great by themselves but are also versatile - use your imagination :)
Just add the included spices and whatever you like, I like bay shrimp, and you've got a great meal in about 10 minutes......... 'got 'em in about 3 days......... Life is good!.!.!
I like this noodle so much. Easy to make it, unexpensive, has a lot of flavours. I bet everybody will like this noodle also if they tried.

This is the best noodles you'll ever get from a package like this. Perfect for a quick meal, easy to make, and easy to eat (one of my least favorite things about ramen was hunting down the last noodles in your bowl, idk call me lazy, but these are perfect for me)These were wayy worth the $17 I paid for 30.
I like the product but it is Noodles and should be handled with care Yet it Delivred with bumps on the package and the noodles inside were smashed little bit and the suace were leaking.

There is a Chinese article from Taiwan (found in yahoo-Hong Kong) that issued a product recall for all Indomie Noodles.  The test result from Taiwanese authorities shows that the product contained excess amount of preservatives. Although damage to human may not be immediate but prolonged consumption could lead to kidney disease.I, myself, used to love this product but I have reduced the consumption of all Instant Noodles from once a day to once every 3 to 4 months.  Best to stay away from these processed food especially one with a recall.([...])
i got this from a recommendation of a friend.at the very best, its "alright".nothing great.

First let me say that I bought this on sale for under $20.  Given that; the per pound price was a good value.  The salmon is what you'd expect from a shelf-stable product.  I'm not a huge fan of the tins so I wouldn't base my buying decision on receiving a Checkered Tin.
Not at all what we excepted. Similar to canned salmon in vacuum pkg. We thought we were getting smoked salmon which we love with bagels and cream cheese.

column9: Fantastic Salsa from a mix and FAST to make
column10: This year I have gone back to using Mrs Wages mixes. They are fast and easy to use. I always recommend Mrs. Wages to all new canners. It's a great way to build your confidence in canning. And its a great way to get your canning done if you need to get it done fast. And this Salsa mix still lets you add your own touch to make it just a little hotter or a little different. Yet still get it done fast!

I like to use these frequently in cooking, but when I buy them in small containers at the grocery store they don't last long, and I'm overpaying.I was impressed at how much I got of these for the price.  The three bags will last me quite a while.  They taste fresh.  I'm happy I bought them.

column9: Good quality for a good price.
column10: Previously I bought some mustard seed that was unbearably bitter, but the mustard I made with this seed is very tasty and (after mellowing a few days) not bitter at all. Pleasantly spicy.
If you're a fan of Russian mustard, get this and make your own from scratch.
Just received and have incorporated this brown seed into my latest batch of mustard sauce.  I can tell by the aroma that this will be a great batch!

The three bags of brown mustard seeds were a good value and provided a tangible gift for our congregation on Resurrection Sunday.  We were able to half fill 250 small plastic bags (2" x 2") with the seeds, and had some left over.

Three bags must be a lifetime supply. What a good price. I received three bags, gave one to my daughter, put one in the pantry unopened, and filled a 20 oz. storage jar with the other. They are not perhaps as pungent as I had expected. I use them to reheat rice prepared with cumin and other spices. I put chesse chunks in the rice, a little yogurt on top, and a sprinkle of black mustard seeds on this, then reheat in the microwave.

I bought this mustard seed to use in some pickling I was doing.  I got three pounds for the same price that I would pay in the grocery store for a few ounces.With the extra I made some spicy mustard.  It's awesome.  I take it and spread it on a whole pork loin and then roast the loin.  The flavor is out of this world.Great Value.Great Product.Great Results.
I ordered this to make an Oktoberfest Beer Mustard recipe and these mustard seeds are so incredibly bitter, I had to throw out every jar!

column9: Great price, but could be fresher.
column10: I was tired of buying small jars of mustard seed at the store at $4-$5 dollars each, this product is maybe 1/10 the price for an equivalent amount. While I like the price, the first of 3 bags I opened didn't seem very fresh. I made a balsamic mustard with it and it was good, but not quite as good as previous batches with McCormick mustard. I'll make a decision on whether or not to purchase this product again after I open bags 2 and 3.
I wonder why it took so long to come out with this,they are sooo good...
Could not find this product anywhere until I found it on Amazon.  Lesson learned:  look to Amazon first! And you can't beat the easiness of the site!

Product shipped in summer in regular Amazon Carton. Candy arrived in melted condition. Contacted the shipper; he ignored my cotact. This represents very poor service; one of the two worst I have experienced from an Amazon supplier and I order often from Amazon. The Dark Chocolate candy is great but NOT in the condition as received. Reese's was NOT the Shipper.

They may only be 2oz, but these little guys have a lot of punch.  They taste great and really do give you a boost of energy - without the massive crash later.  I have tried all sorts of caffeine free sports drinks and this is the first one that is worth it.
Eric's Sport Ade is just what I needed. I tried it on one of those rainy, dark afternoons and it gave me the punch I needed to power through the long day. Will definitely stock up on this!
This is a great french syrup. You just need few drops to prepare a great a refreshing drink for kids. You can also use it for cocktails.

column9: Fantastic nutritional gift from the sea!
column10: I can't say enough good about Eden's Wakame.  I absolutely love it and prepare a simple raw wakame salad from one 2.1 ounce package at least once a week. Furthermore and most importantly to me as a raw vegan resident of Florida, it is a must have in my hurricane pantry for it soaks quickly providing a highly nutritious fresh green vegetable.  This product is truly a delicious and nutritious gift from the sea. I should also add that it is a good buy here at Amazon.

I have purchased Wakame from a well-known largely organic food store.  When I received this shipment from Amazon I was pleasantly surprised how fresh the seaweed was.  I didn't know it should NOT be dry and brittle (store purchase) and accepted it as a quality of dried seaweed.It is much easier to cut strips for homemade seaweed salad and much less expensive.  Overall, an excellent buy at nearly $2 per pkg cheaper.Update March 10, 2011*****I find if you cut it along the short way (width) before hydrating, instead of trying to cut it in long strips, it is almost the quality size that you can get from a restaurant when using Cuisanart kitchen shears.If you can, read/purchase a book called Seaweed- Nature's Secret to Balancing Your Metabolism, Fighting Disease, and Revitalizing Body & Soul By Valerie Gennari Cooksley, RN.  It is awesome!  You'll find yourself eating a greater variety of the greens. I found my copy at Half Price Books in Orland Park, ILSeaweed: Nature's Secret to Balancing Your Metabolism, Fighting Disease, and Revitalizing Body and Soul

column9: Love this wakame, great for seaweed salad, or soups!
column10: I buy this product regularly and have it stocked on all times.  I'm a huge fan of Eden Foods, especially since it's a company that appears to have integrity regarding their products.  Anyways, this seaweed is great for soups (for adding another depth of flavor), or even to make seaweed salad, with a little vinegar, honey, soy sauce and minced garlic.  I soak the seaweed first and make sure to rinse the seaweed several times.  Then blanch it for about a minute, and then drain the water.  Then cut it up, and mix it with the above ingredients for a yummy side salad!

My daughter (4 yr) and I love to just chew on these.  I leave them out over night and then they are nice and crunchy the next day.  We like the flavor even though my son hates them.  There is certainly a seaweed taste to them as that is what they are, but we enjoy them as is.  They are very salty and sometimes we just nibble on these which of course is much better than nibbling on potato chips.

column9: the packages hold more wakame than they look
column10: I used this to make miso soup by mixing 2 tablespoons of miso paste into 2 cups of boiling water & adding wakame with a pinch of msg-free chicken boullion.  It was filling, very tasty & with very few calories!  I accidentally added a bit too much wakame to my soup, so I will be using less next time.  (These things expand a bit).  My dogs were begging for a taste of wakame so I gave them some & they loved it too!
I liked this wakame, to chew when you feel like for something salty (though is a bit too salty) nutrition value is my main point of consuming this wakame.
When you are hungry for a Great candy bar this is the one to sink your teeth into, it just brings a smile to your face.

Delicious.  This is me and my children's favorite soy sauce.  I am ordering it from Amazon because I can't find it in the stores anymore.  Not too strong, mildly sweet with a light ginger flavor.  It tastes good simply over rice, on California rolls, or for dunking potstickers.  Try it, you'll like it.

This is a really good product.  While it is only 4 ounces, it is actually about a quart of freeze dried shallots.  I have long used fresh shallots extensively in cooking, and these are an excellent replacementwhen "fresh" is not required (such as salads, etc).  They save all the work of peeling and chopping fresh shallots for cooking.  The product, while fairly costly (as are fresh shallots), is a real time saver, and worth every penny of the cost.  Freeze dried is much better than just plain dried.  I use freeze dried herbs whenever I can find them, as they more exactly replace fresh products.  If you use shallots, you will love this product.

column9: shallots on hand all the time
column10: Great way to keep shallots on hand.  The fresh ones are not inexpensive especially if part of it is wasted.  This allows me to have it on hand and not have to run out to get them at the last minute.  Convenient to have and taste is very good.

I use a lot of herbs and spices. If I can find what I want in a McCormick product, I will usually purchase the McCormick product. I was skeptical about freeze dried shallots. If you are picky enough to use shallots, how can you not suspect freeze dried shallots?Yes, fresh, hand selected shallots are  better, but you don't always have them handy.These are great. Just rehydrate or use dried in your recipes containing liquids. You will be hard pressed to discern!
This product re-hydrates beautifully!  I live a long way from the store and shallots add such a wonderful dimension to many food dishes, it is just plain fun to have them always available.

I have two dogs, a basset and a corgi, and they are total chewers. If they don't have something to chew on then they're running around the house like little mini-tornadoes. They don't like rawhide chips, get bored of unflavored bones, and are only occupied for ten to fifteen minutes with all other forms of chew toys.  Keeping them in flavored rawhide gets expensive.  These things are a great deal.  Big bones, flavors that make my dogs happy, and way less expensive than anything I could get at the local pet store.

column9: Too big for my 4.5 lb. Yorkie!
column10: These are probably ok but supposedly I was ordering the "small" size ones and they are HUGE!  My Yorkie can't enjoy them at all.  Will give to my GrandDog.  Need to advertise these better!
I bought the large size for my min pins because they last for days while they might chew up small sized rawhides in less than an hour.

column9: Great variety at a good price
column10: I ordered the small-sized bones for my miniature schnauzer.  He's not a big fan of the natural rawhide bones, so I decided to order a flavored variety pack.  What a success!  According to the package the flavors are hickory, beef, and chicken, and it comes with a mix of twelve bones and rolled rawhide.  The price isn't much better than a local pet store, but I would buy these bones again.Also, if you are concerned with the country of origin, these bones were made in Brazil.

My son is 10 months old and adores Fruit Medley by Gerber.  There are very small chunks mixed in so your baby can start to chew and get used to more solid foods.  Fruit Medley is a mix of peaches, grapes, pineapple, banana, and orange.  A great start for babies beginning to eat more solid foods!

A nice blend of several different fruits. This stage 3 food was tasty. Not as thick as some other stage threes and there are no bites or chunks. It is more like a thin custard. My son always loved this.
Rarely find the baby fruit I used to make a Baby Food Cake so ordered it fom Amazon...came very promptly and now I have plenty to make several cakes.  Good deal!  Pat Thompson

I first tried this tea from my local grocery store and it doesn't even compare to the taste of the arizona raspberry. This stuff taste very good. I highly recommend this from amazon because of the price, you cant beat it with the free shipping and no tax.

column9: Great taste, cheap price, very satisfying!
column10: This drink ***SLURP*** is soo good! I am drinking one right now and I have not had a razz berry tea that taste as good as this one! Absolutely DELICIOUS! Peace Tea is an amazing drink with all of their flavors being terrific!

column9: Tea is great, whats up with the price?
column10: This tea is amazing I bought it on here when it was 22$ for the 24-pack and set up a once a month subscription. Now it says 60$ for a 24pack..who would pay that when its 99cents per can at the corner store. I will be cancelling my subscription and be watching the price more closely now. The tea is insanely good though just beware the price, it seems to fluctuate a lot. Only reason I have 4 stars instead of 5 is the changing price.

column9: WAS way too expensive, now GREAT!
column10: I love Peace Tea Razzleberry but the price of this bulk is just INSANE!! When you buy a can at walgreens its 99 cents, this price is $2.50 per can, that is just dumb!UPDATE:When I originally wrote this review the price was crazy, now its great, so I encourage you to buy this delicious razzleberry tea, its low calorie and tastes fantastic!

I've purchased Peace Tea several times from Amazon. I liked the taste and was very pleased with the ease of deliery via subscribe and save. However I was disapponted to learn it really isn't all natural even though the can has statements that lead you to beleive it is. My teenage son noticed that it contains sucralose (i.e splenda). I just cancelled my subscribe and save order for this product.
I buy lots of this tea at gas stations and quick marts, so when i found this it was great, at a dollar a can this was far cheaper than paying tax on a single can, great buy
I love razzleberry peace tea it is my favorite drink coming off drinking soda. I love the sweet lemon tea also highly recommended, even my dad liked it and he is a stickler for sweetened tea.
This is really good tea, but I can buy a can for .99 at Walmart.Why in the world is yours $60. for 24 cans?

I was excited to see this product for sale as it sounded great and healthy by the description.  Then I looked up the ingredients and see that it contains Sucralose.  Sucralose is deadly.  Do not buy this tea until they remove this poisonous ingredient.
Very refreshing and love the flavor of raspberry,just enough and not too much. Would definately buy again. Like the can size too, 23 ounce.

I absolutely love Peace Tea. I just tried it for the first time yesterday and I would love for it to be able to be bought in bulk. I am actually planning on getting my friend a 24 pack when her birthday comes around in June! I def recommend this drink. It is a delicious tea with not as many calories as Arizona Tea and other teas you can get at the gas station.

The treats came in a brownish/yellowish package rather than the blue/green color displayed, but though a different color package, the treats are the same as what I had before (in the blue/green pkg).  Being I was getting a package of 10 bags, I was hoping the expiration date was far out and it was (June 2010) so am very happy.  These particular treats (Friskie soft/tender chicken) have become just about impossible to find in stores anymore so was thrilled to find them online.

I have one cat with severe constipation and the other with some hairball problems.  Friskies hairball remedy with chicken is the one treat they will both eat.  I like the price as well as the convenience of home delivery on a self-chosen time basis.  I never have to worry about going to the store and finding they are out of stock.  Thank you Amazon.

My cat takes two types of heart medication; one is a small pill and the other is made up of divided granules from a human-sized capsule. I am always on the lookout for soft, pliable treats in which to insert her meds. Until I had picked up a bag of these treats, I had been using Whisker Lickins Tender Moments treats. However, those can get dried out by the time you get to the last half to third of the bag, rendering them useless for the pills. These are very soft, and while they're more expensive than other low-end brands, they stay fairly soft, even down to the last one. They're also much less expensive than Pill Pockets and can be bought in more retail outlets. The extra benefit of helping with hairballs is yet another plus!

Our cat loves these hairball treats. In fact, I have to make sure she can't get to them. She got into the bag one time and ate about half. Needless to say, she was sick for several days after her blunder. But she still loves her treats. To her, they are just a treat. For me, they do help her remain hairball free.
These treats really do work. Getting my cats to take Laxatone was impossible. They are a little oily so dont feed on something that might stain. Recommend several a day to prevent hairballs.

I have tried every hairball remedy out there and this is definitely the best.  Why?  Because the cats will eat them with no problem.  It was always a battle to get any of the other remedies in the cats, half of it ended up on me or the fur or the floor.  The remedy is no good if you can't get it in the cat.  LOL!But every cat I have owned/own loves these "treats."  I do a maintenance feed once a week and when the shedding gets bad I do it every day for three days.  Even better, it gets great results.  No more surprise globs on the floor, no more hacking sounds in the middle of the night.  LOL! I hardly ever give these 'Wow' reviews but this product deserves it!Also the price is about the same as the box stores but they don't always have them in stock so this is great too.

Our cat has medium lenght hair and like most cats grooms often. I started to notice that she was hacking a little & wasn't using the litter box as often,(#2)so i looked up online and it said she may have hairballs. There are a lot of black nasty pastes out there but its difficult to dose a cat with them. I only feed my cat Friskies so i went to the website and saw the hairball remedy treats. I couldnt find them at my local stores so i ordered them from amazon. My cat loves the taste and within a few days she was back to her old self. With this pack of 10 i should be well stocked for a while.

These things REALLY work!  I bought these based on all the positive reviews as a desperate attempt to find something that would stop our female tabby from throwing up 2-3 times a day, every time she ate.  I've been giving both our cats 3 a day (less than the "treament" amount but more than the "maintenance" amount), and in the past month, the tabby has thrown up maybe 2 or 3 times total.  Our boy cat, who had hairballs more rarely (maybe one every other week), hasn't had a single one since they started getting these.  And they absolutely LOVE them!  They're moist and chewy, and I've been able to train them both to sit up on their back feet on command for these treats.  I hadn't held out much hope for these since we'd already tried Petromalt and had switched them to expensive hairball formula cat food, but I was definitely surprised at how well they work.  Go for Subscribe & Save to save some money -- a box of 10 packs every 6 months is just about perfect, and if you wind up with too many, you can always skip or delay a shipment.

column9: The only treats my cat can eat
column10: My cat gets sick from crunchy treats but gets hairballs if we don't give him anything.  It seems that I can no longer find these particular treats in stores, so I'm glad they have them here.  They are reasonably priced and it's great that they can be delivered with Amazon Prime.

Both of our cats love these soft treats--and ONLY these treats! We give them these in addition to their indoor cat food to help keep down the hairballs.  A great thing since one is a long-haired Main Coon and the other is a meuium-hair Pastel Calico.  Getting them in bulk from Amazon is a HUGE money saver and convenient since these treats have become expensive and difficult to find in our area.  I recommend the treats AND the auto-ship option from Amazon!

column9: One Happy Owner and Two Happy Cats
column10: Friskies created a wonderful product that my cats love to eat and it stopped the fur ball problem completely. It is like and hide and seek to find it in the stores. Thankfully Amazon carries this product.
I don't know how it works, but these help my cat have good breath and not have hairballs, even when we travel and she is nervous.  Good to have, we just give her 1-2 treats each day.

These treats are the only ones that one of my cats will eat.  And thank goodness Amazon has them, because most of the stores around me have stopped carrying them, for some reason.  We're on the subscription plan at my house!

when I did my weekly shopping and found they no longer carried these wonderful hairball treats that brought my fluffy cat back to life after she became full of hair from self grooming. I've found these to be a Godsend and was so glad I was able to still find them online. These treats help the cat ease out the excess hair she accumulates no matter which end it lubricates. I can't live without these as she's so fussy, they are all she will devour when bound up by hairballs.

Friskies Hairball Remedy is now impossible to find in local stores in the San Francisco Bay area. I was happy to find it on Amazon. It works for my cat. It is the only hairball remedy we have found on the market that my cat will eat and she loves it. It is the only one that she will hold in her stomach without heaving it out.

column9: my cats favorite treat via Amazon.com
column10: product came extremely fast in the mail was fresh and packaged well.I can give my cat Pretty Kitty other treats instead of these she will sit thereand look at me until I put at least 1 of them in the bowl with the other. that's howmuch she likes these.

Two of my three cats love these.  In the past, I used these treats to hide a pill for a sick cat.  It worked like a charm and worked much better than pill pockets.  two of my kitties love these and beg for their treats.  the 16yo cat seems to get less hairballs and it keeps things moving for him.

These are like candy for our cat, who goes crazy when she hears the bag rustle (or anything that sounds like it).  If you want to give your cats treats, they will probably love these.  They are also soft enough to wrap around a pill, so if you need to give your cat medicine they are a great option.  However, I only give 4 stars because I doubt the nutritional value of treats in general and I'm concerned with the almost addicting quality of these.

These treats are amazing.  I moved into a new condo with new carpet and I think my cat was licking herself constantly to get the carpet fibers off.  As a result, she was having hairballs at least three to four times a week.  Brand new carpet and hairballs are not the best combination!  I tried these treats after reading all the great reviews on here.  At first, I gave her at least six everyday and they slowly started to work.  After she went a couple days without a hairball, I started to give her four every other day.  They continue to work.  These are more expensive than other treats, but they are totally worth it if your cat has issues with hairballs.  My cat won't eat these as a treat, but I just put them in with her food and she eats them right away.  AWESOME product.

column9: Only Soft Hairball Remedy Left (that my cat will eat)
column10: After Pounce discontinued their soft hairball "pillows", Friskies is the last soft Hairball Remedy (that my cats will eat).  My Vet gives his cat 6 of these to his cats (cuts down on vomiting) and recommended it to me.  I have done the same and my medium hair cat rarely vomits and has regular poop habits.  Highly recommended.

my cat is very finicky, but she is my baby...we couldn't find her treats anywhere (actually, we still can't find her favorite ones...whitefish and tuna (something like that)  but she does love these!!!
I have been giving these treats to my cats for several years now and they love them.  It gets rid of hairballs in no time at all!

These are a great way to help prevent reoccurring hairballs. I wouldn't recommend them as a treatment since you have to give alot of them to get rid of existing hairballs. But once my cat's hairball issue was under control we maintained him on these. Four stars because you'd have to give him the whole bag to get rid of hairballs.. but they are great for maintenance purposes.

This is my 3rd order of Hancock Gourmet Lobster Co. Lobster Mac & Cheese from Kitty Hawk Wholesale.Buying 2 - 2.5 lb. casseroles from Kitty Hawk Wholesale is much more cost effective than buying the small portions.Kitty Hawk Wholesale always delivers the casseroles promptly wrapped securely in bubble wrap and paper in a styrofoam container.There is  lots of lobster in large chunks. Every forkful is a taste of heaven for lobster lovers.From the Hancock Gourmet Lobster Company:This is not your grandmother's mac & cheese! This is a remarkable dish with astounding richness and flavor. Pasta in a creamy mascarpone-cheddar sauce with sweet chunks of Maine lobster. All this topped with a crunchy mix of panko bread crumbs, herbed butter, lemon zest and parmesan cheese.The New York Times Food Editor says "This is a cashmere comfort food".2008 Winner 1st Place Award  Fancy Food Show2010 Winner for "Outstanding Frozen Savory" International Fancy Food Show.Featured on Good Morning AmericaShipped FrozenAll Natural

column9: Low fat, vegetarian, non-fried alternative to ramen, but a bit bland
column10: There are 3 flavors in the annie chun "ramen house" lineup, and I recently tried this one, and the "soy ginger" flavor. The "ramen house" lineup includes a packet of pre-cooked noodles that are non-fried and low fat. They come soft unlike the hard brick that usually comes with ramen. There is also a liquid soup packet. This particular flavor I found to be somewhat bland. The noodles are cooked perfectly and are a good consistency. The soup is not spicy at all. If you added some tofu, vegetables, scallions, etc you can make a more filling meal out of it. I added some soy sauce and it improved the taste considerably.My recommendation is to go with the MUCH better (but not vegetarian) soy ginger flavor: Annie Chun's Soy Ginger, 4.9-Ounce (Pack of 12) It has a much richer and better taste. However, if you are strictly vegetarian, this is still a decent alternative to regular ramen noodles. Another vegetarian option I find to be tastier then this is the Annie Chun's Udon Soup Noodle Bowl, 5.3-Ounce Bowls (Pack of 6). It is also vegetarian, includes a few vegetables, a bowl to cook everything in, and is my favorite.If you aren't vegetarian, id try the other flavors first, but this flavor is still decent, especially when other ingredients are added. A little hot sauce would probably liven it up quite a bit. It also has a very reasonable amount of sodium compared to similar products. Its shelf stable and easy to make with either boiling water or a microwave. I pay about $1.50/ea in my local grocery - the amazon vendors often hike up the price where its not worth buying online.If you are looking for other vegetarian/vegan soup options similar to ramen, another brand to look for is "Thai Kitchen" and "Simply Asia". They offer some excellent rice noodle bowls and soups that are also gluten free as well: Thai Kitchen Noodle Bowl, Roasted Garlic, 2.4-Ounce Unit (Pack of 6)Ingredients:NOODLES: WATER, WHEAT FLOUR, TAPIOCA STARCH, SALT, WHEAT GLUTEN, LACTIC ACID, ACETIC ACID, RIBOFLAVIN (VITAMIN B2), SOUP BASE: ONION (ONION, WATER, CITRIC ACID), ORGANIC MUSHROOM BASE (ORGANIC MUSHROOMS, SALT, ORGANIC CANE SUGAR, ORGANIC MALTODEXTRIN, NATURAL FLAVORS, ORGANIC ONION*, ORGANIC SOYBEAN OIL, ORGANIC GARLIC*), ROASTED CABBAGE POWDER (CHINESE CABBAGE EXTRACT, MALTODEXTRIN, SUGAR, CORN OIL), WATER, CORN STARCH, MIREPOIX (MALTODEXTRIN, ONION, SALT, SUGAR, YEAST EXTRACT, CORN SALAD OIL, CARROT, CELERY, SPICES, RED WINE), GINGER (GINGER, WATER, CITRIC ACID), SALT, YEAST EXTRACT, GARLIC (GARLIC, CITRIC ACID), BLACK PEPPER, NATURAL FLAVORING (NATURAL FLAVORING, MALTODEXTRIN), WHITE PEPPER. *DEHYDRATEDPRODUCT MANUFACTURED IN A FACILITY THAT USES, SOY, MILK, PEANUTS, TREE NUTS, EGGS, FISH AND SHELLFISH. I tried this flavor after enjoying Spicy Chicken flavor( which really was very good) and was dissapointed. I expected a little more flavor. It was just ok, I probably will buy the other flavors except for this one.  It simply wasnt flavorful enough for my taste.

column9: 10 cent ramen is better than this
column10: I bought this today as a snack for lunch at the grocery. Usually I am pretty pleased with this brand's soups. However, there is a distinctly playdough smell when you open the package of noodles, and as for the the flavor after cooking, well ... might have cooked real playdough and ate that instead. distinct vinegar taste to added flavor packet. All in all, i would prefer 10 cent top ramen over this.

I really enjoyed this ramen soup. Although others have described this flavor as I bland, I found it to be refreshing and light. As the other reviewer suggested one could add tofu and veggies to make it into a meal.

I stopped eating meat and dairy 8 months ago and really missed my ramen noodles. I have always kept the old trusty "ramen bricks" on hand for my kids or for just a quick lunch but they all consist of some animal product so i could no longer eat them. Then I discovered these. I was so excited when I saw on the label that they were Vegan. I was not disappointed either. They are really good. I had to add a little salt I will admit but I really expected to have to. I have discovered that anything labeled Vegan for some reason needs salt added. I have no idea why. But I really liked them. I will surely be buying more of these.

I like plenty of products from Annie Chun. They're usually a nice alternative to instant ramen...I did not enjoy this, ok? It was bland and what wasn't bland was sour in a vinegary unpleasant way.Despite being called spring vegetable flavor, there were no vegetables to re-hydrate.I got this at the grocery store and would not get it again.Stickin to ramen and Nissin Chow mein, although I'm looking into nissin udon and some more authentic yakisoba (NOT maruchan).I really like the annie chun's sticky rice, though. perfect for those days in college when you just need rice.

I purchased a bag of this soup at my local grocery store and was so disappointed in its flavor; it had none.  Despite emptying a flavor packet into the broth, I might have just as well left the water with nothing added at all.While vegetarian, this product is not worth it. In addition to lacking taste, it is somewhat time consuming because it isn't a one-step process to get to the final product.  The directions tell the user to soak the noodles in hot water, drain the noodles, add room temperature water and then heat the product in the microwave.If you want some flavorful ramen, try Dr. McDougall's Right Foods Vegan Miso Ramen, 1.9-Ounce Cups (Pack of 6), Dr. McDougall's Right Foods Ramen Chicken Soup with Noodles, 1.8-Ounce (Pack of 6) and/or Dr. McDougall's Right Foods Vegan Chinese Noodle Soup,Lower Sodium, 1.4-Ounce Cups (Pack of 6).  Their soups have some flavor and don't require the soaking of noodles and subsequent refilling of water.I'm so glad I did not buy these in bulk - definitely pick one up from the store before purchasing a good number of these.

Ramen is one of those items I like to keep on hand. After becoming vegan, I was hard pressed to find a ramen I could eat. Then I found this ramen at Whole Foods and decided it was so good, I had to buy it by the case!My favorite way to enjoy this ramen is to prepare as directed, but add miso, seaweed and sesame oil. DEEElicious!Also try Annie Chun's "ginger soy" flavor. It's pretty tasty too.

The Quaker Stila Crispy Oat Cookie Bar was not what I expected at all. It has a crispy outside, and blueberry filling on the inside. There was not much filling on the inside, and had kind of a grainy taste. The outside was too crispy for my taste. It was so crispy I couldn't break it in half with my hands.

I received this "Quaker STILA", which is advertized as a "crispy oat cookie bar with fruit filling"; in my case, with a `blueberry' filling.  I received this `bar' just about the time of its expiration date.  It had a distinct `crunchiness' about its shell that contained the grape filling, which meet its advertized "crispy" bar touting.  The `crunchiness' really did not distract from the product, as it wasn't `hard' from the sense that one had to force a bit through it - just a little more crunchy that what I was expecting.  But, as it was at its expiration date, it did seem to be a little `drier' and  `off taste' to me.  The shell had a nice cinnamon dusting on it that `kicked up' the enjoyment of eating the bar.  I also enjoyed the grape filling - it's consistency was sort of like a Fig Nutin.  The box touts that there are "100 calories Per Bar"  and "0g Trans Fat" -- which appears to be an appeal to the health-conscious or diet-minded eater.  Having had nothing for dinner the night before, one bar and a glass of milk quenched my immediate hunger pains on an early Sunday morning.  As I need a fuller breakfast, I need perhaps two of these to get me through the morning until lunch.  As, I don't see these cookie-bars as a replacement for my current bowl of cereal in the morning, I don't see myself in occasionally purchasing more of this product.

I took these bars on a recent camping trip and was disappointed in how unsatisfying they are. After about half an hour I was hungry again. They are tasty, kind of like a stepped-up Nutri Grain bar, but I would rather have the extra 20-30 calories and be more satisfied.

column4: T. Lee "God has died lots of times, but someo...
column10: These cookie bars were delightful.  A great combination of chewy sweetness and oatsy crisp.  Nicely balanced between dry and mushy, and a good size for a quick pick-me-up.  When I get tired of yogurt for my work lunch pack, I'll keep these in mind for something new.

The Quaker Stila Blueberry Cookie Bars are quite tasty as a snack.  They are of snack size, 100 calories per bar, very little fat and sugar, yet are satisfying, easy to carry and something a little different for those who are trying to eat consciously.  A good product.

I love cereal bars, I really, really do.  But the Nutrigrain, which has been the staple for the world, is just too most.  Special K's Cereal crisps are okay, but a little too crisp.  Where's the middle ground?  Right here.  These Oat Cookies are the perfect blend of crisp, oaty, and moist to satisfy the most discerning connosieur.  What I loved the most, though, is that the blueberry flavor is not overpowering.  Obviously there's some artificiality to it, but the blueberry is not too much, nor too little.  Makes a great snack or lunch compliment.

column9: liked flavor, not sure about crunch, poorly packaged-damaged
column10: Well, this item got mixed reviews in our household.  One daughter did not like it all, the other did.  My husband could have taken it or left it, and I liked the flavor but the texture I am still not sure about, it was a little too crunchy I think, but I'd eat them again I am just not sure I'd spend my money on these instead of buying something else that we prefer and is more well received be everyone the same in out house.  I was also disappointed that the box arrived in a bubble envelope and was quite crushed, the bars were all broken inside to some degree.

Really love blueberries, and these aren't a bad light breakfast on the run. But they are extremely dry, and maybe a bit bland, not much of the tartness I love so much about blueberries is detectable here. Make sure to enjoy with a cup of tea.

These Stilia bars are wonderful. They taste great, are only 100 calories and my whole family loved them - especially the rabbits. They're quite filling and the juxtoposition of a crunchy outside with a jam-like inside made for an excellent snack. The only downside is that we haven't been able to find these in our local supermarkets. I will say that these are extremely fragile and that sometimes you'll end up with some broken bars before you even open the wrapper. Doesn't make them taste any less awesome though!

I've eaten Nutri-Grain bars on and off for a while, usually because I'm lazy and don't like to cook in the morning.  These are a little better than the Nutri-Grain bars if only because they're crunchy.  The chewiness of the Nutri-Grain bars makes them seem even more bland than they usually are, whereas with the Stila bars the crunchiness livens it up a little, making it almost seem like you're eating a pastry instead of something good for you.  So as long as it's competitively priced I'd recommend it.That is all.

i wish i could find these in my local grocery - they're that good!i love blueberries and this bar combines a satisfying bit of inner sweetness with a crispy exterior - a win!and at 100 calories per bar, this is a good snack for my regime

column9: Lighter Alternative to a Pop Tart
column10: At 100 calories, The Crispy Oat Cookie Bar is good for a snack. They are small-a little more than half the size of a toaster pastry--but tasty. The crust is crunchier than a Pop Tart, more cookie like, with a sprinkling of oatmeal. The filling is just like a toaster pastry, which makes them very yummy. They were gone pretty quickly in my house. These are ideal for portion control snacking, just throw one in your lunch bag. However, they wouldn't make a good breakfast for anyone other than a toddler, since they are rather small to fill you up.

I enjoy eating breakfast bars when I'm in a rush and want something light.  Unfortunately, this Quaker Stila Bar did not live up to my expectations.  The center is blueberry flavored, but I did not get a strong blueberry flavor (it instead had a purely artificial flavor).  I didn't care for the texture either (if you want something crispy, I recommend Special K Fruit Crisps, Blueberry, 10-Count Bars (Pack of 6)).The nutrition does not make up for the mediocre taste.  It's only 100 calories per bar, which isn't bad at all, but there are only 2 grams of protein and 2 grams of fiber.  From my breakfast bar, I'd prefer a bar with more fiber and/or protein, to ensure I don't get hungry quickly.

column9: Good if you like cereal bars and crunchy things
column10: This is similar to the common fruit-filled cereal bars you find in the grocery stores, the difference being instead of the bar being soft, it's crunchy. The fruit filling is sandwiched between two cracker-like halves. That's the main selling point: the crunch. Taste-wise it's exactly like the soft cereal bars--I didn't notice a difference.The downside to being crunchy is it is more prone to making crumbs, although I never had a problem with large pieces of cracker falling off, as the filling helps keep it all stuck together.

column9: Nice taste - just a little dry ...
column10: I received this product for review through the Amazon Vine Program. I am a big fan of anything blueberry and while the taste of the cookie bar was very good it just seemed a little dry. Still all in all a good snack for a low calorie diet.

column9: A Delicious and Interesting addition to the snack bar world
column10: These bars are crunchy and not soft like many others which is their key differentiating factor.  The crumble apart approach seemed to give this a more substantial feel than other bars as I crunched through them.  Nice flavor in that they are not too sweet, but sweet enough.  I love the fact that they are simple and straightforward with 100 calories.  You can eat these relatively guilt free and they were excellent for me when going out the door in the morning to get something in my stomach on the way to work and eat while driving.  A really nice addition to the sometimes bland snack bar world.  Highly recommended!
At only 100 calories this treat is quite the surprise.  Crunchy with a fruit center.  You can eat almost 3 for the comparative calories in a Snickers.

I am a big fan of cereal bars and use them as a snack or meal supplements all the time. Most of them are a nutritious and tasty alternative to the more caloric snacks and candy bars, and I genuinely enjoy their taste. These blueberry cookie bars are no exception. Overall I like their taste, although they are not my favorites. The outer cookie layer is a bit too dry for my liking, while the fruity part is a bit too mushy. The overall texture of this bar is similar to the untoasted pop-tart. One thing that I like about these bars is that they are very low calorie and nutritious - only 100 calories, 1.5 g fats and 0.5 g saturated fat. So if eating (relatively) healthily is one of your primary concerns then these cookie bars have a lot going for them.

Quaker blueberry stila-good for a snack or breakfast.  I received this product and I was impressed with the packaging-a cute box that is a slanted rectangle.  The product is obviously packaged for women, who think neat product packages are great and thus more marketable.  The lack of calories also makes it a product likely to appeal to women-per bar, it is only 100 calories.Taste is another matter.  The product states it is naturally and artificially flavored.  The oat cookie bar is utterly tasteless-the only thing that saves this bar is the fact that it has blueberry filling in it.  In order to save calories however, there really is not enough blueberry filling to mask the tastelessness of the oat bar.  The blueberry filling also tastes artificial, and like the filling of a blueberry poptart rather than a "health" bar, that has 0 trans fat.Overall, if possible I would give this 3.5 stars, due to the low calorie and the low sugar content of the food.  However this is not a product I would buy-when I try to be healthy, I eat plan yogurt or plan oatmeal.  I think the purpose of this bar is the convenience of it-you can just open it anywhere and eat, such as at your office or in your car.  For me though I think I will prepare breakfast food from now on, as I simply do not find breakfast bars satisfying.

column9: At 100 calories each, they are an OK nice snack. I won't buy them again though.
column10: This snack is somewhere between a fig newton (filling on the inside), a granola bar (crunchy and easy to carry) and a cookie (sweeter than most granola bars). I received one box and used them as an afternoon snack.the pros: One hundred calories. Fairly tasty. Portable. Better tasting than a lot of other 'low calorie' snacks.the cons: Some artificial flavorings. Fairly heavily processed. Mostly carbs, which is a concern for me.I'll probably stick with protein or Zone Diet bars as an afternoon snack going forward. The Quaker Stila bars are tastier but the others I mentioned are better for my overall nutritional needs.

I like the taste of these.  They are soft on the inside and crispy on the outside. They are delicious at only one hundred calories and I can't say that about many other snacks. They come individually wrapped and I like to throw a couple into my purse for sudden hunger pangs after my gym workout.They are made with real blueberries and have none of the artificial taste some other snack products can have. They are very filling. I have been using this as my one snack of the day that doesn't involve fruit or other natural foods. If I need something fast each day, usually late afternoon, one of these takes care of me.Here are the nutritional facts from the side of the box for one box:Calories from Fat 15%daily valueTotal Fat 1.5gSaturated Fat 0.5g3%Trans Fat 0gCholesterol 0mgSodium 115mg5%Total Carbohydrate 18g6%Dietary Fiber 2g8%Sugars 8gProtein 2gVitamin A0%Vitamin C0%Calcium 0%Iron2%Folate2%Now for the bad part.I will not continue to buy these, as tasty and convenient as they are, due to the fact that they contain high fructose corn syrup which is an ingredient I try to avoid.Studies have linked it to type II diabetes. I also try to avoid palm oil, another unhealthy ingredient in these. I will throw an apple in my purse for a snack from now on.

column9: High Fructose Corn Syrup - and other problems
column10: I trusted the Quaker Oats Company to bring me a wholesome, safe snack. So as soon as I received the box of "Stila, crispy oat cookie bar with fruit filling" I pulled out a blueberry cookie bar and devoured it. It had a nice ratio of crunch to sweet filling and I thought it would be a good snack to keep on hand. It wasn't until a few minutes later, when I started to feel really bad, that I actually read the box in greater detail.The first item listed in the blueberry filling was high fructose corn syrup - not blueberries. Additionally, there was modified corn starch, sorbitol, palm oil, and a host of not very healthy ingredients. Further down the list (after canola oil and wheat gluten,) I found another listing of high fructose corn syrup - stuff so bad, they don't allow it to be sold in other civilized countries, like Germany.With ingredients this bad, I wondered how even the USA would allow it to be marketed. Then I noticed it was made in Mexico - distributed by Quaker in the USA. The ultimate two-time corporate sellout - make it with cheap poisonous ingredients and pay (cheaply, no doubt) for it to be made in another country. Shame on you, Quaker Oats Company!

column9: Crispy Tasty low cal pastry bar!
column10: I first tried these because they were on special at less than a dollar for a box of 6 with on pkg coupon. I chose the apple cinnamon. At first i was unsure if i liked them or not but after i got past the fact that they are not the over the top sugary sweet granola type bar that hurts your teeth from all the sugar i liked them more and more. A week later i decided to search them out and try a different flavor. I found them and they were still very reasonably priced even though not on sale. About half the price of a similar sized box of granola bars or other breakfast or cereal bars. I bought both blueberry and strawberry.  I love the blueberry. I agree with the reviews comparing it to an adult pop tart.  To those who find this a negative comment, many of us still love pop tarts but don't eat them because of the high calorie count. Numerous other comments claimed they were 'tasteless and bland' and they would rather eat plain oatmeal or plain yogurt!  What is more tasteless and bland than plain oatmeal or plain yogurt???  Several other comments recommended just eating a real pop tart but only eat half, or to only eat part of a granola bar for the same calories...seriously???  How many of you out there that have weight problems can honestly eat half of anything and save the rest for later?? If we could, we wouldn't be overweight.  Most of us have trouble stopping at one bar!  If you would rather eat an apple or carrot sticks why even try these? On the other hand if you are watching your calories and need a sweet treat to keep you out of the cookie jar or vending machine at work, these are an excellent option if you prefer a lightly sweet crispy treat. If at first they don't seem sweet enough, give them another chance.  Once you get used to not having the overpowering sweetness of granola bars you will love these!Oh, one more comment on the manufacturing of these bars in Mexico. Consider that maybe these bars were originally produced for customers in Mexico and their popularity prompted Quaker to try them out in the US? Many popular products now consumed in the US originally were produced and sold soley in other countries and when their popularity grew, they eventually found their way to the US.  Swiss chocolates, Mexican salsas, French pastries, Italian pasta & sauces etc.To sum it all up, these are very tasty, crispy, low cal snack bars. Very reasonably priced at about 1/2 the cost for a similar size pkg of other bars. (compare to kelloggs special k pastry bars. You get 2 for the same amt of calories but they are super thin and not as crunchy or hearty as Stila bars) Overall 4 enthusiastic stars!  I would give 5 stars if they had more flavors and stevia based sweeteners instead of hf corn syrup and sugar.

Have you ever gotten a jelly filled donut only to discover after biting into it that all the jelly got squished out somewhere along the way? That's hat Stila bars taste like. Except there's no doughy, sugary outside to enjoy. Just brittle, grainy, stale cracker that needs to be washed down with a quart of milk because it takes days to get the metallic aftertaste of artificial sweetner out of your mouth. There's some kind of fruit paste clotted on the bottom of the thing, but you can't taste it over the sugar-free pop-tart "oat" bar surrounding it. Bleh. Can I have a diet, caffeine free, low-sugar, non-flavored rice cake instead?

column9: Good concept, but where is the filling?
column10: Stila is a toasted crunchy cookie type bar with rolled oaks sprinkled on the top. I really like it because of the crunch factor, and also because it is not overly sweet. However, the first ingredient is the filling and high fructose corn syrup. There are also several artificial ingredients, including blue dye.  It has somewhat of a biscuit flavor, which I like. I would have given Stila four stars except for the fact that Quaker really skimped on the filling, leaving it very dry and lacking in blueberry flavor. In fact Stila's "blueberry" flavor is barely detectable.  The word "filling" in my mind has a connotation of being a significant component like a turnover or pie filling.  Stila's so called "filling" does not qualify.  Still I like Stila mainly for the texture and even thought it lacks the "wow factor" I may try it again sometime. Quaker don't be so stingy with the "filling," and what the heck does Stila mean anyway?

There are so many snack foods out there and so many promises with each one.  It is often dificult to find one that isn't too heavy on what you should not eat, yet have some satisfaction in taste.  We found these snacks to be pretty good.  The cracker part was okay, a little flakie perhaps but its flavor wasn't too bad.  The blueberry filling was very tasty so that to us over road the cracker part. Not bad at 100 cal for one, because one seems to quanch the urge to nibble.  We liked them. I'm sure we will purchase them.

When trying these my wife and I both came the consensus that this is basically a pre-toasted pop tart, but about half the size.We don't have anything against pop-tarts (we quite like a few flavors), but were we to want a pop-tart, we would've just gotten them.Definitely not impressed with the taste, texture, or value of these cookie bars.

This cookie bar is okay - if you prefer your healthy snacks on the sweet side.The outside is cruncy and crumbly (eat over a plate) and doesn't taste too bad.  The inside is a creamy blueberry concoction that reminded me of eating a cold, blueberry Pop-Tart. Which is not something I would recommend.It appears to only be 100 calories with a carb count of 18. There are better options than this one out there.

column9: Stick with fruit or another healthy snack
column10: I liked the blueberry flavor of these cracker bars, but the cracker itself is somewhat bland and way too crumbly.Pros:Good taste like a mini Pop TartOnly 100 caloriesZero transfatsConvenient sizeCons:Expensive packaging that is wastefulToo expensive for what you getMade in Mexico...sad for QuakerToo much sugar (first filling ingredient is high fructose corn syrup)Too many chemicals and additivesCrumbling, dry cracker is messy

column9: A good company making a bad product
column10: I was ready to give these bars a middling review based on taste, until I read the ingredients.  That was the end for me, but I'll come back to that later.The first thing I noticed is that the crust around the fruit filling resembles a pop tart.  Not my idea of a quality product I'd want to imitate.  The crust is dry with not much flavor except sweetness.  The filling is even more disappointing  - also dry, thin and not really tasting of blueberry at all, but also sweet.  So, OK, the flavor is mediocre at best.  But, if you want a portable sweet snack, I thought these bars might be acceptable in limited quantity.But then I looked at the ingredients and it was all over.  What are the FIRST TWO ingredients?  high fructose corn syrup and sugar.  Well, that accounts for the sweetness without much other flavor.So the bottom line is:  Poor flavor and hazardous to your health.  It doesn't get much worse than that.Zero stars if I could, but, in Amazon's system, one star is what I give.

column9: nice texture but flavor and ingredients seem like graduating from pop-tarts
column10: A pleasingly crisp exterior conceals a thin layer of oversweet filling.  The ingredients list explains why: High Fructose corn syrup shows up twice, as does regular sugar and brown sugar.  The taste/texture combo made me think of an adult version of pop-tarts.I'm a fan of natural foods (and minimalism in processed foods), so the long list of artificial ingredients in these bars is major turn-off.  Considering HFCS's reputation, why not use regular corn syrup?  FDC Red #40, why?? And there's a laundry list of preservatives as well.  Especially off-putting considering that the marketing and packaging both seem to trumpet the food's wholesomeness.Portability might be a plus, except the GF commented on how the bar crumbled as she ate it in the car, leaving crumbs all over her lap.  Why not a thicker layer of natural fruit preserves (much like Stonewall Kitchens preserves are made of all natural ingredients), to make this actually fruity and wholesome?Recommended for coaxing people off pop-tarts, but those of you who already enjoy "adult" food will not be impressed.  I won't repeat.

These bars are quite tasty and a little crumbly. If you factor in the weight to calorie ratio, they are about the same,(ratio wise),to Nature Valley bars. The Amazon or Quaker description says 5.5 ozs. However each bar is only 0.91 ozs. The whole package of 6 weigh 5.5 oz. But I did give them 4 stars on taste because of my particular fondness for anything blueberry. One would have to check pricing per ounce with other brands for the value conscious.

column9: 5 Stars on Taste and Texture, 4 on Good Health
column10: Wow, these went fast in my household. Everybody loved them. They are quite delicious and their crispy/chewy textures really make for a nicely sized snack. I think we have a new favorite snack bar. Everyone can't wait to try some other flavors.If you like fruit filled bars, then you aught to really try these. They are really good.

These Quaker Stila Crispy Oat Bars are delicious.  The perfect cross between a cookie and your traditional nutri grain style granola bar, they are a great snack.  We have been watching our diets recently, and these seem to be a better choice than many other granola bars--with only 100 calories (about 30 less than what we normally eat) and they don't seem any less filling.

I was pleasantly surprised at how these 100 calorie bars tasted.  I've tried a lot of whole grain cardboard tasting health snacks, and these are some of the first that had good taste, and low calories, while not making me feel I was eating something mixed with sawdust.The berry filling is fine -no complaints, but what really sets this apart is the crunch you get when biting into it.I'm tired of eating oat bars that are soft, or that have to have 300 calories of chocolate or sugar to get you to eat it.  This bar has neither, but still tastes pretty good.Recommended.

These bars arrived on not only my one day off, but a day I planned on spending at the beach. Perfect way to really give these a trial by fire and see how they performed in a high calorie burning day. We were gone all day: hiking, swimming, sunning and playing frisbee; by 3:00 p.m. the box was empty! LOL I read in other reviews that people were disappointed that the "filling" wasn't "filling" or "filled" to the level they thought it should be. When my family ate these, we throught they were like Fig Newtons, where you have a very cooked jam sandwiched between two crunchy layers, NOT a Hostess Fruit Pie, which is what I think some reviewers wanted. For an "On the Go" snack, these held up beautifully. The temps that day were 98 degrees, 112 degrees on the actual sand. They didn't melt or stick and eaten with a thermo cup of fresh lemonade, they were filling, tasty and delightful. Are they a 400 calorie blueberry muffin with streusal topping? Heck no! They're a portion and calorie controlled snack meant to take the edge off of your hunger so you don't go mental at Dunkin Donuts. ~snort~  All in all, my family enjoyed them and wondered what other flavours would be available to buy.**And as other's have asked: "What the heck is a Stila????" I know there's a good pun in there somewhere. ;)

When I first saw these I was expecting them to taste and feel like a bunch of Fig Newton's together and smooched down.  The Quaker Stila Cookie Bars turned out to be a bit crunchier than I expected somewhere in-between a Fig Newton and a cracker, but much closer than the cracker.  Since it is crunchy, you are going to have a few crumbs, but the blueberry center does make this a decent snack.

column9: Good taste but dry and hard
column10: I know they're supposed to be cookie bars, but even hard cookies are a bit easier to chew than these are. Also, the fact that they are hard and very dry does not make them cookies. They taste good and the filling kind of reminds me of that in Pop Tarts, except that these don't hurt my stomach like Pop Tarts do. They're sweet but it isn't over the top. A little moisture would make these bars much more agreeable.

column9: A great mid-morning or mid-afternoon snack
column10: This "cookie bar" reminds me of a thin strudel. It is soft, but somewhat crisp, with a flaky consistency. I find it just sweet enough to satisfy my sweet tooth.The blueberry filling is good -- it isn't very moist or gooey, like a jam. It tastes like blueberries and isn't unnaturally sweet or blueberry.From a nutritional perspective, this is perfect for me. Each bar is 100 calories. Fat is extremely low at only 1.5g. Sodium is a little high at 115mg (5% average daily value). Dietary fiber is a good 2g (8% of average daily value).In general, I like these with either my mid-morning coffee or my mid-afternoon tea. They are a good compliment with either. It's the perfect pastry-like treat without all the calories of a traditional pastry.

These bars are crunchier than I expected. With the soft fruit filling, the cookie bar is definitely crisp.  I thought that the filling has a nice blueberry flavor, but could be a little less sweet.  The cookie part could benefit from some oats, other than just the ones in the topping.  Pleasant and tasty enough, but could be a little more substantial.  I suppose for 100 calories, they have to be a bit lighter, so pretty good.

column9: Very tasty, crispy, and the blueberry jam is good, too!
column10: OK. Now these I like! Individually wrapped, very good insides, crispy outsides, not too sweet, not too crunchy... just good stuff! These lend themselves to lunches, though I've been eating one about a half-hour after I've put in my daily workout. Very good.ADDED after reading other reviews: I do not find these dry at all, and the filling is just the right amount for my taste. The tops do seem to be collapsed a bit, but what the heck? In you mouth they collapse all the way!Ho, and if you want to know what a dry cookie is, try Quaker Soft Baked Oatmeal Cookie, Raisins, 8.8-Ounce (Pack of 12). Those will dry you up like the Sahara!

****You have to take this product, Quaker Stila Crispy Oat Cookie Bar - Blueberry, 5.5-Ounce (Pack of 6), for what it is.  It is not a Pop-Tart, which is bigger and more thoroughly filled with the fruit-like substance these two food-chunks offer.The product under review is airy, more like a small Nerf ball than a large marble, although it is in no way spherical or useful in any games.  I was surprised that the filling did not fill the shell.Because the filling does not fill much of the shell much of the shell does not abut anything that's more liquid than solid, like blueberry jam compared to blueberry paste.****CRUMBLYBecause of that much of the shell is so dry that when you take a bite of the top of it it tends to crumble rather than tear, more like a potato chip than a potao knish.Now, I'm not saying that the typical consumer of this product cannot eventually figure out the exact measures necessary to figuring out how to eat it without spilling crumbles but I am saying there's a reason you don't see the manufacturer, Quaker, bragging all the time on how many thousands of these bars they have shipped to the International Space Station over the years where I'm pretty sure weigthlessness and the susceptibility to encroachement by crumbits into the various electronic and mechanical devices is considered more dangerous than that same degree of encroachment in the backseat of your car.Or even the front seat.****PACKAGINGThe package of my Quaker Stila Crispy Oat Cookie Bar - Blueberry, 5.5-Ounce (Pack of 6) is interesting.  When viewed from above, the shape is not a rectangle as you would expect.  Said another way, the horizontal cross-section of the box of almost every such product, and literally millions of others, is a rectangle whereas the cross-section of this box is a parallelogram, i.e., the opposite sides are parallel but the corners are not square.Below is my best representation of a parallelogram, where you should observe the only the stars and not the dots, but it might not turn out right in the final version of this Amazon review.  If it doesn't ignore it.**********.*...............*..*...............*...*...............*....**********This is interesting because the curious mind wants to know why this package is different from so many others.  There must be a reason the experienced and highly paid people at Quaker made such an unusual decision.
