It's certainly not a treat you can give them and turn your back.I much prefer treats that they can totally eat, and I can't see this "rollerball" treat being very popular with pet owners.

Length:: 0:22 MinsI selected this item thinking I would try it out on my parents dogs, but when my husband saw it on the counter, he wanted to try it with Kitty. Ha! She hates everything; there is no way she is going to like this stuff. I was wrong. To my total and utter shock, my cat actually liked it. So, here's the video to prove it.

column9: I'm not sure what to think . . . and neither does my dog
column10: I was surprised when opening the package this product came in and found this "Lickety Stik" device.  It looks like a bottle of roll-on deodorant and that's how it works.  My first dog liked it and figured out she is supposed to lick it, but my other dog wasn't sure what to do with it and wanted to chew it.  This is worrisome because if he got hold of it, he may turn it into a bunch of plastic slivers and I wouldn't want him swallowing those.The Lickety Stik treat is a new concept and I understand the idea, but I don't think it's quite there yet.  It's also a little unusual to stand there holding the pets' treat.  Usually, when giving a pet a treat, I expect to get a few minutes of peace and quiet while he/she is enjoying the treat. There are no directions on the bottle, so I wasn't sure how to use it at first, but it didn't take long to figure out.  You just hold it in front of the dog and they have to do the figuring.I probably won't be buying this again.

So, my dog likes it. I'll just get that out there right away.But, it's awkward to carry and can be messy (which I didn't think it would be) but since you have to sometimes give it a little encouragement to get anything to come out, sometimes it just decides "Oh you want ALL of it!" and I have a sticky snouted puppy.And, she has since lost interest in it and prefers treats she can smell better.

I can understand this might not be for every dog;  my mother's dog just tried to eat the whole roll-on.  But my dog has no issue with it at all and loves it.  I taught her to recycle using this, and she goes out of her way to find stuff to recycle so she can get some.  It's like feeding a baby lamb out of a bottle.  If you have trouble getting the stuff to come out, squeeze it a little because that gets a little more on the roller ball, maybe that will encourage them to just lick and not chew.  My dog even has fun selecting which flavor we're going to open next.

I decided to try this out after seeing an ad in a Bass Pro Shops catalog. I have two chihuahuas. One of them loved it and could probably lick it all day. The other dog wouldn't go near it. All in all, I think it really just depends on the dog itself; hence the mixed reviews here. It's not a bad product by any means, but probably not something I'll be buying often - just more of a fun treat every so often.

I was resorting to the old trainer's trick of smearing peanut butter on the fridge or a plastic stool, so my new rescue dog could happily lick it off while I brushed him. It worked but it was very messy. Lickety Stik works much better, although I do generally need a helper to hold it while I groom. The big test will come when I next take him to the vet and bring LS along--will it work the same while he's getting his temperature taken? Or will the experience of the thermometer ruin the treat for him? If the former, I'm sure all the vets and techs at our clinic will be ordering this stuff! I was a little concerned with the stuff upsetting my dogs' digestive systems: the new guy has an  iron gut it seems but my other dog has a sensitive tummy. She, however, had some (inserted herself while I was grooming the newbie) and was o.k. We were using liver flavor. Overall, I'm very impressed so far and ordering some more.

This product should have more explicit warnings on the packaging. My husband and I bought this as a treat for our 55 lb Doberman/Boxer mix. He loved the flavor and it served as a great distraction if we wanted to clean his ears or trim his dew claws. Unfortunately, with one swift bite he popped the roller ball into his mouth and down his throat. We needed to rush him to the emergency room where they induced vomiting and then monitored closely for 2 days at home until he threw it up on his own .... After surfing the internet we found numerous other claims with people having the same issue- some even needing to spend a few thousand on procedures to remove the ball.  Additionally, customer service for this company was a HUGE disappointment.  They were unshmpathetic and kept on about how it was not meant for chewing.

I was recommended this for my 15 pound rescue dog and her ongoing training.I initially loved the product...till she clamped down on the neck of the bottle sending the small down (roller) down her throat...I was very very lucky as I administered Peroxide immediately and she brought back up after 5 minutes...but please be aware that this can be dangerous

column9: my pets LOVE this -- great treat !
column10: I think the packaging is ingenious -- who would have thought to put great meat juices into what looks like a bottle of roll on deodorant!YAAAA -- 10 points for ingenuity !  And the dogs love licking the little roller.If only it was re-fillable !
My 2 dogs love licking the treat and I don't feel guilty about too many treat.Excellent to practice commands.

Lickety Stik lickable pet treat from PetSafe are a hit at my house. My dog gets excitement every time I pulled it out.  It seems to be as good as a a moist treat without the sticky mess. A tidy rollerball dispenses all-natural liquid goodness --my dog just lap it up!All-natural flavors, naturally preservedOnly 1 calorie in every 10 licksOver 500 licks per bottleNo mess roller-ballGreat for trainingConveniently fits in your pocket

I still carry regular treats in my pocket but this product is great. It is like a deodorant roll top. It is made in the USA and has only 1 calorie per 10 licks. So far my golden has liked all th e flavors. It is something different and when I am trying to keep his attention on me and not on a passing dog, I have it

column9: My Dogs will Do Anything for Lickety
column10: I bought this product hoping to find something that will help me when I am trying to brush my 3 Siberian Huskies.  Lickety works better than I expected, they will stand for 45 minutes to get brushed if I use this.  Huskies are picky in what they will eat, but this is like cat nip to them.

column9: A so-so reaction from our dog
column10: I guess the idea here is that you can reward your dog with quick and tasty lick of a thin liquid on a roller ball. Seems like a decent idea, especially if you're trying to train your dog.The problem, in our case anyway, is that our dog is sort of lukewarm on this treat. He'll lick it sometimes, but other times, he just isn't interested. I asked him why, but he declined to comment.

column9: A Nice Alternative to Dog Treats
column10: My dogs can pack on the pounds quickly especially during the winter month so I am always on the look for low calorie alternatives to dog treats that they can enjoy without gaining unwanted weight.  These Lickety Stiks are interesting to say the least.  Much like an ink pen, the dogs roll the ball with their tongues to get the flavored water out.  The package claims only one calorie per ten licks (and over 500 licks per bottle) so that is really nice.  The first couple times I tried on both my dogs, they would give I a sniff, then a couple licks because trying to grab it out of my hand with their mouths.  But after a couple uses they no like try to take it and lick.One major problem with the Lickety Stik, or at the very least the liver flavor is that the smell is extremely strong, which is a big problem because liver does not smell very well,  and gets stronger with every lick to the point it starts to make my eyes water and stinks up the entire room.  Also, after prolonged inactivity, the liquid solidifies on the ball making it harder if not impossible for the dogs to use, but that is easy to remedy with a little warm water.  Once, or if, you get past the smell, this is a good alternative to fatty dog treats.

I have a three month old pug puppy who is incredibly food motivated.  Carrying around treats on a walk while I'm leash training him can be a hassle to fish out without spilling the rest or getting crumbs in my pockets.  We received a free sample of Lickety Stik at our puppy training class because of a pug's tendency to pack on the pounds and I was really surprised at how quickly the puppy took to it.  He will do tricks and readily follow on the leash to get a lick of this treat and becomes excited when he sees the bottle.The main drawback to this thing is that it stinks to high heaven and if I get a strong whiff of it the thing makes me gag.  The dog loves it, however so I am really considering buying more of this product in the future.

I got the Lickety Stik through the Vine Program.  I was a little skeptical upon ordering.  I have two dogs that both need daily medications and they also get vitamins.  It was always a battle to get them to take either and had to revert to the shove down the throat and blow on the nose tactic.  That is until now.  Put a little of this stuff on whatever they need to take and wham gone down the throat.  It took about a week and then I stopped using it and the dogs now take their pills without any treatment.  Highly recommend and made my life a little easier.

I have been giving my dog this for several weeks as a treat and am not sure if she is really getting any juice or she just loves the smell. It is hard to tell if the ball is turning when she licks it or if it remains stationary. She always comes running when she sees me pull it out the pantry so I assume that she is still getting her 'treat'. I do like the size of the container, but wish that I could tell how much is remaining.

column9: Okay, but did not satisfy my dog
column10: I tried several times to get my jack russell terrier to use this treat, but he prefers chewing on something rather than licking his treats.  The only treat he has patience with licking is a little cup of  doggie ice cream.  Even ice cubes he will crunch instead of lick.  I was also a little bit bothered by the smell of the product; there was an oily odor to it.  This treat may work for little dogs or dogs who have more patience but sadly not my dog.  It is a good effor though.

This is a really fun idea! It is a fun treat to give them, and my dogs REALLY like it. The reason why I am giving it a low rating, is because it stinks, really bad! The smell is so offensive that my boyfriend won't let me feed this treat to my dogs while he's around. If my dogs didn't love the taste, and if it wasn't so much fun to feed to them, it would be in the garbage. I won't be buying it again, and don't recommend it. However, if you ever find it on sale or find a free sample or something, it is kind of a fun thing to try ONCE. Another issue is the fact that it comes in dark flavors, which can (and did) stain their mouths and cause dark tear stains.
Great training aid. Very easy to use.  My puppy will follow this Lickety Stik anywhere!  After a while, just shaking the container gets her running to me.

column9: Awesome. For training, not an a regular treat!
column10: Many of these reviews seemed to be confused. This Stik if really created and used for training dogs/puppies. It is much easy to give them a quick lick when they walk next to you instead of giving them lots of treats or clicks. This product is a god-send. My puppy loves it and walks much better on the leash as a result. Also, just because you dog doesn't like the taste doesn't mean this deserves a poor review. Dogs have different tastes! For what this does, it deserves a better rating.

This is great stuff!  I have a dog w/ no teeth and he could not have treats w/ the others.  Problem solved!  He LOVES this.  It's a bit messy but I've learned how to "administer" the treat w/ minimal dripping.  My others beg for it but I save this for my 19 y.o. toothless guy.  What a pleasure to be able to reward him too after potty call!

column9: Good but Not Good Enough for My Picky Dog
column10: Likety Stik is a great product for some dogs obviously, but Foxy, my ten-year-old standard poodle, is not interested. She first thought she was to take the entire container into her mouth. When I didn't give her the opportunity to try to swallow the whole thing, she tasted the juice on the ball. Deciding it was pretty good, she looked around to see if any other dogs might just have happened to come by for a visit. She is a picky eater. When she reacts by looking to see if any other dogs are around, it is evident that something is extra tasty. If she really, really likes something super tasty, she doesn't take the time to look around for other dogs. She has licked it a few times, but she seems somewhat reluctant. The low-calorie idea is neat, but my picky eater needs all the calories she can get.From a people's perspective it seems a good product, but no matter how much I shake it, I find it necessary to turn the ball manually to make the juice available. It would be fun to try this stick on a dog with more enthusiasm about food.Four stars.

column9: He likes it (and licks it) but sticky ball
column10: Our dog really likes this thing.  It smells like it is full of flavor, and he seems to really enjoy licking the thing for as long as I'll hold it for him.  If you are unfamiliar, the flavored juice in the container is released each time the dog licks a small ball at the tops of the container; as the ball spins, it gets covered in the juice, which the dog licks off, etc.  So, well done!  My one beef with the product, though, is that the ball is a little tough to get spinning until it is fully lubricated, which means that I often have to use my fingers to get it started, which isn't ideal because I don't want to get any of the flavored juice on me.  That said, my dog is a big fan of this product.  So, while I think this is a good product, I'm giving it four stars because I think the delivery mechanism (ie the ball) isn't the best, and could be improved upon.

column9: This is a great training aid
column10: My dog loves this and she has learned amny tricks fast.  The best part is that it doesn't put weight on her.  I use it all the time.  Highly recommned it as a traiing aid.

My dog is a bit shy about eating in front of people, so I should have known that he would not like these.  He didn't.  He looked at me like I was crazy.  I tried to make him try it, but he resisted and then I felt bad about doing it.One time during a bad storm he was hiding under my desk and he licked it and seemed to like it, but I haven't got him to do it since.I think the product is probably good - and there's a lot in it and it looks safe enough - it's like a deodorant roller ball - but my dog is just too shy.My cat liked it.  I wasn't sure how good it was for cats though so I didn't let her try it again.  They should make these for cats though - I had a cat that would lick her fur off, this would have been great to help divert her.It's a lot neater to keep in your pocket than regular treats.  It would be great for training a dog if you had a dog that would lick it.
Yes, this must be very good, all of the dogs loved it, and didn't want to stop licking it.  They lined up waiting their turn.  Would recommend as a treat.

My dogs seem to find Likety Stik extremely tasty as demonstrated by their desire to keep licking it. On my part, however, there are some reservations.  I have the liver flavor and for one, it is one of the worst smelling doggie treats that I have.  Not too sure if people want to carry this around in their purse. The stick works like a rollerball, like some of the anitperspirants you see out on market.  When you first open, it does not roll very easily, but eventually it will get going after your dog licks it a few times.  The second major reservation that I have is that if it is being licked, then the part my dog just licked cleaned, saliva and all, goes back into the fluid reservoir which doesn't seem too clean to me. Some may argue that this shouldn't make any difference to my dog who loves licking his hooha and whose favorite appetizer is cat poop, but I cannot help to think that this may be a festering ground for bacteria.  This may be prevented by having certain chemicals present that inhibit this possibility, but then it loops back to my concern of feeding these to my dog.  Although novel, I don't really see a benefit of having this as a treat other than the caloric count.

I got the savory chicken flavor for our dog, and he totally loves it. He'll perform any trick just to get some licks. It's easy to use and there's no mess. Great idea for a product! I plan to buy more!

At first the dogs were confused and the golden terrified. But once they sniffed it and figured out how to lick it, they loved it. I think it smells awful, nothing like bacon. But the dogs appreciated it. It is a great way to give the dogs a treat without all the calories. One calorie to every ten licks. Just be sure to store it out of reach. I can see my basset counter surfing, grabbing it, and chewing it all up.

I have 2 large dogs who I allow to lick this every day. They seem to like it.  It must smell and taste good to them.  I like giving this to them as a treat for doing something good instead of something with a higher calorie content.

column9: Product is awesome, watch the price here!!!!
column10: I tried this product on a new dog I had in training, because I liked the idea of a liquid for increased reward value.  It has turned out to be a great reward for many dogs I work with as well as a great reward in numerous situations.  In many performance sports you need to be very careful when rewarding your dog on a practice field that there are no crumbs left behind.  This product is PERFECT!!  I also don't need to worry about my pockets getting eaten out of my pants after training.My advice is to watch the price you pay here!!!!  I buy mine locally at less than 1/2 the price you see advertised here.  Even Petsafe will sell it to you for $8.99 not $13!!!Otherwise certainly a 5 star product!!!!!

We have two little dogs and they have shared the licks.  I can't speak to the taste, but I feel like I'm giving them puppy crack because they became very upset when I put the stick up.As a human, I'm a little less enthused about the whole thing.  First, it's more like a bottle of shoe shine than a bottle of deodorant.  So, as you turn it upside down, you have to squeeze the bottle a smidge to bring the liquid to the ball.  Squeeze too hard, and your dog will get a face full of Lickety Stik juice.  The dog doesn't mind, though.Both dogs started to try to chew the bottle.  They sort of got the hang of it, but I'm not sure that I'm giving them a life lesson here or anything.  It's certainly not worth the patience, for instance, used in showing a toddler how to drink from a straw.Still, as a novelty, I'm cool with this.  I really do think the dogs will get militant when the bottle runs out, though.  For all I know, it's just sugar water, but whatever it is, they really like it.

I love the idea of the Lickety Stik:  a dog treat without all the extra calories.  Unfortunately, the design of this product makes it difficult to use.  The roller ball is very firmly fitted into the top so that it doesn't really roll.  It's mostly stuck in one position unless I manipulate it with my fingers (which are then covered in a strongly-smelling liquid that is difficult to wash off).  My two dogs quickly figured out what to do with this "treat", and they will lick and lick, but nothing comes out unless I either (1) squeeze the bottle to force the liquid out (which then usually drips onto the floor) or (2) move the roller ball with my fingers.Overall, this is a great concept that needs a little tweaking in the execution.

I have my Min-Pin boarded at the home of a friend who has what looks like a Westie. I took the bottle of "Lickety Stik" over when I went to pick up my dog. Offered it to both dogs. The westie loved it, however my Min-Pin would have nothing to do with it. Maybe that's because another dog licked it, however that's doubtful as most dog I've met aren't that fussy. Its kind of a cool idea but I think a dog biscuit works just as well. One other caveat, it looks like the same bottle that roll-on deodorant comes in so make sure you know for sure what you're smearing on your arm-pits or you could attract some unwanted attention

The five stars are from Panda the Puppy.  This thing smells horrible, and looks disgusting, but the puppy loves it. He loves it so much that I can tolerate the horrible smell for him.  Panda loves treats, like most puppies, but this treat in particular gets his attention. It is working as a great training aid too.  He sits, he licks.  It is a treat that he is motivated to work for, and it makes training easier. We do have other treats that work, but this one has the benefit of a fast grab. I don't have to dig in a bag or really search for it.

This is like a deodorant bottle with gravy in it.  My dogs took to it right away and did every trick as if I had a chunk of steak in my hands.  I figure it's a lot cheaper than conventional treats and not as messy as wet ones.  You do have to squeeze the fluid out sometimes so if they aren't ready for it, it drips.  If you aren't over a rug or other cloth surface it's not a problem, because they'll lick it off the floor.  I do have to keep it out of reach when I'm not using it because I'm afraid they'd jump up when I'm not looking and run off with it for me to discover it all chewed up with a stained carpet under it!

My dog was pretty confused when I put this in his face. Whenever I do he'll lick it once or twice then step back and look at me like, "Can I have a real treat now?" At least he doesn't hate it, but he sure doesn't get excited about this whenever I pull it out.But don't go off my review alone, other dogs seem to like it. Just not my poodle.

column9: Move Over Ban Roll On Deoderant:  lol  Here is Lickety Stik!
column10: OK, so my dog loves this and she is a picky eater.  I literally had to force her mouth open and give a roll of it on her tongue and she has been hooked ever since.  I usually only give her high quality treats and chews but I figure a few licks of this roll on won't her her.  I don't think I will buy it because it really is not a healthy treat for her but since she likes it and it does not make a mess I gave it 4 stars.  If it was better nutritionally I would have given it 5 stars.  This is definitely a great concept!  I just wish is contained better ingredients.  : )

This is the most unique dog treat I've seen. The liquid treat is dispensed from a container that reminds me of a large lip gloss tube with a roller. I've given this unique dog treat "4 stars" instead of five as an average based on the varied reactions from my two small dogs. The smaller Malti-poo loved the treat and from his reaction would give it "5 stars". He immediately licked the roller, received the treat, and wanted more. Our Cavalier King Charles Spaniel is a pickier eater in general and wouldn't even try it at first. He finally did, but didn't seem to like it. We have the chicken flavor and it may be he just didn't like the flavor.Since our Malti-poo likes it so much, I have just ordered the three-pack that has chicken, liver, and bacon flavors. The three-pack is a better value than the individual packs and I'm hoping our Cavalier will like one of the other flavors better than the chicken. This is a unique idea to reward dogs with a treat without filling them up like traditional dog treats.** Update:  I ordered the three-pack and my Cavalier definitely likes the bacon flavor much better than chicken!

I came across this PetSafe Lickety Stik and decided to give it a try.  We just got an 8 week old Bassett Hound puppy and decided to try out this Lickety Stik as a training reward due to its low calorie content.  Bassets are know to get fat quick so a low calorie reward is needed as Bassetts basically only respond to food.Basically, this thing has the same construction as a stick of roll-on deodorant.  You turn it upside down, the liquid inside saturates the ball in a second or so and your dog takes a lick or two of the ball.  It works fantastically for training a puppy or dog.  We got the bacon flavor and she absolutely loves it.The puppy loves it and will do anything to get a lick of this thing.  It smells terrible to us(a really disguisting rancid bacon odor)but she absolutely adores it.  The price of $8 may seem a little high, but we've have been using the same Stik for over a month now, numerous times each day and we still have a third of it left.  We will definitely be buying more of these.Lickety Stik is a fantastic product that is great for training or just a treat.  Highly recommended!

column9: Good idea for certain dogs/needs, but...
column10: As other reviewers have mentioned, this looks like a bottle of roll-on deodorant. It's not quite what I was expecting. You have to squeeze it a little to get the liquid to flow, and then the dog can lick at the roller ball, similarly to how a hamster would drink from its water bottle. It works well enough, and my dog likes the taste okay. It seems to bother her that she can't chew on it, and it bothers me that I can't just hand it to her and let her go to town on it. Yes, it's convenient and non-messy to carry around. For my dog, the low-calorie aspect isn't necessarily a good thing. For example, when I take her on a hike, she runs around like crazy, so I actually want her to get some calories from her treats. The other times I give her treats, I'm usually giving her something chewy that will help remove dental plaque. So overall, this isn't a great option for my particular dog. If your dog has a weight problem and you like to give it treats, this is probably a good alternative for you. This isn't something that I'll purchase again myself.

column9: Just don't set it next to your roll-on deodorant... :)
column10: Imagine doggie treat flavored underarm deodorant.... have to squeeze just a bit to get the roller wet, then turn upside down and let the dog lick it. Unique idea.  Would probably be useful as a training tool. Our dog definitely likes it.  I imagine this works best as a daily treat. I shudder to think what would happen if you let the roller dry out, dog ends up with a tounge rash trying to push the roller past the dried out spot... or worse, squeeze to hard and drip doggie treat juice all over!! I'm just saying...  :)All in all, worth a try for the dog that has everything or just needs a change of taste...All the best,Jay

column4: Sarah Vigil Swiger "Author of The Divine Plan"
column9: One out of two dogs love this stinky treat!
column10: I have two dogs, one Black Labrador and one Chihuahua.  The Lab can't get enough of this stinky treat and even tries to grab it from me with her teeth.  She will lick on it all day if I let her. The Chihuahua sniffs it and snubs it. She couldn't be less interested. So, one out of two dogs loves this stinky treat.  Humans, on the otherhand, hate the strong smell.  I think it's fun and can imagine it is a great treat substitute for obese dogs who need to watch their calorie intake. If you aren't adverse to strong odors you'll love the handiness of this Lickety Stik!

Like other reviewers have said, this may take a short time for your dog to get used to. The dog learns to lick the roller ball and get to the juices. This may not be as satisfying a treat as doggy biscuits, but I can see this product being useful for training. For instance, if your dog pulls on the leash when you go for walks, stop and call the dog to you. If he listens, let him have a few licks before continuing. I can also see it being useful for dogs who are overweight and whose owners want to cut back on calories yet can still give the dog a little treat for good behavior.

I am only reviewing the Bacon flavor, but my dogs picked up on how this works pretty quickly and love the taste of it.  At first they wanted to bite the bottle and chew it like a treat but I worked with them for about a minute or so and they got down that you only lick it.  I have 3 dogs and all three of them liked the taste of it.  I like it because it seems like a more personal treat than just a dog biscuit.  I recommend this!

column9: My Yorkies think it is yummy, but I think it is inconvenient
column10: Both of my finicky yorkies love this treat, but I don't!  It smells awful and I have to hold it for them to enjoy it, unlike other treats that I toss to them and let them enjoy while I enjoy a little peace and quiet.  Also, the liquid gets in their "beard" so the odor of the treat lingers even after I tuck the bottle back in the treat cupboard.  It is rare for both of my dogs to agree on a treat and it is fun to watch them enjoy it, but it is inconvenient.  I will not likely repurchase this.

I am of the curious sort when it comes to dog treats and new ways to reward dogs so I jumped at getting this product.Lickety Stick arrived and three dogs were eagerly sitting in front of me; a cocker spaniel, a norwegian elkhound, and an australian shepherd.I unwrapped the stick and squeezed a little juice out of the tube onto the roller. I presented it to all three dogs. The cocker spaniel and the aussie eagerly licked away. The aussie licked away so much the cocker needed a wet cloth over the top of her head due to dropping juice on her head. The elkhound however, wanted no part in it.After a couple days of using it and trying it out I am left with the premise that it's an interesting take on a a dog reward - but in the end, the execution and possibility of making a mess leave this treat stuck in the treat drawer. I don't see myself buying these in the future.

column9: A Little Weird, but my Yorkie LOVED it.
column10: I guess I didn't really read the description of this product very well, but this was not what I expected! It is like a little roller ball of deodorant only it is filled with liquid log treats. (this one is bacon) It was easy to open, but I did have to squeeze the bottle a little and then roll the ball around to get the initial liquid to come out. Once my dog realized what she was supposed to do, she was ALL OVER IT. In fact, she got so excited that she made her self sick. I'm saving this one for an "every now and then" treat.

column9: Not sure it's worth the trouble
column10: My little dog (a Shih Tzu) seemed to have trouble licking the rollerball consistently enough to fully enjoy the treat.  Her inclination was to try to bite the top - and I'm wondering if that's what most dogs would try to do.  Of course, a dog can't tell you in words if they like something - you have to go by behavior.  And when we took this away from our dog, she really didn't protest like she does when it is a favorite treat.The premise behind this product is interesting - and I can understand why the idea of a rollerball made sense.  I'm just not sure it all works together well enough.  I can't envision seeking this out and purchasing it for my pet.

column9: OK, maybe not so great for large dogs
column10: I tried this on my mom's dog while he went through his resume of tricks, but since his mouth is bigger than the Lickety Stik he kept trying to bite it.  He got annoyed after a few tricks when he realized I wasn't going to give it to him and wandered off to find my mom who was holding actual treats.

What a great idea for a treat.  Lickety Stik is constructed like a roll-on deodorant with a flavored dog treat inside.  Hold the Stik upside down and my dog licked away at it.  It is low calorie (great for my dog who is on a diet). It is also very easy to carry.  I keep it in my pocket.Since it has a cap and has plastic construction, it doesnt get crushed in my pocket. It makes a great little reward during training sessions.I find it especially helpful to reward my dog when Im teaching him a new trick. With the lickey stik he was very eager to see the stik come out.A few notes on the Lickety Stik's use.  The first time you use the Lickety stik, you may have to move the roller-ball with your fingers to get the treat to flow a little.  Once the dog understands that licking the ball makes the treat flow, it is not an issue. Also when he is done licking, there is no dripping.The Lickety Stik also has a clear window at the base of of the bottle so you know when it is time to reorder.The Lickety Stik is not large which makes it easy to trasport. However it does mean that if it is your primary treat for you dog, you may run out quickly.Overall, I can say that the dog was enthusiastic about the stick. It was easy to use. It was fun to give. I am happy with this product.

When I picked up the padded envelope from our mail basket, my cocker spaniel snapped to attention.  By the time I had the bottle out of the envelope, the Rottweiler had joined us.  Their anxiety grew as I struggled to break the plastic wrap around the top.  Finally I had the bottle ready for action, after a very long 30 seconds.I had to rub the roller ball to get the liquid inside to lubricate the ball.  Squeezing the bottle forces the liquid to ooze around the ball.  Both dogs wanted to eat the bottle rather than lick the ball.  They give it a five-star review and suggest that the Vine program send more to our house.The rottie still wants to eat the bottle. The cocker has learned the licking technique.  The cocker is quite responsive to the sound of the bottle being shaken. (Cockers are the original foodies.)The major problem I have is that the ball does not move freely.  I get some liquid on the ball and hold it out for the cocker.  She licks it very clean.  Then I have to squeeze more liquid out and roll the ball around with my thumb.The ingredients seem to be healthy, or as healthy as something with bacon fat in it can be.This product can be a great training reward, but you will have a sticky thumb. The first time I offered my thumb to be licked clean, the cocker started to eat it. If you are training your dog, you probably will want a rag to keep your thumb clean.My vine review philosophy is to first test the product without regard to price.  Now that I have checked the price, currently around $8, it seems a good value for a training tool.  $8 does not buy a decent size bag of training treats.  And the dogs are much more responsive to the bacon than to freeze-dried lumps.  However as just a treat for being a good dog in general, it is not as satisfying as a regular-sized biscuit.  Pity my poor dogs who are only getting this one bottle of bacon treat.

column9: Finally a treat both you and your dog can enjoy!
column10: First off, i would have to say that I did not find the Bacon flavor to be appealing at all.OK I'm kidding.  I didn't actually lick it.But my dog did, and she loves it.The basics:The container is like a roll-on antiperspirant.  If you use roll-on deodorant, and buy this product, you may accidentally sport a new aroma if you are particularly groggy in the morning.Its a no-calorie treat if your dog is ... uh... "easy to see" as they say.  My dog is a bit thick (like a barrel on stilts), so I had some high hopes for this product.The pros:My dog loves it.Its low calorie.No crumbs!The cons:You can't throw it in the laundry room as an easy way to get them to be put up.I had to hold it upside down, and it would drip.When my dog is aggressive she threatens to take it away from me.Overall, I would say that this is one of the few products that delivers exactly what it promises.  I recommend it.

For those that follow my reviews you know I have many dogs so I just had to try out this product.  It was so funny the day I received it. I was surrounded with furry friends. Incase you don't know dogs can smell just about anything and they knew something was in my hands that they were going to like.  The container reminds me of roll-on deodorant.  I know that sounds gross but nevertheless it did. It is made where the dogs lick the top of it to receive their treat.  Okay, now all I had to do was let the dogs lick it and believe me they were ready.  They piled around me and all took their turns, it was so cute.  Now, did they come back for more?  You bet they did, each seeing who could get their tongue on it first.  I could tell to them it was a tasty treat and for me it was a time to interact with my animals and show them love. You can't just let them play piggly wiggly and lick it all in one day, because they would, believe me. You have to allow only so many licks.  I liked this product and so did my dogs and plan to purchase it for them. Dog biscuits are of course a lot easier, you just throw them and they catch, but this is a special treat that allows you time with your animal. Nice product.

column9: Perfect for use while training your dog
column10: The Lickety Stik is fabulous!  My dog immediately took to it and gets so excited when he sees the bottle.  I have been trying to train him to fetch a ball and then give it back to me, but I have had to wrestle the ball away from him.  I was worried about giving him too many treats because of calories, not to mention the expense.  I started letting him lick the Stik once or twice each time I got the ball away from him.  It didn't take long before he would drop the ball when he saw the Stik, and now he puts it directly into my hand, just so he can lick the Stik. I plan on using it to train him to do other things, as well.Considering how many times I have used it, it is a good value for the money.  It's kind of awkward to give him as a regular dog treat, so I save it for training and give him dog biscuits or other treat.

First of all, let me say that my dog likes the taste of this treat - a lot. However, I have a large dog...and evidently an impatient dog. Rather than lick this "roll-on" treat, she would rather just bite it and chew it. That's really the only down side. Found out my daughters kitten liked it too. It's weird, like a 1980's deodorant company trying to do something profitable with their out of date product line. I wouldn't buy it, but my pets liked it.

It's a good idea, but my dog did not get it at all.  It's design is like a roll on deoderant - the ball inside moves while licked putting more of the liquid flavor onto the ball and into the dogs mouth.  You can ration how much the dog licks and put the lid back on.The smell wasn't strong unless you put your nose on it for a big whiff.  It must have smelled good to my dog because she went nuts over it.  The problem was it was too small and she kept bitting it and trying to yank it from my hand.  Then later when I was gone - she got it off the counter and chewed through it.  Yes, I know - she wasn't well behaved with it.  BUT she couldn't resist the temptation and after I had let her lick it I guess she figured it was fair game.Overall - I believe it's made for a little dogs but I didn't know that when I got it.

column9: The Dog loved it, I didn't
column10: Well, when I ordered this I wasn't quite sure what to expect, but it sure wasn't a roll on deodorant container filled with stinky liver flavored liquid.  For me personally, I've always stood by the belief that while the dogs are the one enjoying the dog toys and treats, the are more made for the humans than anything else and there is something totally repugnant about a dog eating from a deodorant container.Jilly, my puppy, loved it.  She kept on trying to take it out of my hand and bite at the container until she realized she had to lick but she did love the flavor.  The only real negative is that Jilly got "liver breath."  Also the ball in the container didn't spin and I had to squeeze and I got a drip or two on the floor.  I have wood floors so no harm no foul, but if you have carpeting you might get a stain, but Jilly helped with the clean up.But I couldn't quite get over the container and even though Jilly loved it the doggy breath and the fact I didn't like her licking a deodorant container was a big turn off.  Plus, if I used roll on deodorant I won't want my dog to associate it with treats, in case she got in the bathroom and ate the real deodorant which I'm sure could make her very sick.3 Stars.UPDATE:  The cat found this on the table and started pawing at it, so I opened it for her so she could have a lick and she loves it more than the dog!

I was excited to get the Lickety Stik for my dogs. It sounds like a good idea BUT the roller part DOES NOT roll and in order for the dog to get something to taste you must squeeze the container which can be a mess. I have four dogs, as I dog train in obedience and in tracking. In the beginning all four were interested, but then they all became frustrated with it. I ended up with $25.00 of this garbage. SAVE YOR MONEY.it's not worth it!

I have three beagles and a lab.  To be honest, when I read about this product, I was dubious as to its ability to make them happy.  A lick?  That's it?Well--I was right, and wrong.When I first broke it out, the lab tried to eat it--he wasn't happy with the one lick.  The beagles saw him try to eat it, and then they were all about eating it, too.  But once they realized what it was all about, they LOVED it.  They were like crack addicts.  I put it on the dining room table, out of reach, and we kept catching them walking on their hind legs, noses over the table ledge, trying to get it.  They got so sneaky!  Climbing onto the chair?  Really?  When it was time for bed, when they usually get a cookie, they all ran to the table and gave me the distinct message--"WE want THAT!"Last night I put the Lickety Stik on a tall shelf in the hallway of the house--and this morning, they "knew" exactly where it was, and wouldn't leave the hallway until I grabbed the thing and walked them outside.So, we're calling it either crack for dogs or catnip for dogs haha..It's sort of like a roll-on deodorant style container.  The beef-gravy-like substance covers the ball and they simply lick it off.  Of course, as I said above, they will try to eat it at first, until they get the idea.  Although I'm convinced that should it get left within reach, they will eat the entire container.)It's a small container--about 5 inches long.  The picture made me think it would be much larger.

My two dogs apparently loved the scent and taste based on the way they were all over the Stik as soon as I uncapped it. The problem was the roller ball. It didn't roll very well. This became the pattern -- place thumb on ball, roll, let dogs lick off residue, place thumb on ball, roll again ... It became tedious very quickly. My main dog grew impatient and latched onto the bottle with his back teeth, easily piercing the neck allowing the flavored goo to ooze out. I tossed the Lickety Stik lickety split.

I bought this product because we originally thought our new puppy had a condition called megaesophagus which requires them to eat and stay in a vertical position for 30-45 minutes after eating and other people had recommended this product to keep the dog occupied during that time.We later found that our dog doesn't have this condition (thank goodness) so I was going to return it but I decided to try it out when my puppy got a tick on her head, thinking it would keep her focused while I got the tick off (which it very much did)The only one I have used is the chicken flavor and when I took off the lid, I gagged and threw up in my mouth. It stinks that bad. But my puppy did seem to like the taste of it.

This product is a bit odd, to say the least. It is designed in a roll-on deodorant type of bottle and your dog must lick the rolling ball to enjoy his treat.When first trying to get my dog to try it, he really looked at me, looked at the bottle, looked at me, looked at the bottle etc. You could literally see in his eyes that he was wondering what the heck he was supposed to do, or what I wanted him to do. Finally he took a swipe at it with his tongue. I assume he was unimpressed because he made no effort to go for another lick, despite my encouragement.The whole idea is just weird. I give my dog treats as well..treats, or to reward good behavior, or just to be nice, or to get him to lay/settle down for a little - in other words to keep him busy for a few minutes or so. This type of treat obviously goes against the idea of keeping him occupied for awhile while keeping my time free since you have to sit/stand there and hold the bottle for him. Now, don't get me wrong, we always have a variety of snacks on hand and I would not mind standing there holding this bottle for him if he actually liked the treat. It's just one of those little extra things we do to show our love. However, he just seemed to not like the taste once he did figure out to lick it, otherwise I assume he would have continued to lick.The texture of the liquid inside just looks gross to me. It is a clearish, somewhat dark brown color. Kind of like pancake syrup although not as sticky/tacky.If your dog will lick the roller ball and likes the taste, then I guess it is a good buy, but if not it is obviously a waste.I also cannot help but wonder who sat around and thought "Hmmmm, let's create a liquid dog treat and put it in a roll-on deodorant dispenser!!"
My dogs would not lick it or even pay attention to it. I thought it would be great for training as I am a consumate treat "dropper", but they were not the least interested. Too bad
The roller ball was sort of hard to get going. My dogs kept biting the bottle and wouldn't lick it very much. It also had a very strong smell.

column9: Interesting, but what's the practical use?
column10: Lickety Stik is an interesting idea. It's a small bottle filled with a thick brown liquid - a liquified dog treat, essentially - which you can squeeze out and smear over the top (sort of like gel deodorant). Your dog, I guess, is then supposed to lick this as a treat, but unfortunately my dog was just confused. I was still able to dab the liquid on his paw, and he seemed to like that quite a bit. So it still works for me to some extent.The big issue, I think, is that I'm not sure what the practical use of this product is. Maybe it's convenient for training; instead of carrying a bag of treats, you can just pop this thing in your pocket. Or I suppose if you have an elderly dog who has trouble with solids, it might come in handy. Otherwise it seems more convenient for me (and probably for many others) to stick with the dry treats.

As I look for inspiration...I thought this pumpkin tea might  put me into a pre Halloween state of mind! :) It does tastes like pumpkin and mild spice. I'm pleased w it! I'm sharing w friends! Sit down for a moment;  lets chat and drink tea! Boo! See your terrified...puts ya in a good spirits!
Somehow had one bag of this, gave it to my mom, she LOVED it so much I had to hunt down where to get a whole box. Sent it to her and she is thrilled.

Sunflower seed butter is really delicious. I prefer the flavor of sunbutter to peanut butter, but it is different, not necessarily a full replacement. I love peanut butter as well. It isn't so much a dessert butter like macadamia and cashew butters (I'll eat those straight for dessert, sometimes on ice cream, but I wouldn't dream of a macadamia nut butter and jelly sandwich). It fills a somewhat similar niche to peanut butter (hearty, filling, a bit savory) but it has a unique flavor and is a bit more delicate than PB. If you or someone in your family has peanut allergies, this is a no brainer. If not I think it is still worth trying (perhaps find a place where you can find a single jar before committing to six?) It is a bit pricey compared to peanut butter, but has a great flavor and is very versatile (good on sandwiches, ice cream, veggies, or a finger dipped into the jar).

column9: Awesome, but look out for soy!
column10: I have a ridiculous number of severe food allergies. Sunbutter was one of three major sources of protein for me. Yes, it is delicious. Yes, I would eat it religiously if all other things were equal....but they are not. Sunbutter recently began processing this product on equipment that processes soy and, while properly labeled, I got so used to the product that I didn't bother checking the nutrition label.I am allergic to soy and can no longer have this product. I rated a three because it is still a wonderful product - but changing equipment has cut out a good-sized portion of their key consumer pool.

I have tried other brands of sunflower seed butter spread, and this is the best brand.  SunButter comes the closest to tasting like peanutbutter, from what I can remember (been years since I was diagnosed with severe intolerance to nuts and peanuts).This brand has a good balance between salty and sweet, and has a roasted seed flavor that gives it the little extra yumminess.  Other brands taste flat compared to Sunbutter.I eat this on fruit (apples & bananas & some cinnamon), toast, rice cakes, soy cream, smoothies, sandwiches, and by itself on a spoon.  Makes me feel like I have one less "hole" in my diet, and a great protein treat to boot!

I need to say up front I didn't buy mine online but in our local "natural foods" type market but it was this brand and variety.  I had seen it mentioned on Dr. Oz and thought it sounded interesting, and the girl tasting it looked like she actually liked it!  It is REALLY good.  Tastes a lot like sunflower seeds but with the texture in your mouth of a natural type peanut butter, sort of creamy-oily but very spreadable and stirable unlike a lot of natural pb.  Not an overpowering taste, a little bit sweet even.  And supposed to be very healthy.If you are interested in trying some, note that there are a lot of versions including organic, so pick the one that seems best for you, consider trying one jar from a local store if you can find it and then when you like it buy it online for (probably) a better price, even if you must buy 3 jars at a time.  I can even get my 5 year old to eat it, though I have to add grape jelly lol!

I have tried various nut/seed spreads from different makers of such products. This is my personal favorite.  It's very smooth in texture,and I really like the flavor as well.  If you like peanut butter, and also like sunflower seeds, give it a try!

As a mom of a child with multiple food allergies, and as a peanut allergy sufferer myself, we LOVE this product.  I tried Sunbutter for the first time when I was on vacation with my hubby and we have consumed it happily since then.  When my son turned out to have tons of food allergies this became a wonderful staple to help keep good fats and protein in his diet without risking exposure to other things that could cause him to be sick.  Comes HIGHLY recommended.  My 2 year old asks for it EVERY day!

This product is a great alternative to peanut butter, or any butter. I like it just as much as I ever liked peanut butter. It has a similar nutty flavor, with a great contrast of salty and sweet. The shipping was fast, and its a delicious and healthy snack you can eat with just about anything!

This is a staple at our house. It's great with a sliced apple or just on a spoon. It has replaced peanut butter for us and we are glad amazon carries it so we can have it home delivered. At the local store it is $8 a jar.

My five year old daughter has a severe peanut allergy - sunbutter has become a staple in our pantry. It is such a great alternative to peanut butter. Glad to see it offered here on Amazon at such a reasonable price, as it often sells out at our local grocery store.

Very satisfied with Sunbutter. We use as a peanut substitute. We can't tell the difference between it and peanut butter. I saw one review that said it didn't taste like peanut butter. I don't understand they must have gotten a bad batch or something.

This stuff is fantastic! And, it's so much more than a peanut butter substitute.I like it on toasted sunflower seed bread; also, in place of tahini in a hummus recipe.Hummus makes a great dip for sliced apples. Think outside the box!

We have a child with allergies to nuts! The reality of having to give up our family staple of peanut butter was depressing. We went 1.5 years w/o any substitute and I can tell you that a jam sandwich just doesn't do it! Then we found sun butter and it was life changing! We have tired a variety of brands and this one is the best by far. I have a couple of kids who prefer the red lid but most of us like the yellow lid better. It is creamier like melted pb on toast.

I have been using SunButter for some years now as a Peanut Butter alternative. Not due to any allergies, but peanuts contain high levels of L-Arginine, an amino acid that is known to build muscle mass but may also inhibit the immune system (or so I have read). Sunbutter is very tasty, especially so if you like sunflower seeds. I like it better than peanut butter, and the fat composition is supposed to be healthier for you, so why wouldn't you try it ? I find that the "Natural Sunbutter" is tastier and smoother than the "Creamy" variety, but both are very good. Yes, more expensive and less common than peanut butter..... but I think anyone would enjoy it.

If you love sunflower seeds, it will take an army to keep you from diving into this jar and eating the whole thing!  Great, nutty, sunflower seed taste!  Very rich, just like the seeds themselves, so you don't need to eat a lot of this to be satisfied. I LOVE this stuff!

If you haven't tried SunButter at least once, I most certainly highly recommend it.For some reason because it is a seed and not a nut, I can digest it.  Yes, I react to peanut butter but not sun-butter.  So some fun of having "peanut butter" is back in my life.  Not it doesn't taste exactly the same.  I like it better!

My son is severely allergic to peanuts and several other tree nuts.  Needless to say we have had no peanut butter in the house since we found out about the allergy.  This has been really hard on me because I LOVE peanut butter.  I found sunbutter on a blog and decided to try it.  It is amazing.  It definitely has a sunflower flavor, but it has a peanut butter texture.  The smell is amazing as well.  I have used the sunbutter just as I would peanut butter; sandwiches, cookies, any other baking, on top of celery.  I just can't say enough good things about this product.
So happy to have this!  We eat it at my house almost everyday!  Taste almost identical to peanut butter.

I purchased this product in two cases since I found it here on Amazon.com at an amazingly lower price than I had been paying for it at the Health Food Store in my area.  It is an all natural product without preservatives and other additives that can be harmful to your health.  I discovered an allergy to peanuts; not life threatening but consistant with negativeness to my health, and was missing my peanut butter sandwiches.  When I found this product, I was very pleased with the smoothness, the taste, and the nutritional value of it.  I am on a no or low sugar diet to improve the Candida yeast infection throughout my body and thankfully, I tested positive to using this in my diet.  If you love sunflower seeds and love a good nut butter sandwich, try this product(with a little honey).  I gave my Chiropractor/Holistic Doc. a jar of it and he loved it.  Don't go overboard with it though, it still contains fat, though good fat, it is still fat and may be hard on your gallbladder if you indulge. Enjoy!SunButter Natural Sunflower Seed Spread, 16-Ounce Plastic Jars (Pack of 6)
My kids love them.  My older boy has nut allergy and can't have peanut butter.  Soybutter tastes terrible.  I'm so glad to find this product on Amazon.

column9: delicious and cheaper than purchasing at WhFds
column10: Sunbutter is a staple in our family due to allergies. It is a delicious replacement for peanut and other nut butters, and purchasing it online saves us about $1.50/jar over the regular price at our local health food store.

This is a step above peanut butter, imo.  I'm not even a huge sunflower seed fan, but this is just yummy!  Slightly sweet taste, and has a smooth spread like peanut butter.  The only thing that keeps me from buying this vs. peanut butter is the steep price of the Sunbutter :(  Wish there were some better deals on it or it was a part of subscribe and save.

For living so far from Cincinnati, this was a great price on this product. The seller shipped quickly, and the product arrived with no problems at all.You need to make sure you have enough medium cheddar cheese around to make a 3 way. Too bad you can't find Kahn's hot dogs on the west coast, for an authentic Skyline coney dog.

I've used Chicken Stock Base for all my chicken, seafood, turkey, meat, rice, and lamb recipes for the last 40 years and I've yet to be disappointed.  CSB is a balanced addition to any recipe requiring that 'something' to enhance its flavor and allow for the individual flavoring shine with the comment 'wow', 'this is really good'...without competing with additional spices like turmeric, curry, saffron, ginger or cardamon.  It's my favorite basic spice bar none!
$29 for 3.2 oz. really ?  I saw the same exact product for less than $8 from other vendors.Why would anybody pay almost four times as much for chicken stock ?Otherwise, it is an excellent product.

Brownie Points has great customer service, and their brownies are truly terrific.  The brownies have tasty combinations and I like the fact that they come individually wrapped.  You can freeze them and take out as many as you want.
I sent these brownies to my 20 year old son twice, and he said it was like dying and going to heaven.  He is very picky about what sweets he eats, so that is a huge compliment.
Received these as a gift from a friend...best brownies I've ever had!  Try them (you won't regret it!)

These are very tasty.  For me --a little oregano goes a long way but the seasoning does not overpower the olive.  My only complaint is that they are a little oily (because they're packed with olive oil...) I really like the packaging; they are easy to bring along for lunch or snack (each packet is 2.3 oz. or... 65g).Nutrition Facts (from packaging):Serving Size 4 olives (15g)Servings per Container about 4Amount per Serving:Calories 15Calories from Fat 13Total Fat 1.4g (2%)Saturated Fat 0.4g (2%)Trans Fat 0gSodium 195mg (8%)Total Carbohydrate <1gProtein 0gCalcium 1% and Iron 2%Ingredients:  Green Olives, Salt, Lemon Juice (seasoned in a natural marinated with extra virgin olive oil, oregano, garlic, coriander and Lemon Peel) PRODUCT OF GREECE

I bought these from a suggestion in an article online, might have been Oprah. The quality is high and ingredients work well together but I am used to cheapo green olives from the grocery store. I like a more pickled taste and these were a bit lighter with more on an olive oil/lemon/oregano flavor. They are great for on the go with a great resealable bag. Their are about 4 servings per bag with 4 olives per serving. Now I don't know about you but who eats just 4 olives? I end up eating the whole bag *yikes* sodium overload. I would try other flavors because I *love* olives but the price is a bit much, at about $.19 per olive.

I found these in a little farmers market in MA and I've been hooked ever since. They're addictive and I almost never stop at one serving. They have a great tart flavor and the seasoning and olive oil give them a nice texture too. All of the Cat Cora olives are good, but I think these are my favorite!

I was looking forward to adding a new lunch snack. However, these olives are pathetic - pale green, flavorless without a hint of oregano or lemon.  I guess I just fell for the pretty face.I will try to return the remaining 7 packages.
I love this drink. Its a bit sweet and thick for me, so I do a 60juice/40water mix and it lasts longer, and tastes better.
Since I can no longer get the product from my local grocery stores, I turned to Amazon to continue my healthy eating journey. Love the promptness and convenience.

Nowadays, it's really difficult to get a really natural Pineapple fruit, specially where I live, but this product is just fantastic! You can feel the smell and the flavor of a natural pineapple.Thank you!

column9: What Would Pimiento Cheese Spread Be Without Them?
column10: Just a plain old cheese sandwith, that's what. Just take some good sharp grated cheddar, some grated Monterey Jack, add a little Mayo, a little grated sweet onion, a smidgen of sweet pickle relish and a spoonful of these wonderfully flavored pimiento pieces, mix them up and serve on crackers, celery sticks or bread. Yum, Yum, Yum!

Dromedary Sliced Pimientos, 4-Ounce Jars (Pack of 24)Low calorie, light, delicious. Toss in with salad, mix with low-fat canned chicken, combine with grated cheese--they fit in with breakfast, lunch, dinner, supper, or even an informal, fast snack.

Zuke's produces some great products. Recently, I tried the "Natural Purrz" healthy moist cat treats (Savory Salmon flavored). The nice things about these treats is that they are low-calorie (only 2 calories per little moist treat). Also, Zuke's products are made with high quality protein and grains, and all ingredients come from the US (Made in the USA!). That said, these small treats remind me of my cat's monthly Heartgard medication - it's only palatable to some cats. Seamus, my fatty tabby, likes these, but not as much as the Greenie crunchy treats. Echo, my svelt black cat, won't touch these moist treats. Overall, they are a great option for a low-calorie treat, but use in moderation. It also comes in a "tender chicken" flavor.The active ingredients in Natural Purrz (Savory Salmon) include: salmon, barley flour, rice flour, vegetable glycerin, malted barley, tapioca, gelatin, water, menhaden fish oil, brewer's yeast, natural flavors, lecithin, cultured whey, acetic acid, salt. Vitamins and Minerals: Vitamins A, D3, E, B12, taurine, ascorbic acid (Vitamin C) calcium pantothenate, riboflavin (B2) niacin, thiamine mononitrate (B1), pyridoxine hydrochloride (B6), folic acid, zinc oxide, sodium selenite (source of selenium).So, overall, one paw down for overall palability... That said, they don't go to waste - while the protein content is likely too high for my dog, JP loves these as small additions to his Kong toy...

We have lovingly dubbed these treats "kitty crack". Our 11 year old lynx point siamese goes NUTS for these treats. He will follow you anywhere and comes running if he even hears the bag being jostled. I like that they are natural, but would prefer if they were completely grain free. They are small enough to be eaten quickly, but just soft enough that they are easy to break apart for training. Definitely a favorite in our house now!

The Cats absolutely love these things! They are all natural too, which I love, and my poor male cat has almost no teeth and these are the only natural treat I can find for him that he can eat comfortably. They are soft and I cut them in half for him. They smell really good too.. Like meat!

As soon as I started opening these, my cat began sniffing the air.  The next thing I knew she was beside me begging for a treat.  She gobbled them down like there was no tomorrow.  The same thing has happened each time I get them out.  She gives them a 5 paw review.

My cat has food allergies - he can't have chicken, turkey, corn, or soy, among other things. So finding cat treats he can have has been a challenge, especially when he decided he didn't like the simple dried fish or freeze-dried beef lung type of treats. However, he goes completely wild for these! Since they use rice flour & tapioca as the binder, they don't trigger his allergies. YMMV, cats are very individual in their tastes, but if you have a cat with food allergies, you may want to give these a try.

My two kittens (6 & 7 Months) don't even think about eating these (Salmon flavor). I don't think they even recognize that they are food.The good news is, after they leave them on the floor they come back later and play soccer with them, which they do enjoy (so thats why it gets 2 instead of one star).(Bought at local pet store for about $1.50 more than amazon's price, for what its worth.

column9: Good, healthy option, but my cat does not like them
column10: I bought these as a healthier option for my cat's treats, but she won't even touch them. She does however like the chicken flavor of the same brand. If you have a finicky cat, you might want to try the other flavor.

Got my order quickly. It's difficult to find chicken free food and treats and these were a good price. Saved me trips to numerous trips to the store.  My cats loves these too. Although, I don't recall getting an invoice w the shipment, but it may have been there.

column9: Even the pickiest cats will like these!
column10: My cat does not like any cat treats.  We have tried every single one!  We purchased these treats at an SPCA benefit and tried them.  The cat LOVES them.  She will chase them around the house and savor them.  They seem siliar in consistency (and smell) to the Bil-Jac treats for dogs (although they aren't the same thing).  I think the meatiness of the treat is what my cat likes ... not a lot of fluff.

i was surprised at how much my little marlee loves these snacks ... a real winner!  these treats are definitely on the soft/moist side which is what i need for a kitty who doesn't drink water.  even though they are small, i will cut each one in half to use as small training treats.  i'll definitely be buying more of these.

column9: Human interpretation of cat behavior or yummy in my cat tummy
column10: How does one know what exactly the cat thinks of these?  I can only go by observation and 2 out of 3 cats go nuts for them, i.e. begging, meowing, jumping, meowing, circling, meowing.  I was worried they were too hard as I can hardly break one in half, but that doesn't slow them down - even my 11-year-old tabby.  The taste must outweigh the gnawing and smacking necessary.  More proof: a side-by-side taste test revealed both cats will choose these first before Whisker Lickin's brand treats.  But of course they will hog down the 2nd place treats in a blink too.  I gave a 4 star since I do think they are rather hard.  I also appreciate the free shipping. I will order again.

I have 6 cats and am always looking for new kitty items. Most of my cats loved these. Out of the 6 only 1 refused to eat them. Another ate it but did not seem real impressed and the other 4 gobbled them up like there was no tomorrow. This is an item I will buy for them again.

I got these treats for my two cats who are not really that picky.  They seemed to like them and begged for more like usual.  They are pretty firm for a semimoist treat.  They almost look wax like but the cats chows them down with pleasure.  I have ordered them more than once from Amazon already.
Cats love them - both the chicken and salmon flavors.  They also offer a glucosamine chondroitin product (for cats with joint pain) that is much less expensive than some alternatives.

column9: Kitty Doesn't Like 'Em, But I'm Sure they'd be good for her!
column10: I give this product three stars because I love Zuke's for our dog, and I am sure that if our cat would eat these, they'd be way better for her than the high fructose corn syrup crud she prefers.  But the sad truth is, she doesn't like em.  And for a cat that will steal pickles, I think that's saying something.
IT WAS PERFECT! IT ARRIVED ON TIME AND EXACTLY AS I HAD EXPECTED IT TO BE.  IT'S CAT FOOD WHAT ELSE DO YOU WANT ME TO SAY?

my cat is "special".  he has some weird condition/allergy?  that causes him to have angioedema of assorted body parts and it appears to be triggered by an ingredient in most cat food.  this is the only product which does not cause him to swell.
Meaty, saucy and full of protein.  The dogs really like this product, and they get it everyday!  I would recommend this to spice up dry dog food.

I am very pleased with every aspect of this transaction.  I was notified when the item would be shipped (included tracking).  The preserves arrived 2 days later (I thought it would take longer).  It was well packaged and the order info was included.  The preserves taste great!
I ordered six Cavendish MonkeyChews and a Cavendish Fruitcake (reviewed separately) and found the Monkey Chews to be a great, albeit overpriced, snack.

column9: Fabulous for beach themed wedding cake!
column10: This product arrived in only 3 days from Florida to Oregon, far more quickly than stated.  The packaging was a work of art unto itself.  Everything was carefully wrapped and was in perfect condition.  The shells are gorgeous!  Just the perfect size to use on a cake.  The detail in each shell is lovely and the pearlescent finish is just exquisite.  A beautiful product for a happy bride-to-be!

column9: Our Fussy Cats Appreciate Pity the Kitties
column10: We have two extremely fussy, spoiled felines.  We first tried Three Dog Bakery We Pity the Kitties Salmon Treats when we found it when we visited a grocery store out of town.  Our boys went nutso!  Much to our chagrin, we couldn't find it in our town.  My hubby was sad, so I went to Amazon and we found them.  Our Boys are happy; my hubby is happy; and I am relieved.  We trust the quality of Three Dog Bakery We Pity the Kitties Salmon Treats and we trust Amazon!

column9: Sadly these are processed in China!
column10: I bought these for my cats and they loved them. The packing does not show any "MADE IN" information. With some research and a call to Three Dog bakery I found out these are US caught fish sent to China for processing!!! For the safety of my pets I will no longer give them ANY treat made or processed in China. We just don't know what is going on over there. Treats are a great size for cats and they love salmon so much, but my fear of Chinese processed pet foods/treats will stop me from getting these ever again.I have found a USA caught and USA processed freeze dried salmon treat that I will stick with from now on. Give Whole Life Pet Products Pure Meat All Natural Freeze Dried Salmon Filet Treats, 2-Ounce a try instead of these.

We have 2 cats and one of them is crazy for these salmon treats.  She doesn't usually go for other treats but these she LOVES!  She would sit there and stare at the cabinet where we store the treats and meow and meow until we give her some treats.  We're also able to lure her out of any hiding places with these treats.
Be warned- once you give your cat these treats, he/she will bug you constantly for more.By far, these are the favorite treats of my cat.I do wish they were a bit cheaper.
Both of my cats go crazy for these. They meow and run to the drawer they are kept until they are given one, and 30min later repeat.We call it kittyCrack. enough said.

column9: We Pity the kitties, SALMON*** cat treats!!
column10: As others have suggested, my cats have inhaled these, with great gusto.  But given the composition, (a bag of 60 or 70 pieces weighs one ounce) its really a treat, not suited as a regular meal.**** the salmon product is great!!!  The chicken product is totally ignored by my cat(s).  Mine and cats owned by friends.  So if you are new to this, start with the salmon.Also, in my most recent order, something changed.  I ordered 6 boxes, 5 contained the usual tin foil, inner bag.  This is a bag inside the box shown above.  The 6th box, however, had a clear plastic inner bag, and for some reason, my cats reaction was more subdued.  She ate them, but not with the usual excitement.  Not sure what to make of this.Its tough to describe a cats excitement.  But if your favorite dessert is tiramisu, imagine the salmon product is tiramisu for cats.

Name is really cute and these treats look good on paper. Quantity was pretty small. The meat is freeze dried.My cats gave me a "surely you're joking" look and walk away from these treats. I gave them to the neighbor and her dog liked them. My cats may have an unsophisticated pallet. For treats they like Friskies Natural Sensations, Whisker Lickers, and some flavors of Whiskers Temptations.

I do not like hard candy or candy in general really, but these actually taste like the real lemon they are made from and are tart in a natural lemony way and not too sweet. It's hard to find the Claey's brand in stores, so I order in bulk. I just wish the shipping was cheaper.

these licorice hard candies are exactly as you see in the picture, and taste even better.  i've eaten panda black chewy "natural" licorice, but it's not sweet enough when i want to eat some (real) CANDY.  this claey's licorice tastes just as my taste buds imagined/hoped they would.  i'm sold, and about to place my second order of them.  each piece is approximately 1/2" by 1/2", the perfect size, the perfect taste, the perfect candy for my sweet craving.  some might think they are a little pricey, but we need to indulgence ourselves on occasion...we deserve it, right?  my new favorite candy!
If you like reasonably hot cinnamon this is not for you.  Very mild.  If you like mild than this cinnamon drop is for you.

There's a very nice watermelon flavor to these candies.  If I had any complaint...and I really don't...it would be that I'd prefer the candies individually wrapped.  Otherwise, I'm pleased with my selection.
The lemon drops are delicious just like I used to remember. Now have them all over the house in little dishes.Service was wonderful.  Thank you
This falls pretty short of what I had hoped for.  It has the slightest taste of watermelon I guess.  It really tastes like bubble gum.  Not recommended.  Jolly ranchers taste more watermelony.

Delicious, loads of flavor without being overwhelming and burning. Very addictive. I ordered several other flavors as well and liked them all. Old fashioned quality is my main impression. The dusting of confection sugar adds to the presentation and taste.
This product is just what my chrildren and their friends wanted. I can assure you that it won't last long. I'm sure that I will be ordering again.
I happened to fall upon these candies at a little store in Oakland, Oregon and absolutely fell in love with them. The Green Apple and Wild Cherry flavors are by far my favorite.
Simple and delicious cinnamon drops with lots of flavor.  We enjoyed having these is a candy dish around the house for ourselves and guest.

I have these, along with the cherry and lemon versions, in a candy dish on my desk at work.  I've had to buy a pound of each type twice now in the last 2 months because they go fast, everyone seems to like them very much (I do too!!).

My husband and I discovered Claey's Drops in our local chain drug store, but they only stocked lemon and horehound flavors. I am a big fan of anything cinnamon or minty. I also try to search out candy made in the USA, as I find candy from Mexico and Canada to have a strange, off taste to the sugar.The Claey's Cinnamon Drops are perfect! Not too large, not too sweet, and a true cinnamon flavor. The one pound bag is actually not that large. I plan to buy another bag of a different flavor, plus will buy my husband a bag of lemon flavor as a gift.

column9: Tastes good, and good for you ...
column10: at least if you have a blocked salivary duct, like I do.  My doc told me to suck on these to keep the saliva flowing. They're sour enough that they do that quite well.

The lemon drops were as expected but the took so long to get here that they missed the party for which they were intended.  We ended up having to buy some at the local store.  I guess we will snack on these for Halloween, instead.
At least 30% of candies have some different taste and not as strong taste as I would like for this candy or it used to be in those candies.

column9: Never drink it hot, must add ice & sweeten condensed milk
column10: Previouse reviewer doesn't know what Thai Iced Coffee supposed to taste like.Thai Coffee is never to drink hot.  You can add sugar and top it with half/half or sweeten condensed milk.
I love Thai Ice Coffee. This is one of the better mixes I have tired. Robust flavor that is not overly bitter.

column9: Worst coffee we have ever had!
column10: I made a mistake ordering this (Thought i ordered Thai tea) but wanted to give it a try since i had it.  I made the first batch and threw out the rest.  My wife and i agree - very bad for our taste.  If you gave it to me and did not tell me what kind of drink it was - i am not sure i would guess it was coffee.

column9: Baby likes the taste but they stick
column10: My baby skipped the purees and would not touch rice cereal. These puffs were one of her first solid foods when she was about 7 months. They are puffed up air things which easily dissolve in the mounth so there is no choking hazard. Most of what is in the container and puffs is air, so don't expect a lot of nutrition out of it. The container has 6 half cup servings of 25 calories. My little one got far more servings out of it. It is just to get them used to solid stuff, not to fill them up. Unlike the rice cereal, my little one liked these rice based puffs. The vanilla puffs have cute little star shapes. Not looking at the label of the container, my husband popped open the lid and ate half the container. He freaked out once I told him he ate baby food but said it tasted pretty good. I tried a few and I must say they are fairly sweet and not bad tasting at all. They are much sweeter than the HAPPYBABY brand puffs and that sweeter taste is preferred by my sweeth-tooth baby and hubby. The disadvantage of these puffs is that they tend to stick. Babies put their fingers in their mouth and end up with drooly fingers. When the little one was picking up the little puffs with her wet fingers, these puffs started sticking to her fingers which was somewhat frustrating for her (the reason I docked one star).

column9: Invigorates Ordinary Coffee Into A New Aromatic Flavor
column10: When your everyday coffee has lost its fidelity, and the marriage of sugar and cream no longer excites, introducing a new partner of flavor may be the solution.Vanilla extract has for its history been drawn into relationship with bakers, chefs and cooks. In my home, it has all the usual uses in cake and cookie making, but also, as a more daily use as a coffee additive. McCormick is the brand I use most, and always the purest.A few drops dosing my cup just as I pour a cup of freshly ground, freshly brewed coffee, in addition to slightly warmed and whipped cream, with a spooning of sugar, and my day begins with more than a 'cuppa joe.'This threesome of sugar, cream and vanilla tosses an aroma around the room, down the hall strong enough to entice curiosity from neighbors and neighbor's cats alike. If no one is there to share, feel free to drink alone. May your love of the cupped elixir find new vigor.--Brockeim

I know the price varies for stage 1 foods but sometimes they are a lot cheaper on amazon then in the stores. I wasn't sure how many were in the package so I decided to just buy one.  There are 8 packs of 2 in this package so for the price, you are getting 16 containers.  I personally wasn't sure if I was getting a great price or paying slightly  more then if I went to the supermarket.  I like these gerber containers of baby food.
