There was a noticeable difference in our dog after being off the Pedigree and on the Cani Vitalis; a worse difference.  She doesn't get up as easy and isn't as playful and spunky.  We will have to go back to what we know works.
My dogs go crazy over these treats, and not just this flavor but every treat  cani vitalis makes. My dogs are papillons so are only about 5pounds each. Makes this the perfect size treat.

Plant was large, full and healthy.  Given as a sympathy gift, they stated that the plant was beautiful and undamaged.  When I ordered this I was told from the beginning that it would not be delivered for 5 to 7 days.  So if you are ordering for a funeral this is something to consider.  It arrived in 5 days.  I will order from this group again.

Del Monte appears to be so ashamed of where pup-peroni products are made that they no longer include that information on the package or on their web site.  When a corporation is too embarrassed to disclose such information, there is usually a very good reason for them to be ashamed.My dogs liked these products, but I have since switched to only giving them products made in the USA and food/treats which do not include meat by-products.  I don't always trust USA manufacturers, but they do have fewer quality control problems than some foreign countries I could name.

column9: One of my dogs loves it
column10: I wanted to buy it from amazon.com as I was lazy to do shopping.  However, after comparied the price, retail stores are much cheaper than online.
Reminds me of lemon icebox pie. Tastes a little bit like Eagle Brand milk too. Very creamy. NOT gelatinous. They carry this brand at our Fresh Market.

I first purchased Patum Peperium's Poacher's Relish at Fortnum & Mason in London and brought it back to the U.S., and now I'm looking to purchase more. Quite savory, being salty and salmon-y tasting, spread very thin on toast for a quick savory bite in the morning.
This is a fantastic artisanal pasta. It was very easy to boil al dente and since the surface of the pasta is not smooth, the pasta really absorbed the flavor of the sauce. Highly recommend.
My dog wouldn't eat these and neither would my daughter's two dogs.  I don't know what it is about the flavor but they didn't like them.
These are the kind of glacee apricots which I remember eating years ago.  They are extremely sweet and moist, but they have a deliciously intense apricot flavor.
If you like apricots, these definitely will be a special treat.  They are sweet, plump, & juicy.  Great Taste!  Good gift idea!

Glazed Australian apricots have long been a family favorite for special occasions.  We have found them at other sources, but  the ones we have purchased on Amazon.com far surpass any others we've enjoyed in the past. Exceptional rich, tangy flavor and moist luscious texture - yummy! Superior Nut Company's are the most sumptuous ever.

These apricots are glazed but they retain the taste of fresh apricots I knew as a child.  They are not the dry kind with crunchy outer layer (which we also like); these apricots are very juicy and brought us more pleasure then I expected when purchasing.

Where I live, Pistachios have been more expensive than some of the other nuts, so I haven't used them much. But buying them in bulk like this made them more reasonable.I've been enjoying them quite a bit. They are soft, almost like a Cashew, yet flavorful. Excellent for chopping and using in muffins. I'm also going to try making a salad dressing with them, and maybe some deserts.The quality of these was very good, they appear to be quite fresh.

The taste, quality of this individually-wrapped cookie was disappointing; nothing like I expected.  Wanted a rich, homebaked-type cookie, something special, individually packaged.  These cookies were described as: "Premium" so that's what I expected.  Another brand of choc. chip cookies, packaged in bulk, taste better than these.
I actually like the Grandma's chocolate chips a litle bit more but cookies are quite tasty with large chocolate chips

My girlfriend recently purched them from a grocery store, and wow are they good. I was scared at first, frightened really, most healthy food I have tried in the past has been complete garbage, always tasting like plastic, or you know some orphans died because of what you just ate. But no sir, not these chips. I think these chips may possibly deserve an award, Nothing flashy like the Nobel peace prize but maybe a regional bowling participation ribbon. In this context a personal teleporter would be the nobel prize and the top food product, some sort of cheese and cow monstrosity that has no calories would be the congressional medal of honor. These definitely have their place and they will not budge. Fortunately I have an amazing  girlfriend who provides me with these astounding discoveries of healthy food.

I bought a box of these because they were on sale - and I'm glad I gave them a try! They have great flavor and texture - and they are so light too! My husband and I both enjoy them, which I think says a lot that a man is willing to try them too. Give them a try - they are a great snack and don't taste like a good-for-you (i.e. cardboard) snack!
The lower calories make a cheesy cracker snack easier on the waistline.  Love this and all of the other varieties as well.

column9: Great Little Low Cal Chip/Cracker Thingies
column10: I've really come to like these Kellogg's Special K Cracker Chips. They have a great flavor and texture and are just the right size for snacking. They come in several different flavors that are all good, but these Cheddar Cheese are by far my favorite. I big serving is just a fraction of the calories of regular chips and goes a long way toward satisfying the salty/crunchy craving.

We bought these at the grocery store and love them.  The price on this package doesn't make any sense though.  If you look at the other flavors such as sour cream and onion they are 1/3 of the price.  If I'm understanding the pricing correctly these will cost about $7.50 for a 4oz box.  Is the cheddar actually gold?

column9: Not sure how people eat them
column10: They look and feel like pop chips, but they taste like some bizarre frankenstein of chemical flavoring from new jersey. I can only describe the aftertaste as strange. I don't know what it tastes like ... something that isn't meant to be eaten though. I guess others like them, that's cool, I think they're horrendous.

column9: BEST rice crispy bars and chocolate fountain dippers EVER!
column10: All of Krafts flavored marshmellows make EXCELLENT krispy bars. I was worried about the carmel but even those tasted amazing in a krispy bar. Chocolate, coconut, caramel and strawberry ALL of the flavors are great. I also used the mellows themselves at my daughters wedding for chocolate fountain dippers and they were a big hit!

I've prepared these pheasants several times and they always turn out well.  This size is great for a dinner with about 4 people.  Just make sure you don't over cook it because it's NOT CHICKEN.  I made that mistake once and definitely learned from it.

My dachshunds love to chew on bones. I used to order this brand in the knotted bones and my dogs loved them, but the company changed the recipe and now my picky dogs won't even touch them.  I have also bought the compressed rawhide chicken top bones, which my dogs like too, but they never chew the actual rawhide so it doesn't keep them busy for long.  I saw these online and thought I would try them - what a hit!! My dogs are so happy! They love the chicken tops and it seems to take a Little longer to chew off then the pressed rawhide bones do.  Also, the rawhide is thin enough that they even enjoy chewing that as well.  I hope they continue making these just as they are, they are fabulous!!!

My dog Sasha loves this product.  I order frequently because she can't get enough of them.However, the tops need to be baked less.  Some batches tend to have the chicken tops crack and fall off.  The idea of these is to have then chew it off somewhat.

Our gerbil, Armand, loves pumkin seeds, but we don't like to give him salted ones.  The ones from the grocery store are always salted when they have them, and washing the salt off is a pain.  This fit the bill, are a lot less hassle, and the gerbil loves them.  We were out, the grocery store stopped carrying them, but now domestic peace is restored.

I received a sample as part of a cultural event and fell in love with them.  They are crispy and just the right amount of sweetness.  Once I open the package, they all seem to disappear.  I have to find a place to buy more!

column9: Now I Make Pad Thai that Tastes Like It Should!
column10: Tamarind paste has not been a staple in my pantry -- until I discovered what a difference it can make in my cooking.  I created a marvelous Pad Thai sauce, simply by using this paste (and a few other ingredients).For all its goodness, I have to say that you've got to have a little faith in order to put something like this in a sauce.  It resembles nothing so much as road tar, black, gooey, utterly yucky-looking.  But do give it a shot -- its worth your time and effort.By the way, I bought the 6-pack.  That's a lot of tamarind paste, more, in fact, that I can use in this lifetime.  I'm sharing bottles with friends and relatives.Highly recommended for those who enjoy oriental cooking.

column9: Great stuff - but use with caution!
column10: I too am probably going to be giving away several jars of this paste - a very small amount goes a long way, and I'm not sure how long its shelf life is.  There are spaces on the label for batch number, manufacturing date, and expiration date - but just one number (91016) stamped in that general area - appears to be a batch number.While the lack of an expiration date is annoying, I'm otherwise very happy with this - makes pad thai taste like pad thai, so long as you don't overdo it.  I had never used it before and was working with a recipe calling for processing your own tamarind pulp, so I tried guessing at the right amount.  Next time I'll remember to read the bottle - "one teaspoon for six persons...."  Am just beginning to experiment with other uses.  The manufacturer's web site suggests using it to flavor stews and as a replacement for mango pulp or for vinegar in recipes, and yes, there are lots of recipes out there that call for it.

First time buyer from this supplier.  Product was on time and as described.  For tamarind, I've always used real bean pods with the shelling, soaking and straining to wind up with a messey kitchen and watery sauce.  When I opened the first jar of Tamicon, I knew those pod days were over.  This sauce is thick and tangy just the way it needs to be for my cooking.  A favorite item for my friends is BBQ with a unique African BBQ sauce that requires tamarind.  Now I have less excuse for not making it more often!

Yes, there are six containers to the order, but you might be surprised that you'll use these up b/4 too long if you like to try new recipes with tamarind. If you enter the Foodnetwork site, and word search "tamarind paste" or "tamarind concentrate" you will find a plethora of recipes using this.  I have two I use often...one is for baking fish fillets with a Bali-style sauce that's easy to whip up, another recipe for glazing pork ribs on the BBQ with a tasty sauce. The list of recipes is endless.  If you are a foodie and enjoy exploration of foods that are out of the ordinary, this will fit the bill.  It looks and pours like dark molasses, but b/c the individual containers are 8 oz size, they don't take up room in the fridge and won't sit there for years while you try to finish one jar. The price is so reasonable for six containers, you can afford to gift one or two away.

I am on a sodium-restricted diet (1000 mg/day) and have taken the opportunity to learn how to make many of the condiments that I used to enjoy when I didn't care about salt.  I made a killer quart of Worchestershire Sauce using, in part, this tamarind paste.  The recipe used about 5 oz. of paste.  I use the sauce to season potroasts and hamburgers, so the six-pack would be about a year's supply for me.I don't know Pad Thai from bow tie, but in Worchestershire sauce this tamarind paste was just fine!
I bought this to make a sauce and it taste great gives a good flavor.  I really enjoyed it an it lasts a long time.

This paste is excellent. However, getting it in a pack of 6 was certainly more than I think I will need for a long time - but at this price, I just gave a few away to friends that love to cook as much as I do. One negative tho - one of the sealed foils on the inside of the item was not adhered and so some of the paste (which is actually more like a very thick syrup) had leaked out and was all over in side the bag. It didn't look like tampering as much as just didn't adhere in the filling and packaging process.

Came well packed but one foil seal a little bit shmooshed open, i think it might have happened when/if shipped by air, and atmospheric pressure popped it open. Did not look as if a person opened it, so i started with that one. I always cook it anyway.This Tamarind paste is a very good price and tastes great in anything that needs some sour taste, even good in savory soups.Would buy again but i think i am stocked for life. It should keep forever i think.:-)
My kids love soy chocolate milk. It is a great alternative to cow's milk if you are looking for one.
I drink this because of the low fat high protein content and when I drink it a t night it's like taking a sleeping pill. Amazing stuff.
As someone who is lactose intolerant, I was hesitant at first to try soymilk because my friends all said it was nasty.  I figured i'd give the chocolate flavor a try.  It's EXTREMELY YUMMY!:)
These have been a favorite for over 20 years, and to the best of my memories, it never has had nuts.

I rate this product four nuggets of goodness. Minus one nugget for not containing any nuts despite the name which strongly suggests the product contains nuts. However, that doesn't stop my wife from eating copious amounts of this breakfast cereal. It's by far her favorite, and we go through an absolute ton of it each year. I think it's tasty. Still wish it had some nuts in it.
As always these are great, my mom loves them. This is a huge box, I cant even find them in the store in this size. Thank You.

Having enjoyed the wonderful flavor for breakfast for the first time in a very long time, I decided to do some research on whether there were nuts.  (It has been a couple of years since I've eaten Honey Nut Cheerios, and I remembered nuts.)According to an article I read at Wikipedia,  General Mills introduced this delicious honey-and-nut flavored cereal in 1979 with almonds in it. The nuts, the article says, were discontinued in 2006.Now, let's take a look at the nutrional value.  Evidently we can expect the contents of this cereal to change periodically, because there is a statement to that effect on the Cheerios website.More or less, a small serving (3/4 cup) has 110 calories.  I don't usually want to stop at 3/4 cup of cereal.  That little serving has 9 grams sugar and 290 mg sodium.  It supplies 25% of a day's requirement of iron.  How many of us need all that iron?The good things included are 2 grams fiber and 50% of a day's requirement of folate, along with small amounts of vitamin A, vitamin C, calcium, vitamin D, thiamin, riboflavin, niacin, vitamin B6, vitamin B12, phosphorus, magnesium, and zinc.Ingredients include whole grain oats, sugar, oat bran, modified corn starch, honey brown sugar syrup, salt, canola and/or rice bran oil, and natural almond flavor.The box says that the product can help lower cholesterol and heart disease.I hope you will find this review helpful.

My brother just got his care package.  This isn't the first thing I sent him, since he has been deployed, but I think it is his favorite by far.  He said "...everything in there was delicious and unique. Shortly after I opened it, there was a crowd of people asking, "do you want that?" Your package was definitely a highlight of my day."  Defiantly purchase this for those soldiers that are deployed.  (I am not saying guys, because my brother works with many ladies as well.  Thank you ladies for all you do too!!!!!!!!)

These little nuts are amazing! Almonds are so healthy for us and add a little sweetness and this becomes the perfect treat. I love carrying this bag in my purse for a quick pick me up or even in place of popcorn or candy during a movie. Thank you Hail Merry for the delicious, healthy and different snack items.
I bought this to turn some Halloween cocktails black, did exactly what it was intended to do!  Worked perfectly :)

column9: Great for fussy babies and the not-so-fussy
column10: I have used Good Start Supreme for both of my children. My first baby was terribly colicky and would scream for an average of 6 hours a day. I used a few different kinds of formula after I finished BF and this is the only one that didn't give her terrible gas.As with any formula, give it two weeks of use before switching to something else. The doctors said that my first might have a milk allergy (She was gaining weight fantastically but I was supposed to cut dairy from my diet, try soy formula...). I didn't do any of those things. I used Good Start Supreme.She'd spit up about half of her bottle during and after every feeding with anything else - I was covered, she wore a bib all of her waking hours, and I wore a burp cloth on my shoulder all day. She'd would still spit up a bit with Good Start, but it cut it down by at least 2/3.My second child (2 years later) wasn't nearly as bad. No real gas, no spitting up but after finishing BF I wasn't going to take any chances. Both of my children had great weight gain and were healthy and content with this formula.If you'd like to give it one more shot before giving up, try Good Start for 2 weeks. I'm not a doctor though, just a mom that wanted to figure out what the yelling was all about before jumping on the allergy bandwagon. Depending on your own child's health issues, your experience may vary. I also recommend the Dr. Brown's bottles, especially for babies that have gas issues.The only reason it is not 5 stars is the price. I go through a large can every 6 days even though she has started solid food. It is expensive to feed my little one, especially if she doesn't finish her bottle.
I ordered the Nestle Good Start with DHA & ARA, but they sent me Gerber Good Start, Gentle Plus instead.  Also, the can is only 12 oz. and not the 24 oz can.  A rip off!

My two cats are very picky eaters. Up until recently, I was feeding them Royal Canin indoor cat formula. They loved the food, but one of the cats had constant diarrhea and bathroom problems, and the other would occasionally throw up undigested kibble. I began to research the food they were eating and kept finding a bunch of reviews about how the food is garbage for cats and very overpriced for what you get. I tried converting them to different types of wet food, and also a version of a Blue Buffalo cat food. They would not touch anything else and refused to eat. A couple of days ago I decided to try again, this time with Spot's Stew for Sensitive Cats in Turkey. From the time I opened the bag to when it was in their bowl, they showed interest in it. I guess the recipe is very attractive to cats. I've slowly begun mixing it in with their old food and hope that they will be fully transitioned within a few weeks. They don't show any aversion to the new food. In fact, I think they're going to the bowl more often. They almost never finished their daily portions (I follow the food portion charts) before, and now they do. I also have not experienced any sensitive stomach problems from either of them during the transition. I have my fingers crossed that this will be the food I was looking for. So far it's a keeper.Update a year later: My cats are still very much enjoying this food. The one that was throwing up undigested kibble hasn't done it since being switched. The other that had constant diarrhea and bathroom problems has also completely changed. They also seem much more energetic and playful than they were with the old food which also means they get into EVERYTHING but a healthy, happy cat makes me a happy owner. Thanks so much Halo! I couldn't recommend this food more.

column9: No more mess to clean up!
column10: I have two cats. One with a sensitive system and one without. They both luv this food ... and so do I! I had tried every brand there is out there claiming it was specially formulated for sensitive systems. None seemed to work. My poor cat with the sensitive system was throwing up about 2 to 3 times weekly. Once I switched to Halo for Sensitive Systems, he stopped. Sure there may be a hair ball or two once in a great while, but; no more piles of puke to clean up. Thank you Ellen and Halo for creating such a wonderful cat food. It is well worth the price.

I have 2 indoor cats, one has IBS, along with a matted coat & flaking skin. I have tried all the top brands but none seemed to help. Natural Balance, Wellness, NutroMax all seemed to bother his tummy, especially the wet food. I checked the reviews & ingredients on [...] and I switched to Halo dry sensitive food. I can see a real solid improvement in his coat in just one week. His coat is now very soft and shiny,the flakes are gone, & his hair isn't getting matted like it was. The IBS also seems to be getting better now that I primarily give him the dry food with just a little wet food in the morning. Halo is expensive, but they eat a lot less so the cost seems to even itself out. From now on Halo sensitive turkey is going to be the only cat food I will feed my cats.

Kitties taste vary but when we got this bag of kibbles it didn't take very long before ours were totally sold on it.  I was sold too when I reading the ingredients list has turkey and egg as the first two ingredients plus the vitamin E supplement is "mixed tocopherols" rather than the low-end synthetic choice "d-alpha tocopherols".

column9: HALO DRY CAT FOOD IS THE CAT'S MEOW
column10: Our cats were liking Newman's Organic dry cat food and Organix brand cat food, but they inhaled this Halo brand food! They even like it better than their cat treats. Pricey, but our cats love this brand of grain-free cat food. If you care about the health of your little ones, this food is worth the price.

I have a ten month old Persian kitten and have been dealing with loose, smelly stools with frequent diarrhea since I got him at three months.  He checked out fine at the vet, and I finally realized he must have some type of food allergy.  I had him on Wellness Kitten, then Adult food but an employee at the local pet food store suggested I try Halo.  It has a little less protein but almost twice the fiber of the Wellness, and it's made for pets with food allergies and sensitive GI tracks.He has always been a very picky eater, but he loves this stuff.  He even ripped open the bag when I was at work, something he never did with the Wellness.  Best of all, after only 5 days and while I am still transitioning him to the Halo, he stools are solid.  It's like a little miracle.  I no longer have to chase after him to check his bottom when he is done in the little box, nor do I come home to find stool tracked all through my house.  His stool also smells, well, not great, as it's still stool, but not as strong or nasty.I am so pleased with this food.  I highly suggest that anyone else also dealing with intractable soft stool and diarrhea give this food a try.  It's well worth the price.Update: My cat has been on this food now for about two and a half months.  He still loves it.  And he is still having solid, not disgusting stool.  Very happy with this food, and Halo in general.

I switched to this food because one of my cats had chewed raw spots on her back and nothing I tried helped her chronic itchy back.  The vet suggested the condition could be due to a food allergy and recommended I try a natural food with no preservatives or additives.  It took several months of using this product but my cat is much better.  The food also smells good and fresh which I like -- I have to smell it too.  The packaging is well-made and resealable.  Both my cats seem to love the food and are thriving.  It's a little pricey, but worth it in my opinion.

column9: This is a first - MY CATS ASKED ME TO SUBMIT THEIR REVIEW!
column10: WE (3 of us) love this stuff.  The little morsels are pretty small, so we get more of them, and they're easy to munch.  Just a little bit allows us to graze all day long (and into the night after our dinner feeding)  It's easy on our tummy's - no more up-chucking (unless, of course, we've got a fur-ball!)  And our coats are really nice - we still shed whenever possible, but the dander is almost gone, which is a big deal 'cause one of our friends was always sneezing when around us.  Mom was hoping we'd lose some weight since this stew is all natural and healthy without all the fattening fillers in the cheaper stuff, but so far, we're maintaining our hefty weight.  However, she's gonna keep buying this, because she knows in the long run, it's the best thing for our health.  Did we mention she mixes it with the Chicken Stew so we do get a bit of variety in taste. pretty good morsels... pur-r-r-r

This cat food has been great for my cat.  He has a sensitive stomach and this solved the problem.  When we got our cat he was one year old and was being fed very cheap food by his previous owners. His fur felt like wire and he had digestive issues.  We switched him to this food when we got him and now his fur is very soft and shiny and his digestive issues are cleared up. We have had him for over 2 years now. Everyone always comments on how healthy he looks.
I needed to find a cat food for my cats that was healthy and also tasted good.  Alot of the cat food at the grocery do not meet that criteria.  I am very pleased with Halo and my cats love it.

I switched six cats to this Halo product. Cats are aged two through twelve. They all enjoy it and their digestion does seem much better. Very little kitty barf these days. Great product for the felines you love!
My cats really seem to like this food, although they are not picky.  I love the ingredient list - you really cannot get better than that!

column9: Great cat food. Shiny soft cats
column10: I started feeding this mixed with their usual brand about 2 months ago and I love it. The cats like it, unlike the grain-free, and it is making their fur soft and shiny. One of my cats was getting very over weight and he's starting to trim down. And there is also less mess in the litter box.  I love that it is made with real meat and healthy veggies. I wish I could afford to feed ONLY Halo Spot's Stew to my furbabies, I know it would be better for them.  I love this stuff.

Would give the full 5-star rating but for the high price. There's no reason they can't create and sell a 10-lb bag for $21.50 as with the just-as-good "Natural Balance Dry Cat Food, Limited Ingredient Diet Green Pea and Duck Formula, 10 Pound Bag." Both products are good for cats with sensitive systems. The 3 cats here liked the pea/duck food a little better than the Halo, but just marginally. I would buy both, were the prices equal. Either of these foods is superior to Science Diet. It's worth mentioning that the cats ate less of the two products above than they consumed of Science Diet and with better all-around results. So those 2 foods go farther per dollar.DON'T judge cat reactions to this type of food immediately. They are often drawn to flavors added to cheap-ingredient foods but, in our case at least, as some months have gone by, the 3 guys are increasingly drawn to the healthier foods.

column9: Healthy, natural and they love it
column10: One of our cats has chronic stomach issues, this is the only food that he can keep down.  The other cats also love this food.  We wish it came in a larger bag

column9: Cat doesn't puke this stuff up
column10: mr miowyagi developed a sensitive stomach after getting stomach surgery.  After trying a few different cat foods, we found that this one does the trick.No more puking!  I'll pay any price (within reason of course) not to have to clean up cat puke every day, so I highly recommend this.Mr. Miowyagi is a very happy cat again and loves eating this stuff.Thanks Halo for making such a stomach-friendly product!

I bought this product initially on recommendation of the Animal Site on-line.  You click the button and it gives free donations to charitable organizations.  It sounded very natural and healthy for my cat.  One cat had stomach issues, so I was looking for something to help calm his stomach.  This seemed about as good as I could find out there.  But it is expensive.  But it's better than cleaning up cat barf.  I buy it at Petco, as well as on-line.  Your cat might like it too.

The dried vegetable products are great when making roasts, meatloafs, potatoe and macaroni salads or soups.  The dehydrated foods are always available when you need them and don't spoil.  They are good for emergencys and in the long run, you save money.

column9: Tasty, balanced black tea with a hint of cardamom
column10: Wonderful black tea with a touch of natural cardamom flavor.  I use an Ekobrew Refillable K-Cup Ekobrew Cup, Refillable Cup for Keurig K-cup Brewers, Brown, 1-Count with my Keurig to brew one tea bag for a tall glass of tea.  I stir in some sugar and pour this tea over ice.  It's lovely cold.  I have not tried it hot yet.  I don't think I'll ever get sick of it, and that's a good thing since there are 100 tea bags!

I have recently gotten into loose teas, along with a friend of mine. Both of us enjoy the flavor of this tea. I gave it only 4 stars because of how fine the tea is. It easily fits through all of my infusers, and I end up with a lot of it in my mug/tumbler (a lot more than any other brand of loose tea I've tried). The only way I see around this is to use the paper filters for individual servings.
This tea is the best for when you want to relax and fall asleep. It has a great taste and does not require much sweetner ,if any.

column9: After 50 bags I have an opinion - not good but great coffee
column10: As a lawyer for primiarily Italian and French clients, offering a coffee is a serious matter! My clients' response to Weavers was "amazing" and "an American roasted coffee"??? One bag a week in my office is a minimum. Very full bodied, it is immediately distinguishable from any and all US competitors. For the first time I have stopped using sugar or milk ... the coffee speaks for itself. Bravo ... Bravissimo.

column9: If you are not too crazy about acidity in your coffee, this is the one to go
column10: I liked it so much and decided to subscribe. One of the perfect coffee beans I had in years. If you like refined, some what  mild, yet have good presence in aftertaste... I highly recommend this one.

column9: Honestly, you MUST try this coffee!
column10: With all of the big brand coffees out there, Weaver's is a diamond in the rough and smokes all of the other brands. I was Star Struck for many years but didn't realize that I was consuming an acidic, metallic coffee unnecessarily.  I came across Weaver's at a friend's house and was blown away.  2 years later, I am a convert and will never go back to  big brands that fail to deliver.  If you're going to bother to drink coffee (or better yet, brew it at home from whole beans), then try Weaver's organic whole bean coffee.  Do what I did -- I conducted my own taste test with my coffee drinking friends using several well known brands and Weaver's came out on top unanimously.  Give it a try. You'll never go back to the other brews.

column9: French Roast is probably the best coffee in the line.  Here is my 2 cents
column10: I discovered Weavers at the Food Block party last year at warner Brothers.  They were serving samples and one of the employees gave me half a pound of the French.  I have to say this coffee is one of the best coffees I have tasted.  Smooth ! Low acidity and such powerful flavor.  Love it.Ordered a gift box this Xmas, and discovered the TEA ! So excited.  I have tried the French, Organic blend and Astral.  I read the story behind it and loved how its hand roasted in the bay area.  All that aside, love it !  The shipping is  a lil high but worth it !

column9: Not as good as other reviewers said.
column10: Based on reviews of the Weaver's French Roast Organic Coffee, I was looking forward to my first cup.  Sorry to say that I was disappointed.  I found the coffee to be "thin,"  and not full-bodied although I used 4 heaping spoonfuls to 3 cups of water.I've been trying different brands of French Roast since First Colony went out of business and thus far have not found a replacement.  The Weavers was the 4th brand I've tried from Amazon and since there are lots more brands out there, I'm going to keep trying.

This is by far the best coffee so far on Amazon.  I was drinking Kickin Horse but this has it beat.  It has a rich full flavor and I am very picky when it comes to drinking a great cup of Java...this is it.  You will not be disappointed.

I've ordered this coffee 1 time so far & it was excellent.  It's not over-roasted/burnt tasting & the flavor is very complex.  The beans are oily, black & I found no quakers (underdeveloped coffee beans that make coffee taste awful - they stick out because they do not roast/darken properly).  That's a good test of coffee beans:  empty the bag on a cookie sheet & see how many quakers you find.  A few is "acceptable" but more than 10 is pretty bad in my opinion.  If you've always been disappointed in dark roast coffee, you may want to give this a try.  Another dark roast sold on Amazon that I like is: Kicking Horse Coffee Kick Ass Dark, Whole Bean Coffee, 2.2-Pound PouchI use the "pour over" method to brew coffee every day because at this time, there is only one non-commercial drip coffeemaker that gets water to the ideal brewing temperature of 192F to 204 F.  I use cold, filtered water, a Melitta natural brown filter, manual drip coffee filter & brew directly into my stainless carafe.  I heat the water to boiling, pour a few tablespoons over the grounds to saturate & plump up the beans, wait a minute & then flood the grounds with the rest of the water.  There is a lot of crema, the beautiful reddish brown foam that develops on top of the beans, & it smells & tastes wonderful.I brew directly in to this carafe using this coffee cone (pour over method):RSVP Manual Drip Coffee Filter Cone for Carafes or ThermosI use this grinder:Bodum Bistro Electric Burr Coffee Grinder, BlackI use this water kettle to heat the water:Oster 5965 Stainless-Steel 1-1/2-Liter Electric Water KettleI use these coffee filters:Melitta 626412 40 Count #6 Natural Brown Cone Coffee Filters
I am on a quest to find the best rich dark coffee for my wife and I. This coffee was good but not great. I found it to be somewhat bitter.
These beans are fresh and outstanding. Smooth and vibrant dark roast. Try this one first and you will not be hopping around looking for a new brand. The best
I received 2 bags of this coffee, the 2nd one smelled like mold after being brewed.  Makes me not want to order again.
Have tried several of weavers coffees and haven't been dissappointed yet. Always smooth without acidity or bite to it. Same flavor, same smooth rich delicous taste every cup just perfect.

This tea is outstanding!! When I first brewed a cup, I was concerned how light in color it was, thinking weak tea. Then I took a sip. Great!! I have other Nilgiri's, one from Tao of Tea and another from a local tea merchant, but this Davidson's Nilgiri is the best of the three, and cost a LOT less. The flavor is complex and I agree with another reviewer about the flavors in the tea. The body is medium to light, as compared to Assam or even Keemun, but very satisfying.
This is like a cross between english black, darjeeling and a lightly oxidized oolong.  I like it.

My husband is from the area where this tea is grown. It's grown in Munnar, Kerala bordering on Tamil Nadu, Bodinyakanur is the town he's from. I understand this is also grown in Kodaikonnal as well. Both are hill stations and beautiful places to visit if you are ever in South India and want a break from the heat.I am very spoiled, I usually can manage to conjure up someone to send me real nilgiri. The last time I was in India I packed a whole suitcase full of the gold label nilgiri (the frost, 5 lb bags). Long story short, it didn't last as long as I hoped...we ended up having a few kids...and I didn't get back to get more. My inlaws bought me some but it was low quality definately not export quality. And, I ordered from misc. places online. I ended up stumbling on this and I am so so so grateful!This is the nilgiri I was looking for. It's so bold but the tea itself is light. I make ice tea out of it in the summer and everyone is always shocked when they taste it. It packs a punch! This is perfect of me, and I'm on subscription now so I don't run out. But, I'm thinking I'll need two of these a month now that two of my boys are tea drinkers too.I did find a few pieces of sticks in mine. I am not bothered at all. And, certainly am not deducting a star for that. I am impressed that I've found a good quality nilgiri at a decent price! I paid double for a very inferior brand!! Thank you so much for offering this, I am in heaven. And, tonight I'm making a curry to go with my Indian tea.

column9: Brewed hay would probably taste like this
column10: I really wanted to like this tea (it is good for me, a student to like all things inexpensive). And I have had good experience with Davidson's in the past. So I ignored all the previous negative reviews and bought this. This tea has no body, no complexity - I imagine that steeped hay would taste something like this.

I have tried multiple ways of brewing this and its crappy tea! I am sorry I got a pound but thankfully it wasn't very expensive.. this stuff is just bitter beyond words. I tried to love it but I just cannot get the stuff to not be so bitter.

I do not like this tea,it taste nothing like a Nilgiri that I have gotten before through another place that no longer carries it.It is not as complex nor as smooth.I am also not sure if I got the right tea?The big label read Irish breakfast tea and another smaller label on the bottom read Dunsandle Nilgiri?Also as far as taste I am no good at describing the taste but I know what I like and this is not it.

The tea tastes good, doesn't have a particularly complex flavor. It tasted bitter and unpleasant at first, but I realized that it was the Stevia I sweetened it with, not the tea. Since switching sweeteners I've been happier with the tea and I'll probably get more of this blend.Take care not to steep the tea longer than five minutes to prevent bitterness. I've been steeping it for four minutes and it's working out great.

column4: W. Robert Kiser "Happily living in Tidewater"
column10: I've ordered these before and was quite pleased.  This order was a disappointment.  It would appear that the anchovy filets have broken down into a congealed mess of almost anchony paste.  I will not order these again sight unseen.  Although is product is about 20% more expensive in my local grocery, I will buy there where I can see exactly what I'll be taking home.  My advice to others is to do the same.

When I opened the jar I was very disappointed because the jar was NOT filled with anchovy fillets. The fillets were pushed against the side of the jar so looking at the packaging it looked full but the center of the jar was just filled with olive oil!! I feel ripped off.The fish itself tasted fine, but it's not worth this price!!

*****This little bowl is great--I use it for eggs and more because it's so handy and has so many design features that I like. First of course, is the built-in blade for cracking eggs. The whole bowl is melamine (a type of hard plastic) and the blade is too, so it's not anything you'd cut yourself on. But it certainly does help by providing a convenient place to crack an egg. I don't tend to be good at this and end up getting egg white on whatever I normally use, so this blade really helps and does truly minimize shell fragments. The bowl is sturdy too, so it doesn't rock when you crack an egg hard. Also, it doesn't move because of the non-slip rubber ring on the bottom. And the handle sticks out so that you can hold it while you're mixing whatever is in the bowl; the handle is nice and big and suitable for both right and left-handers.The bowl holds up to a dozen eggs and is safe for the dishwasher, but cleans easily by hand too (I don't have a dishwasher). It's such a nice size (1.5 quarts) that I use it for lots of different things; the handle makes it very useful. Plus it's yellow and white, just like an egg--too cute! I think kids would like this too--it would help them to learn how to work with eggs, it's fun and colorful, and it doesn't slip around. Great bowl!Highly recommended.*****
An excellent device. It could be used as a general-purpose bowl, but I prefer to save it for eggs (scrambled and omelettes)-- for which it is particularly handy.

These little cups are so convenient, and surprisingly flavorful with a nice kick of chipotle spice flavor. Make a great lunch at the office, perfect for warming up when it's cold too! The spiciness is fairly mild, but definitely there. It is a bit mushy for my taste (beans aren't whole) but I'd much rather have that than those dehydrated soups that never fully hydrate.

This soup is totally delicious. I don't even know how to describe it. It's just great. It has a little zing to it. Not too spicy though; I don't like spicy things, and I like it.Be sure to let it set for a while after you cook it. The texture is much smoother after you let it sit.

column9: I like my oatmeal like I like my men
column10: Thick and Chunky! Well, I like my oatmeal that way anyway. It takes a bit longer than regular oatmeal to mush up, but who cares!

This oatmeal rocks.  It is inexpensive, but very high quality.  It cooks up perfectly.  Although it is rolled thick, the texture is very soft and is not offensive.  This is very hearty oatmeal.  I can't wait to make oatmeal cookies. :)This is the kind of oatmeal that makes you want to sing in the morning!

Ordered as a gift, they were not what was expected.  The chocolate covered cherries were in fact candies NOT cherries.  Also the peanuts were coated in something spicy and not advertised as such.  Also the quantity was smaller than expected.  I will not order again.

My kids love these. They like that there is a grape flavor to it and it is a nice change from plain applesauce. They are convenient to pack in the lunches for school and the perfect size for my younger ones.

Our twin boys are 16 months old and these are still the highlight snack. They are able to feed themselves, other than when they get to the bottom, that usually requires us to squeeze more to the top for them.  The cap is too small for them to get a hold of so we usually have to hide that somewhere.
My kids love this juice/squeezer. The package is very conviniant. I love it cause you do not have to store it in the refregerator unless you open it.
Not as salty as other misos. Mellow for a winter miso. Fast shipping. A bit pricey compared to miso at the local market, but organic and no alcohol.

We'd been looking for organic miso and couldn't find it at local stores; glad we found this at Amazon; easy purchase and it's delicious.  Easy to prepare, be sure not to over heat because that kills it.  Enjoy!

column9: High in salt, unlike what the nutrition information says.
column10: I bought this because there is an external site that says there is no salt, and the nutrition information says no salt. Actually each TBSP contains 680mg of salt (28% of your daily intake).

column9: Hatcho Miso or not Hatcho miso
column10: Hatcho miso is made in Okazaki a town in Aichi prefecture in Japan, that's about 250 miles from Sendai for the over- excited. It is the most famous miso in Japan. Warlord Tokugawa (Richard Chamberlains 15th Century Shogun buddy) was it's most famous advocate. He drank Hatcho miso soup everyday. Japan's current Emperor is also a "customer"The only authentic Hatcho is exported by Mitoku company. Eden foods are listed by Mitoku as an importer of authentic Hatcho. However, this web page proclaims in a couple of places that the product being sold is made from 100% American soybeans!It has a very earthy flavor. Salt content is fairly high, but, one doesn't eat a sufficiently large quantity to be much of a problem unless one has real health problems with any amount of excess salt.Personally, I believe the benefits from eating miso products far outway the possible detriments.The price being asked is high for genuine Hatcho miso and ridiculously high if the product is in fact American made.Eden/Amazon need to clarify.Caveat Emptor.
A nice tasting miso.  It is salty, but you don't need to use a lot to make a good soup broth.  Add it at the end of cooking so it doesn't get over heated.

column9: I cant get the same taste as restaurant
column10: I cant get the same taste a restaurant or even packaged dry Miso even with good organic ingredients....probably just my cooking skills.  I will go with the packaged dry Miso next time

If you think teas is just for when you are sick, you are saddenly mistakenIf you think decaf tea is "weak", I urge you to try again with the Twinnings Irish Breakfast decaf. This isn't a herbal tea that tastes like your neighbors' old grass clippings. This is real tea.This tea has a rich, strong flavor without bitterness. It has a more robust flavor than Twinning's English Breakfast, which is also quite good. This tea is quite good in the morning as a wake up for those of us who have to avoid caffeine. And of course it's great at night because it doesn't have caffeine to keep you up.I recommend everybody and anybody to try this tea. It is yummy.

After moving to the US from England, I searched long and hard to find a decent cup of tea.  The usual US tea is weak compared to tea in England.  Twinings Irish Breakfast Decaf Tea has great flavour.  It's a very satisfying taste and the beauty of decaf tea is that even though it is stronger in taste, you do not feel wired.  I would highly recommend this product.

column9: The best decaf black tea out there
column10: Caffeine can often be a problem for me and I often like to have a comforting cup of tea in the evening.  I have tried most of the decaffeinated black teas out there and most are poor quality and/or very weak.  I'm not overly fond of herbal "teas," Earl Grey or green teas and this is the best decaffeinated black tea I've found, at least readily available in the States.  Though not as strong as the equivalent caffeinated Twinings version, it is pretty close and has a lovely full-bodied flavor without bitterness.  If you like your tea on the stronger side, simply allow a minute or so longer steeping time on this one(I tend to drink mine brewed strong with a bit of milk).I admit there are caffeinated black teas (including several loose teas) that I prefer over this one, but based on a lot of searching, this is the best of the decafs and I'm glad it's available for an evening cuppa. I still think there is room for improvement in this product area, but this one is pretty good and is definitely a step above the rest of the field.

Twinnings Irish Breakfast is the best grocery-sold decaf tea I've discovered (yet).  I like my tea, apparently, extremely strong: for a normal mug I will use 2 bags of this stuff and let it steep for 8 or 9 minutes.  (Then I add lots of milk and a bit of sugar....yum.)  If you do the math this is about 6x more tea-steeping than recommended on the box.  With other brands, such as Trader Joe's Irish decaf, I will use 3 teabags and let it steep for 9 or 10 minutes, and it still won't have much flavor to it.  I think this is more of a problem with decaf teas than with my taste buds, for what it's worth.  When I brew a cup of caffeinated tea it just takes one teabag for perhaps 7 or 8 minutes to get a really nice strong cup of tea.  So, while this tea, to me, isn't up to the standards of a really good caffeinated tea, or to what you'll get in a nice tea cafe, it's good enough that I don't feel sorry for myself when I'm drinking a cup.  It's ridiculously expensive in my local grocery store ($5 for 20 bags, which works out to 50 cents a serving when I'm using two bags per cup!), so I'm going to start buying it from Amazon now.The English Breakfast variant is "okay", but I definitely prefer this Irish tea, with its stronger flavor.
Twinings makes great tea and I can't even tell this one is decaf.
I normally only buy the caffeine and never the decaf but this was living up to the Twining's tea label and it great taste!
I've always been a coffee drinker until a friend introduced me to Twinings Irish breakfast decaffeinated tea, now I occasionally have a cup of coffee but always look forward to my morning cup of tea.

column9: No bitterness in this full bodied decaf tea
column10: Too often I find black teas develop an unappealing bitterness, but that is not a problem with this lively decaf tea.  I had every intention of ordering the decaf Earl Grey because I love bergamot, but my order was hijacked by an unleashed desire to try something new.  Most decaffeinated beverages produce a different flavor and strength from their unprocessed counterpart, but the full mouth flavor remains intact with this tea.  It is a combination of black teas and nothing else, no flavorings, no additions, and this is a wonderfully satisfying beverage for a purist.  The bag which is like the "flo-through" Lipton bags I remember from years ago is attached to a white cotton thread which appears to be knotted at the bag and the paper tag and there is no metal staple.  Each bag is in a fully sealed smooth paper pouch which is also biodegradable, another advantage.  I thought Twinings used light paper envelopes, so that was a fantastic surprise which I appreciate.  I have drunk it with a Splenda but intend to have it with skim milk as well tomorrow.  It was perfect with Trader Joe's Orange Cardamom cookies.  I'll definitely enjoy drinking this tea and recommend it highly, especially to drinkers of peaty Scotch beverages like Laphroaig.
I like really strong tea, which is almost impossible to get as decaf.  This tea is the best I've found, although I personally use 2 bags for my ginormous cup.
Full bodied for a decaf with great, smooth taste.  Only complaint is that it doesn't do as well with lemon as it does with milk and creamer.
I get so tired of trying to accommodate the whims of the local retailers that I now purchase what I want online! Let the local stores play games; I don't have to shop there!  love this tea.

Very smooth and satisfying.  I am allergic to caffiene and this tea fills the desire for a warm cup in the morning.  Have with milk.  Love getting it on my front porch and also use it at my Cafe. With my subscription and Amazon Prime, it's a bargain.

In New Jersey, I could regularly buy this tea in the store and did.  In Colorado, the available decaf teas are very limited.  I was pleased to find that amazon carried my favorite Twinings decaf teas.  This and English Breakfast are my favorites.

I love the great, rich, Irish flavor of this tea.  I buy it whenever I am running low. The price is a bit high, but overall, I am very satisfied with the quality of this product.  The packaging could be more condensed, allowing for delivery to a mailbox.
Twinings Decaf tea is a refreshing cup of tea at anytime of the day.

This is not a strong nor malty tea, the taste is average- nothing particular outstanding or  to applaude. I have not experience the "decaffinated" effects of this tea, although the words do  carry a placebo effect.I have found tea package in America/Canada from Twining do not have same quality as the Twining sold in England:London/Heathrow Airports. Just not the same in terms of the flavour. Very deceiving as it does not indicate on the website as where it has been packaged.

I love split pea soup.  This one is just the way it would taste if it were home made.  It has a sprinkling of celery in it, but if I had a wish it would also have carrots too.  I will reorder when I'm almost done with what I have.

They always arrive quickly, in great condition, fresh and everything.Sour Skittles are tasty.Oh, plus these are the bigger packages of them, which is neat.

Skittles Sour is my second favorite since my favorite is no longer available. But if the company that owns Life Saver candy ever has enough common sense to start manufacturing the Wild Berry Sours again I'll go back to them in a heartbeat!!!

Have a delicious day! Wish I wrote that but it's off the box.So is this "We make glutenfree delicious..it's what we do" and boy did Glutenfreeda do it again.I've been hooked on Glutenfreeda products since they introduced their frozen cookies years ago. I was delighted to see them come out with instant oatmeal and I wasn't disappointed.I was doubly delighted to see the oatmeal offered on Amazon.com. Win,win! When you read the ingredient list you will see why- Off the Maple Raisin with Flax box :certified gluten free oats, raisins, organic maple sugar,brown sugar , flax meal and salt.That's it and yes you read the ingredient list correctly.Real ingredients for my real family.I was very happy to see a very low sodium content and the addition of flax.I always have a packet with me for a quick snack or those "eat at the desk" lunches. I really love this oatmeal. I think it tastes delicious and is a perfect G free breakfast treat. It is just like all regular instant microwave oatmeal and you don't know it is different at all

I live by this oatmeal Every morning, Much better than using plain oatmeal. I eat a package mixed with a scoop of Whey Factors natural French Vanilla protein powder, a half cup of frozen wild blueberries and about 15 frozen raspberries. It's like eating really tasty pie filling.
This great tasting oatmeal is highly recommended.  Its relative low sugar and delicious taste make this my favorite hot cereal.  Throw in the fact that its gluten free and this one is a winner.

column9: Flavor is good, but Eww, texture!
column10: This review is for the texture snobs in the world.  As others have mentioned in their reviews, the flavor is great and the ingredients/nutrition are better.  Hold on, though:  there's a "but" coming.Remember the flavored instant oatmeal we ate before we knew what "organic" or "gluten" meant?  Brightly colored "banana" bits held onto their fake yellow color and their cubic shape long after the hot water mushified the oats for us.  We ate fake crap, and we liked it.We're older and wiser now, and want real bananas:  real bananas that we re-hydrate ourselves with our steaming hot filtered water for optimum health and enjoyment.Except that rehydrated banana bits don't stay in bit form.  Nor do they rehydrate to sliced banana consistency.  Nay!  Rehydrated banana bits taste like delicious, wholesome bananas, and have the consistency of runny snot.That's right:  runny snot.I love everything else about this oatmeal, but when I want to feel snot run down my throat, I'll go out and contract the common cold, thank you very much.Based on other reviews, this doesn't throw everyone.  Based on other reviews, you might love this oatmeal and shrug off the banana snot texture without a second thought.  But if you're a huge texture snob, I thought you might want to know what you're getting into.I will shudder and finish the rest of my banana oatmeal one snot-filled bowl at a time (unless I can't take it anymore, at which point the food bank gets a wholesome and delicious donation), but I won't purchase this again.  I think I'll slice bananas into gluten-free oatmeal the next time I feel a bananas-and-cream craving.Best of luck with your oatmeal experience, and thank you for pausing to read a different perspective.

I have found this to be a great cereal that doesn't contain any of the normal allergen products. It tastes great and the flax seed is great for the body. I highly recommend this to anyone searching for a hot meal without the junk inside!
I love eating the banana/flax oatmeal anytime of the day. its my favorite flavor. tried them all. I add more water then called for and microwave a bit longer.

My kids love this oatmeal, especially with a little vanilla coconut milk creamer on top. It is so nice to have something they can make for themselves in the morning that is hot and filling. It's good that it comes in a case, because we go through it fast! It's also great for when we are travelling because it is easy to pack and quick to make.

My daughter and I love this and are happy to have it available, as we both are on gluten-free diets and missed the convenience and taste of instant hot oatmeal.  It is very satisfying and healthy, too.

column9: Good to be able to eat oats again. :)
column10: These are perfect for a person with Celiac Disease who is looking for a quick, tasty, healthy breakfast.  They are low in sugar and high in fiber and protein.  They certainly aren't as sweet as conventional instant oatmeal, but that's what makes it much better for the health-conscious person. :)  And a good price here on Amazon, too!

I have been gluten-free for over 5 years and dairy and soy-free for 9 months. My daughter has been corn-free for quite some time and gluten and dairy-free for the past 10 months. We were ecstatic when we learned about Glutenfreeda's Oatmeal being safe for both of us. It had been soooo long since I could make a packet of flavored oatmeal in a jiffy. And with my daughter's corn-allergy, it has been even longer for her. We are now in heaven and love all three flavors, but my favorite is the Banana Maple. We eat it for breakfast, snacks, whatever. It isn't as sweet as we both like it, but a spoon of demerara organic sugar and we're both ready to enjoy.Anyone who can buy any brand or kind of instant oatmeal off the shelf just can not fathom our excitement, but it is truly a wonderful thing to be able to enjoy instant oatmeal again!!
I love the other Glutenfreeda oatmeal flavers (apple and maple raisin) but the banana tastes so awful: stale, musty, like it has been kept in a cellar and aged for 20 years. Ugh.

column9: As Anthony Hopkins said in "84 Charing Cross Road" (1987) "Very nice, very tasty"
column10: This critter serves several purposes. First, as my cats will point out if you sit on the box you own it (cat rules). Second, when the box is empty, and if you are big enough you can be stuck in it.This tasty meal in a pop-top can, reminiscent of C rations takes some strength and skill to open so you will not hear the sound of lids pealing back in the middle of the night and cats slurping the juice.Some cats rub on the hand that opens the can. Others wait until you are out of sight before you hear them devouring the tasty can innards. Bottom line is this product is part of a balanced diet and has yet to encounter any detractors.

Even though the cats love the Friskies, I cannot go higher than a 3 star rating because it doesn't have the best ingredients.  I feel better buying it over other brands even though I don't care for the artificial ingredients and by-products because to my knowledge, Friskies was not on the Cat Food Recall that killed peoples pets.As far as the price goes, I cannot figure it out but Amazon is a total rip-off.  At Petsmart these are .40 a can.  The price here is like .67.  It is not a deal!  Not one bit.  Now, if Amazon changes the price after this review to be comparable to Petsmart or even the grocery store for that matter, then that means they wised up.  It is for the purchase of 24 cans.  Two 12 packs.  NOT two 24 packs (like I thought).  To return them would cost like $10 so it's not worth it.  Do the math before you buy to make sure you don't rip yourself off!

My cats diet is solid food. I bought this as a treat for him as he gets a little grumpy when we bring the dog in from long walks or trips to the park. I figured a spoon full would make a decent treat and each can would last about a week. At first my cat looked at me like I was nuts and he wasn't overly fond of the stuff. I thought that I would end up giving it to my friends who have a ton of cats as it wouldn't go to waste at their house. in the meantime I still kept giving my cat a spoonful every time the dog got to do something fun. My cat now loves this stuff and im ordering my second 24-pack. Highly recommend.

column9: I love my cats. but you can get this at the grocery store...and cheaper!
column10: I love Amazon, but this is probably the first time that I am shocked at the price. Not how low it is, but how HIGH it is! I can't believe the price they want for this case of Friskies cat food. I live in a big city and have my choice of plenty places to go to get my cat food. The price at the local Petsmart is 47 cents (regular price) or 44 cents (on sale). Do you see my point yet? Even if I paid 47 cents a can, do the math .47 x 24 = $11.28! Amazon wants what? $18.94! I do admit that the pate is my cats favorite, as they don't like to eat the shredded or the fillet types of canned cat food. I highly recommend the types of pate that are in this case: the Turkey and Giblets is a BIG favorite with the kitties and salmon doesn't stay long on the plate either! I have seven cats with an age range of 4 months to 16 years old, and all they will eat is Friskies canned cat food and their dry food. I recommend these Friskies items, but you are better off going to the grocery store, Petsmart or even Walmart. I will love you Amazon until the day I die, but I won't buy my Friskies from you. :(

I support a local animal shelter, too which I provide food monthly. By ordering in bulk, not only do I save money but it helps my budget in contributing to saving animals lives. The food is always shipped and delivered professionally and on time. I have tried buying in bulk at discount stores, but my time and gas factored in does not make it as cost effective as having it delivered to my home. Would highly recommend.

I bought this cat food because of the wonderful low price and I enjoy the adorable cat on the commercials. My cats did eat this food, in fact they really enjoyed it. However, after reading the ingredients and doing some research, I completely regret purchasing it and feel just awful for feeding it to my cats. The first three ingredients are (which indicates the most prevalent ingredients) are ground yellow corn, corn gluten meal, and chicken by-product meal. How disgusting is that?! The main ingredient is a cheap corn filler. One thing my vet told me a while back that I never forgot: "When you eat corn, what comes out of the other end? The same thing happens with cats and dogs." Basically, corn cannot be fully digested, it is just a filler and causes pets to actually eat more to feel full, poop out more (more for us to clean in the litter box), and retain less nutrients. The only meat in Friskies at all is a by-product, its not even a real meat! By-products are the stuff leftover once all the actual meat is harvested. We're talking beaks, chicken feet, eyeballs, even chicken poop! I would not recommend this product to anyone, for any reason, ever. It is an absolutely awful cat food. I suppose you get what you pay for. I think the only reason why it was cat-approved may be because it contains artificial flavors that taste good to cats and because I usually feed them dry food for dental reasons and wet food puts off much more of a scent for them to enjoy. I recommend to stay far away from Friskies, as it is simply a very low quality filler food. Even though the price is quite inexpensive, your cat will actually eat more than if you paid for a better quality food, because they will never feel full. Cats need to eat meat, and there just isn't real meat in this food. When purchasing a cat (or dog) food, the most important thing to consider is the first 3 ingredients; just make sure those first three are decent ingredients that you would eat yourself. Now that I know what to look for, I usually buy my pets all natural, dry foods such as Blue Buffalo, Halo or Wellness. All of those brands contain real, whole meats that I myself would eat, with no added fillers or corn.

When shopping for Bay leaves, you must ask: Do I want Bay Laurel leaves or California Bay leaves?  The former have a mild, pleasant flavor that is faintly cardamom-y and very faintly spicy.  They are sufficiently mild and tasty that, several minutes after popping one in my mouth to verify the quality of the product, I'm still sucking on it because it's quite nice.  California Bay, on the other hand, has a very strong, medicinal taste.  If you have purchased dried Bay leaves in the past, you probably bought California Bay.  Cooking with Bay Laurel will be a different but, in all likelihood, very pleasing experience.  Serious chefs such as Jerry Traunfeld advise simply omitting Bay when California Bay is all that is available.This Bay, in particular, is of a suitable quality.  The jars come quite packed with leaves and the leaves themselves are generally not damaged.  There is nothing so miraculous about it that it necessarily deserves five stars by comparison to other Bay Laurel, but by comparison to California Bay, it deserves six.

column9: Not actually for use in espresso machines
column10: Few things I'd like to point out:1.  "Espresso" is not a roast.  It's a drink.  In northern Italy they make espresso from Vienna roast, in southern Italy they use French.  Starbucks appears to be using French roast, so they should just label it French roast like any normal person would.2.  The product description says "Taste Espresso Roast as both a shot of espresso and brewed in a coffee press. This is one versatile coffee!"  This is patently absurd.  It's pre-ground coffee, and it's either for use in espresso machines or presses, but not both.  Here's why:Making a shot of espresso requires a very fine grind.  Making coffee press coffee requires a very course grind.  If you have ground coffee that is appropriate for espresso machines, it will pass through the filter in a coffee press and you will have a cup of sludge.  If you use ground coffee that does not pass through a press's filter in an espresso machine, you do not get espresso.  You get cafe crema, which is a good, but entirely different, beverage.Therefore, a "Universal Grind" is an impossibility.  They should tell you on the label what kind of coffee maker it's ground for, like normal people.3.  It's over-roasted.  Starbucks has an excellent bean-sourcing operation that buys better coffee than any other company of its size.  Then they roast all their beans Vienna or French.  Most beans taste best at a particular level of roasting that varies with the bean, and for most beans that level is not Vienna or French.  So why roast all your beans too dark?  I guess it's just easier that way.  Also, it lets them rename Vienna Roast as "Starbucks Roast" because the Austrians don't seem to care.That said, this is still better than what you get in the supermarket - Starbucks specializes in coffee and sources much better beans than any of the companies that also make cheese, hot dogs, shampoo or cigarettes.Anyway, if you really want some good coffee, do this:Buy a grinder.  Nothing makes coffee lose flavor like keeping it around after grinding.  If you have a drip coffee machine, get a grinder with spinning blades; if you have something else like a press or vacuum pot, get a grinder with burrs.  If you have an espresso machine, get a very nice grinder with burrs.  Amazon has good deals on all three kinds, just do a search for 'coffee grinder'.  It's not that much money, and if you're somebody who's willing to pay for Starbucks you should invest in one.Find a local coffee shop that roasts their own coffee and gives you the date it's roasted on.  Freshness matters!  Good beans don't taste nearly as good after they've been sitting around.Ask the people at your local shop to tell you about the correct amount of beans to use.  Most people don't use the right amount.  If you don't use enough, your coffee comes out bitter, especially if you have a drip machine.  Not enough coffee means the beans you do have get too much exposure to hot water, which makes bitter coffee.
